Context: COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom; Crime in Greater Manchester.

**Archived source account.** A man is killed, a woman raped and three others stabbed at two "quarantine raves" late Saturday that attracted 6,000 people in Greater Manchester. They were a clear breach of coronavirus legislation.

Source citations (as archived): [BBC News](<https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-england-manchester-53040827>).

<a id="event-2020-06-13-3-4"></a>

**Archived source account.** A court in China sentences an Australian man to death for drug trafficking. The man had been arrested in 2013 at Baiyun Airport in Guangzhou. The Australian government condemns the verdict.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-australia-china-drugtrafficking-sente/china-sentences-australian-to-death-in-fresh-blow-to-relations-idUSKBN23K099?il=0>).

<a id="event-2020-06-13-3-5"></a>

**Archived source account.** Colombian businessman Alex Saab is arrested in Cape Verde a week after Colombian authorities froze his assets following the opening an investigation against him for alleged money laundering. The Nicolás Maduro-led Government of Venezuela denounces the arrest as an arbitrary detention and violation of international law.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-venezuela-corruption/colombian-businessman-close-to-venezuelas-maduro-arrested-idUSKBN23K0OT?il=0>).

#### Politics and elections

<a id="event-2020-06-13-4-3"></a>

Context: George Floyd protests / George Floyd protests in the United States / George Floyd protests in California.

**Archived source account.** Protesters gather outside the One America News Network headquarters in San Diego, California, US for their misinformation about the Buffalo police shoving incident, including labeling protester Martin Gugino as a “Antifa provocateur”.

Source citations (as archived): [Times of San Diego](<https://timesofsandiego.com/politics/2020/06/13/protesters-label-one-america-news-network-as-lies-at-san-diego-hq/>).

<a id="event-2020-06-13-4-5"></a>

Context: George Floyd protests / George Floyd protests in the United Kingdom.

**Archived source account.** Protests organized by Black Lives Matter are cancelled in London before the arrival of counter-protesters, including members of the far-right, although some BLM supporters arrived. Far-right protesters and police clashed at a demonstration in Trafalgar Square.

Source citations (as archived): [BBC News](<https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-53031072>); [Reuters](<https://uk.reuters.com/article/minneapolis-police-protests-britain-lond/far-right-protesters-and-police-scuffle-in-londons-trafalgar-square-idUKKBN23K0HL>); [The Times](<https://www.thetimes.co.uk/article/far-right-gangs-to-target-black-lives-matter-protesters-f2kvwp9kn>).

<a id="event-2020-06-13-4-6"></a>

Context: George Floyd protests.

**Archived source account.** French riot police clash with anti-racism protesters in central Paris, as thousands march onto the Place de la République to protest police brutality against the country's immigrants.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-minneapolis-police-protests-france/anti-racism-protesters-clash-with-police-in-paris-idUSKBN23K0J3?il=0>).

<a id="event-2020-06-13-4-8"></a>

Context: 2020 Polish presidential election, LGBT rights in Poland.

**Archived source account.** President Andrzej Duda compares the "LGBT ideology" to "communist indoctrination" ahead of the upcoming presidential elections. Opposition candidate Robert Biedroń condemns his remarks.

#### Armed conflicts and attacks

Context: Afghan peace process; Taliban insurgency; June 2020 Afghanistan attacks.

**Archived source account.** The Interior Ministry accuses the Taliban of killing or wounding more than 400 Afghan security forces personnel in the last week and said the insurgent group had increased attacks ahead of expected peace talks. He also accused them of attacking religious scholars to put "psychological pressure" on the government.

Source citations (as archived): [AFP](<https://english.alarabiya.net/en/News/world/2020/06/14/Taliban-killed-wounded-over-400-Afghan-security-personnel-in-one-week-Govt.html>).

#### Armed conflicts and attacks

Context: Saudi Arabian-led intervention in Yemen.

<a id="event-2020-06-15-0-3"></a>

Context: Mali War.

**Archived source account.** The armed forces say an ambush on a military convoy in central Mali has killed at least 24 troops and left others missing. No group has claimed responsibility for the attack.

Source citations (as archived): [BBC News](<https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-africa-53058690>); [Al Jazeera](<https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/06/dozens-troops-dead-missing-northwest-mali-attack-200615142301025.html>).

<a id="event-2020-06-15-1-1"></a>

Context: China–United States trade war.

**Archived source account.** The U.S. Department of Commerce announces it will relax the blacklist against Huawei to allow American companies to work with the Chinese telecom on setting 5G network standards.

<a id="event-2020-06-15-2-1"></a>

**Archived source account.** At least three houses are damaged after an Indonesian Air Force Hawk 209 crashes into a residential area of Kampar, Riau. There are no fatalities in the incident.

#### Health and environment

<a id="event-2020-06-15-3-3"></a>

Context: COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in North America / COVID-19 pandemic in the United States.

Source citations (as archived): [The Hill](<https://thehill.com/homenews/house/502768-house-gop-lawmaker-tests-positive-for-covid-19?amp>).

Context: COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in Asia, COVID-19 pandemic in Africa.

#### Law and crime

<a id="event-2020-06-15-4-1"></a>

Context: Killing of Rayshard Brooks.

**Archived source account.** The Fulton County medical examiner declares Rayshard Brooks' death a homicide. Brooks was shot in the back by an Atlanta Police officer while fleeing from an attempted arrest for driving under the influence in which he stole an officer's taser and fired it at him on June 12.

Source citations (as archived): [BBC News](<https://www.bbc.com/news/world-us-canada-53047282>).

<a id="event-2020-06-15-4-3"></a>

Context: LGBTQ rights in the United States.

**Archived source account.** The Supreme Court of the United States delivers its decision in the case of Bostock v. Clayton County, Georgia, ruling that the Civil Rights Act of 1964 prohibits employment discrimination against individuals on the basis of their sexual orientation and gender identity.

Source citations (as archived): [BBC News](<https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-us-canada-53055632>).

<a id="event-2020-06-15-4-4"></a>

**Archived source account.** Hundreds of French police are brought in as reinforcements to the city of Dijon, as over 150 Chechens from around France have gathered to avenge the alleged assault of a Chechen teenager by local drug dealers. During the violence, several people are reported injured and one person suffered gunshot wounds.

Source citations (as archived): [BBC News](<https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-europe-53058981>); [The Jerusalem Post](<https://www.jpost.com/international/france-sends-police-to-dijon-after-chechens-face-gangland-war-in-city-631606>).

<a id="event-2020-06-15-4-5"></a>

**Archived source account.** Maria Ressa, CEO of Philippine news site Rappler, is found guilty of libel by a Manila court over a 2012 story linking a businessman to various crimes. She faces up to six years in prison.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-philippines-media/philippine-court-finds-news-site-chief-maria-ressa-guilty-of-libel-idUSKBN23M03B?il=0>).

<a id="event-2020-06-15-4-6"></a>

**Archived source account.** Sudan's public prosecutor announces the discovery of a mass grave containing the remains of students who were killed in 1998 when they tried to evade conscription. The prosecutor accused former ruler Omar al-Bashir.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-sudan-politics/sudan-announces-discovery-of-mass-grave-of-students-killed-under-bashir-idUSKBN23M1OM?il=0>).

<a id="event-2020-06-15-4-7"></a>

**Archived source account.** A court in Russia sentences former U.S. Marine Paul Whelan to 16 years in prison for espionage. The U.S ambassador to Russia John Sullivan condemns the sentencing as "a mockery of justice" in a statement to media after the verdict.

Source citations (as archived): [CNN](<https://edition.cnn.com/2020/06/15/world/paul-whelan-sentenced-russia-intl/index.html>).

<a id="event-2020-06-15-4-8"></a>

**Archived source account.** Black Lives Matter activist Oluwatoyin Salau is found dead in Tallahassee, Florida, US, after going missing on June 6. Shortly before her disappearance, Salau tweeted that she had been sexually assaulted by a black man. Her death is currently being treated as a homicide.

Source citations (as archived): [CNN](<https://edition.cnn.com/2020/06/15/us/toyin-salau-black-lives-matter-found-dead-trnd/index.html>).

<a id="event-2020-06-15-4-9"></a>

**Archived source account.** The Nepali Department of Immigration says that it will deport five foreign tourists (three Chinese, an American and an Australian) and ban them from entering Nepal for two years after they joined protests against the government's response to the coronavirus outbreak.

Source citations (as archived): [CNA](<https://www.channelnewsasia.com/news/asia/nepal-to-deport-foreign-tourists-for-joining-coronavirus-protest-12837948>).

#### Armed conflicts and attacks

<a id="event-2020-06-16-0-2"></a>

Context: Sino-Indian border dispute / 2020 China–India skirmishes.

**Archived source account.** At least 20 Indian soldiers and an unknown number of Chinese soldiers have been killed in a clash in Ladakh in the disputed Kashmir region, amid rising tensions between the two countries. Local media reported that the Indian soldiers were "beaten to death", and the Indian Army says no shots were fired.

Source citations (as archived): [BBC News](<https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-53061476>).

<a id="event-2020-06-16-0-4"></a>

Context: Mali War.

**Archived source account.** President Ibrahim Boubacar Keïta says that opposition leader Soumaïla Cissé, who was kidnapped in late March, is alive. Keïta said "we know who his captors are \[...\] And if it pleases God, he will come back soon".

Source citations (as archived): [Al Jazeera](<https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/06/mali-keita-abducted-opposition-leader-soumaila-cisse-alive-200616191957695.html>).

<a id="event-2020-06-16-0-6"></a>

Context: 2020 boogaloo killings.

**Archived source account.** The alleged gunman in a fatal attack on Santa Cruz County deputies is also charged with last month's murder of a Federal Protective Service officer in Oakland, California. A second man is also charged as an accomplice. Both men had ties to the far-right boogaloo movement.

Source citations (as archived): [NBC News](<https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/justice-department/airman-charged-killing-federal-officer-during-george-floyd-protests-california-n1231187>).

#### Business and economy

<a id="event-2020-06-16-1-0"></a>

**Archived source account.** The World Trade Organization rules that the Saudi government violated Qatar’s intellectual property rights by promoting the pirate TV station beoutQ, which aired Qatari programs like beIN Sports after Saudi Arabia and several other Middle Eastern countries cut ties with the Kingdom during the Qatar diplomatic crisis. The Qatari Communications Minister applauds the decision, while Saudi Arabia denies any involvement.

<a id="event-2020-06-16-2-2"></a>

Context: COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in mainland China.

**Archived source account.** Beijing closes all schools, locks down several residential estates and imposes a partial travel ban, urging residents not to leave the city, after 27 more COVID-19 cases are confirmed in the city, bringing the total to 106 new cases in the last five days. The new outbreak is linked to the Xinfadi Market.

Source citations (as archived): [The Nations](<http://www.thenations.co.uk/news/beijing-imposes-partial-travel-ban-closes-schools-over-new-coronavirus-outbreak/>).

<a id="event-2020-06-16-2-4"></a>

Context: COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in Brazil.

**Archived source account.** Brazil's Ministry of Health reports a record 34,918 new confirmed cases of COVID-19 and 1,282 more deaths in the last 24 hours. Despite the record daily rise, Chief of Staff of the Presidency Walter Souza Braga Netto says the virus is now under control.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronvirus-brazil/brazil-sees-record-daily-coronavirus-cases-official-says-outbreak-under-control-idUSKBN23N3EE>).

Context: COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in Honduras.

#### International relations

<a id="event-2020-06-16-3-1"></a>

Context: North Korea–South Korea relations.

**Archived source account.** The General Staff Department of the Korean People's Army says they are on "high alert" and are looking at plans to mobilize the army into the demilitarized zone, in response to defector groups in South Korea sending propaganda material across the border.

Source citations (as archived): [BBC News](<https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-53059437>).

<a id="event-2020-06-16-3-2"></a>

Context: North Korea–South Korea relations.

**Archived source account.** North Korea blows up the four-storey Inter-Korean Liaison Office in the Kaesong Industrial Region, according to South Korean authorities. Kim Yo-jong, the sister of Supreme Leader Kim Jong-un, had earlier threatened to destroy the "useless" building. A neighbouring apartment complex used by South Korean officials appears to have partially collapsed in the explosion.

Source citations (as archived): [Yonhap](<https://en.yna.co.kr/view/AEN20200616008300325>); [Al Jazeera](<https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/06/south-korea-north-blew-liaison-office-tensions-rise-200616071045580.html>).

<a id="event-2020-06-16-3-4"></a>

Context: Chinese intelligence activity abroad, Sino-Russian relations since 1991.

**Archived source account.** Russian investigators accuse Valery Mitko, President of Arctic Academy of Sciences in St. Petersburg and one of the country's leading Arctic researchers, "of treason" after alleging that he gave a document containing state secrets to Chinese intelligence in early 2018 at China's Dalian Maritime University, where he was a visiting professor. Mitko and his lawyer Ivan Pavlov deny any wrongdoing and say that all the materials were openly available.

Source citations (as archived): [CNN](<https://www.cnn.com/2020/06/17/europe/russia-china-spying-allegation-intl/index.html>).

#### Law and crime

<a id="event-2020-06-16-4-1"></a>

Context: Police reform in the United States.

**Archived source account.** In the aftermath of the killing of George Floyd last month, U.S. President Donald Trump signs an executive order limiting the use of police chokeholds, except in cases where “deadly force is allowed by law”.

Source citations (as archived): [CNBC](<https://www.cnbc.com/2020/06/16/trump-signs-executive-order-urging-police-reform-says-cops-need-more-funding.html>).

<a id="event-2020-06-16-4-2"></a>

**Archived source account.** Moldova asks the U.S. to extradite businessman Vladimir Plahotniuc after accusing him of "involvement in the theft of $1 billion from banks in 2014–2015".

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-moldova-tycoon-usa/moldova-asks-u-s-to-extradite-tycoon-plahotniuc-over-1-billion-theft-idUSKBN23N2XT?il=0>).

<a id="event-2020-06-16-4-3"></a>

**Archived source account.** Pacific Gas and Electric Company CEO Bill Johnson pleads guilty on behalf of his company to 84 counts of felony involuntary manslaughter in the 2018 Camp Fire, the deadliest wildfire in California's history, as well as one felony count of unlawfully starting a fire. PG&amp;E will pay a maximum fine of US$3.5 million, as well as an additional US$500,000 for the cost of investigations.

Source citations (as archived): [Al Jazeera](<https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/06/pge-pleads-guilty-84-deaths-2018-california-wildfire-200616183543588.html>); [The Sacramento Bee](<https://www.sacbee.com/news/california/fires/article243571597.html>).

<a id="event-2020-06-16-4-4"></a>

**Archived source account.** The Indonesian National Police says that they have arrested Russ Medlin, an American fugitive wanted at home in connection with a $700 million cryptocurrency scam, on local teenage sex charges.

Source citations (as archived): [The Jakarta Post](<https://www.thejakartapost.com/news/2020/06/16/indonesia-arrests-us-fraud-fugitive-on-local-sex-charges.html>).

Context: 2020 Tanzanian general election.

**Archived source account.** President John Magufuli dissolves parliament ahead of the election. In the decision, he highlights his government's achievements, citing "expanding infrastructure such as roads, electricity generation and reforming the mining sector".

<a id="event-2020-06-17-3-2"></a>

Context: COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in the United States.

<a id="event-2020-06-17-4-1"></a>

Context: North Korea–South Korea relations.

**Archived source account.** North Korea rejects South Korea's offer to send special envoys to defuse the current tensions on the peninsula, after having destroyed the Inter-Korean Liaison Office, and says the Korean People's Army will re-enter the demilitarized Kaesong and Mount Kumgang areas.

**Archived source account.** Japan says it will keep a close watch over the disputed Senkaku Islands after Chinese ships are seen near the islands for 65 days in a row. Chief Cabinet Secretary Yoshihide Suga says that Japan has protested to China over the issue and that it would respond "calmly and firmly".

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-japan-china-suga/japan-to-keep-close-watch-over-disputed-islands-suga-idUSKBN23O144>).

Context: Syria–United States relations.

**Archived source account.** U.S. Secretary of State Mike Pompeo announces "toughest sanctions" on Syrian president Bashar al-Assad and his wife Asma in an effort to end the decade-long civil war in the country.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-syria-security-usa-sanctions/u-s-hits-syria-with-toughest-sanctions-yet-to-push-assad-to-end-war-idUSKBN23O20P?il=0>).

<a id="event-2020-06-17-4-7"></a>

Context: 2020 United Nations Security Council election.

**Archived source account.** Norway and Ireland win seats in the United Nations Security Council, joining new members India and Mexico. Canada, which was considered a favorite, and had strongly campaigned for a seat for four years on the council, fails to get enough votes. Canadian Foreign Minister François-Philippe Champagne says he is proud of the campaign but declines to comment on the reasons for their loss.

<a id="event-2020-06-17-5-1"></a>

Context: Papua conflict, 2019 Papua protests.

**Archived source account.** A court in Indonesia sentences Chairman of the National Committee for West Papua Buchtar Tabuni and six others to 11 months in prison for treason. The seven men were charged after they joined anti-racism protests that swept across two provinces in Western New Guinea last August.

Source citations (as archived): [Al Jazeera](<https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/06/indonesian-court-announce-verdict-west-papua-treason-trial-200616234247673.html>).

Context: Killing of Rayshard Brooks.

Brooks was shot twice in the back after he fled from an attempted DUI arrest and stole another officer's taser. This officer, Devin Brosnan, has been charged with aggravated assault and two other crimes in the case.

Source citations (as archived): [NPR](<https://www.npr.org/sections/live-updates-protests-for-racial-justice/2020/06/17/879509659/former-atlanta-police-officer-who-shot-rayshard-brooks-charged-with-felony-murde>).

<a id="event-2020-06-17-6-0"></a>

<a id="event-2020-06-17-6-1"></a>

**Archived source account.** Vanuatu's opposition leader Ralph Regenvanu says he is taking the decision to suspend his party from parliament to the Supreme Court, saying the decision was an "outrage".

Source citations (as archived): [RNZ](<https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/419236/vanuatu-opposition-taking-suspension-to-court>).

<a id="event-2020-06-17-6-2"></a>

**Archived source account.** Cook Islands Prime Minister Henry Puna says he is stepping down in September after nearly a decade in power. His deputy and Finance Minister Mark Brown will take over.

Source citations (as archived): [RNZ](<https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/419204/the-cook-islands-pm-to-stand-down-in-september>).

#### Science and technology

<a id="event-2020-06-17-7-0"></a>

**Archived source account.** The Indian Department of Telecommunications bars the state-run telecommunication company Bharat Sanchar Nigam Limited from upgrading its 4G network with Chinese equipment, as tensions between India and China mount over the recent border skirmishes.

Source citations (as archived): [NDTV](<https://www.ndtv.com/india-news/government-to-ask-state-run-operator-bsnl-to-not-use-chinese-equipment-to-upgrade-4g-facilities-after-ladakh-clash-sources-2247969>).

### 2020-06-18

[Pinned Wikipedia revision 1100567279](<https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Portal%3ACurrent%20events%2F2020%20June%2018&oldid=1100567279>).

#### Health and environment

<a id="event-2020-06-18-0-1"></a>

Context: COVID-19 pandemic in Canada.

**Archived source account.** The total number of COVID-19 cases in Canada surpasses 100,000, with 8,266 deaths recorded.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-canada/canada-hits-100000-coronavirus-cases-major-challenges-remain-idUSKBN23P3AX>).

#### International relations

<a id="event-2020-06-18-1-1"></a>

Context: India–Nepal relations.

**Archived source account.** The upper house of Nepal's parliament approves a new map for the country which includes territories controlled by India. The map requires the approval of President Bidhya Devi Bhandari. India opposes the move, saying that the decision to include Limpiyadhura, Lipulekh and Kalapani is not based on evidence or historical facts.

Source citations (as archived): [Al Jazeera](<https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/06/nepal-parliament-approves-map-includes-land-india-claims-200618074902407.html>).

<a id="event-2020-06-18-1-3"></a>

Context: 2020 United Nations Security Council election.

**Archived source account.** After a second round of voting, Kenya defeats Djibouti in becoming a non-permanent member on the United Nations Security Council starting in 2021. They will join four other newly-elected members, India, Ireland, Norway and Mexico.

Source citations (as archived): [Al Jazeera](<https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/06/kenya-defeats-djibouti-win-seat-security-council-200618194420819.html>).

#### Law and crime

<a id="event-2020-06-18-2-1"></a>

Context: Department of Homeland Security v. Regents of the University of California, Immigration to the United States.

**Archived source account.** The U.S. Supreme Court rules in a 5–4 decision that the rescission of the Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals (DACA) policy was "arbitrary and capricious" under the Administrative Procedure Act (APA) and reversed the order rescinding it. Chief Justice John Roberts casts the deciding vote, along with the four liberal Justices.

Source citations (as archived): [NPR](<https://www.npr.org/2020/06/18/829858289/supreme-court-upholds-daca-in-blow-to-trump-administration>).

#### Politics and elections

<a id="event-2020-06-18-3-1"></a>

Context: Aftermath of the 2020 Burundian general election.

**Archived source account.** Évariste Ndayishimiye takes office as the President of Burundi, following the sudden death of his predecessor Pierre Nkurunziza, his inauguration was advanced to June 18.

Source citations (as archived): [Al Jazeera](<https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/06/ndayishimiye-sworn-burundi-president-200618103042383.html>).

<a id="event-2020-06-18-3-2"></a>

**Archived source account.** Brazil's Education Minister Abraham Weintraub announces his resignation. He did not give a reason; it is believed to be due to derogatory remarks he made about the Supreme Federal Court.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-brazil-politics-weintraub/brazil-education-minister-quits-after-antagonizing-supreme-court-idUSKBN23P3FM?il=0>).

#### Science and technology

<a id="event-2020-06-18-4-1"></a>

Context: Censorship in the United States, Donald Trump on social media.

**Archived source account.** Facebook removes a post condemning antifa by U.S. President Donald Trump's re-election campaign, stating the post's symbol for the group was similar to the one used by the Nazis to identify political prisoners.

Source citations (as archived): [BBC News](<https://www.bbc.com/news/world-us-canada-53098439>).

<a id="event-2020-06-18-4-2"></a>

**Archived source account.** Australian Prime Minister Scott Morrison says "all levels of government", as well as essential service providers and businesses, are being targeted by a sophisticated state-backed cyberattack. Morrison did not say which state is behind the attack.

Source citations (as archived): [BBC News](<https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-australia-46096768>).

#### Sports

<a id="event-2020-06-18-5-1"></a>

Context: COVID-19 pandemic in the State of Palestine.

**Archived source account.** Local sporting events, such as equestrianism, resume in the Gaza Strip today. As of tomorrow, football competitions will be played without spectators.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-palestinians-sport/gaza-horse-riders-compete-again-as-coronavirus-curbs-eased-idUSKBN23P366?il=0>).

<a id="event-2020-06-18-5-2"></a>

**Archived source account.** In Germany Matthias Grosse is appointed as president of the national German speed skating association, DESG. This is seen by national and international media as very remarkable as controversial person and parter of drug banned speed skater Claudia Pechstein.

Source citations (as archived): [Der Spiegel](<https://www.spiegel.de/sport/wintersport/eisschnelllauf-matthias-grosse-ist-neuer-praesident-der-general-a-45048474-ac26-4d6b-a5df-047853e87a31>); [De Volkskrant](<https://www.volkskrant.nl/sport/in-de-duitse-schaatswereld-wordt-een-trumpiaanse-putsch-van-claudia-pechstein-gevreesd~b9990699/>); [Deutschlandfunk](<https://www.deutschlandfunk.de/neuer-eischnelllauf-praesident-matthias-grosse-eine.890.de.html?dram:article_id=478996>).

### 2020-06-19

[Pinned Wikipedia revision 1354549707](<https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Portal%3ACurrent%20events%2F2020%20June%2019&oldid=1354549707>).

#### Armed conflicts and attacks

<a id="event-2020-06-19-0-1"></a>

Context: Operations Claw-Eagle and Claw-Tiger.

**Archived source account.** Five Kurdish civilians near Dohuk in the Kurdistan Region of Iraq are killed by Turkish airstrikes.

Source citations (as archived): [AFP](<https://news.yahoo.com/turkey-air-raids-kill-5-civilians-north-iraq-164642137.html>).

#### Health and environment

<a id="event-2020-06-19-1-2"></a>

Context: COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in Brazil.

**Archived source account.** Brazil's Ministry of Health reports 54,771 new cases and that there are now 1,032,913 confirmed cases of COVID-19 in the country, becoming the second country in the world, after the United States, to surpass one million cases.

Source citations (as archived): [BBC News](<https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-latin-america-53092196>); [Bloomberg](<https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2020-06-19/brazil-blows-past-1-million-infections-with-no-peak-in-sight>).

#### International relations

<a id="event-2020-06-19-2-1"></a>

Context: Nuclear program of Iran.

**Archived source account.** The International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) passes a resolution, the first since 2012, calling on Iran to open two of its nuclear sites to international inspectors. Iran strongly opposes the IAEA resolution, which it says was "based on false allegations" from Israel.

Source citations (as archived): [Middle East Eye](<https://www.middleeasteye.net/news/un-nuclear-watchdog-calls-iran-open-suspected-sites-investigation>).

<a id="event-2020-06-19-2-2"></a>

**Archived source account.** The Caribbean Community (CARICOM) says "sorry is not enough" from British financial institutions that benefited from the Atlantic slave trade, and demands reparations from the United Kingdom. This comes after the Bank of England apologized for the "inexcusable connections" of some of its past governors and directors to slavery.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://uk.reuters.com/article/uk-minneapolis-police-protests-britain-c/exclusive-sorry-is-not-enough-caribbean-states-say-of-british-slavery-apologies-idUKKBN23Q10V>).

#### Law and crime

<a id="event-2020-06-19-3-1"></a>

Context: COVID-19 pandemic in Zimbabwe.

**Archived source account.** Health Minister Obadiah Moyo is arrested and accused of corruption in government procurement of around $60 million worth of medical equipment.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-zimbabwe-crime/zimbabwe-health-minister-arrested-over-60-million-covid-19-equipment-contract-media-reports-idUSKBN23Q33D?il=0>).

<a id="event-2020-06-19-3-3"></a>

Context: Killing of Breonna Taylor.

**Archived source account.** Louisville Mayor Greg Fischer announces the immediate termination of LMPD Officer Brett Hankison over violating departmental policy on the use of force against Breonna Taylor. Hankison is one of three officers involved in the shooting, and prior to the incident had previously been investigated and disciplined for alleged misconduct.

Source citations (as archived): [The Courier-Journal](<https://www.courier-journal.com/story/news/politics/metro-government/2020/06/19/breonna-taylor-protests-brett-hankison-fired-lmpd/3222004001/>).

<a id="event-2020-06-19-3-5"></a>

Context: Abortion in Tennessee, Heartbeat bill.

**Archived source account.** Lawmakers in the U.S. state of Tennessee pass the country's toughest anti-abortion laws, banning the procedure from the moment of fetal heartbeat at around six weeks of pregnancy. Governor Bill Lee hails the law while several organizations say they plan to go to the courts over the issue.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-usa-abortion-tennessee/tennessee-lawmakers-pass-heartbeat-abortion-bill-banning-procedure-after-six-weeks-idUSKBN23Q2Z9?il=0>).

<a id="event-2020-06-19-3-7"></a>

Context: Shooting of Matthew Hunt.

**Archived source account.** A police officer is killed and another seriously injured in a shooting in Massey, New Zealand. This is the first time a law enforcement officer in New Zealand has been killed in the line of duty since 2009. The shooter fled, injuring a civilian in the process, but he has since been arrested.

Source citations (as archived): [BBC News](<https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-53102988>).

Context: 2020 Belarusian presidential election.

Source citations (as archived): [Moscow Times](<https://www.themoscowtimes.com/2020/06/19/belarus-leaders-election-rival-detained-as-crackdown-intensifies-a70619>).

<a id="event-2020-06-19-4-3"></a>

Context: 2020 Hong Kong legislative election.

**Archived source account.** Activist Joshua Wong announces he is running for the legislature, setting up a new legal battle with authorities after he was barred from running in the previous election.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-hongkong-protests-joshua-wong/activist-joshua-wong-says-he-plans-to-run-for-hong-kong-legislature-idUSKBN23Q1RK>).

<a id="event-2020-06-19-4-4"></a>

**Archived source account.** Tens of thousands of protesters descend on the Malian capital of Bamako, demanding President Ibrahim Boubacar Keïta resign over his failure to solve the country's myriad of problems.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-mali-politics-protests/thousands-of-protesters-demand-mali-president-step-down-idUSKBN23Q334?il=0>).

<a id="event-2020-06-19-5-0"></a>

The egg, which is also the very first fossil egg from Antarctica and the largest soft-shelled egg ever discovered, may challenge the notion that mosasaurs and plesiosaurs were fully viviparous according to scientists.

### 2020-06-20

#### Armed conflicts and attacks

Context: 2020 Forbury Gardens stabbings.

**Archived source account.** Three people are killed and three others injured in a mass stabbing at Forbury Gardens in Reading, Berkshire, United Kingdom. A suspect was arrested by Thames Valley Police.

Source citations (as archived): [The Daily Telegraph](<https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/2020/06/20/reading-stabbing-three-dead-two-hospital-attack-forbury-gardens/>).

**Archived source account.** A statue of former Soviet Union leader Vladimir Lenin is officially unveiled in the German city of Gelsenkirchen, North Rhine-Westphalia. It is first ever statue of a Soviet figure in the former West Germany. Despite strong opposition from local officials, the state court in Münster has blocked attempts to remove it.

Source citations (as archived): [Euronews](<https://www.euronews.com/2020/06/20/statue-of-lenin-calmly-erected-in-west-germany>).

#### Health and environment

<a id="event-2020-06-20-2-3"></a>

Context: COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in the United States / COVID-19 pandemic in Arizona.

**Archived source account.** The City of Phoenix and Maricopa County officials pass a mandate requiring all residents to wear masks in "places of public accommodation". The mandate makes exemptions for children under two years old and people with certain health conditions.

Source citations (as archived): [AZCentral](<https://www.azcentral.com/story/news/local/phoenix/2020/06/19/maricopa-county-requires-masks-countywide-curb-spread-covid-19/3227812001/>).

<a id="event-2020-06-20-2-5"></a>

Context: COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in Australia.

**Archived source account.** Following a new spike in coronavirus infections, Victoria delays its easing of restrictions and imposes new limits on the size of gatherings.

<a id="event-2020-06-20-2-7"></a>

Context: COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in India.

**Archived source account.** India reports its highest toll of cases to date, recording 14,516 cases, reaching a total of 395,047 and 12,948 deaths. The government in the capital New Delhi orders hospitals to cancel any leave and have workers return to duty immediately.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-india/india-reports-record-rise-in-coronavirus-cases-delhi-cancels-all-medical-staff-leave-idUSKBN23R0JP?il=0>).

#### International relations

<a id="event-2020-06-20-3-1"></a>

Context: North Korea–South Korea relations.

**Archived source account.** The North Korean state news agency KCNA reports that "enraged" North Koreans are preparing to launch propaganda leaflets across the Military Demarcation Line, in response to propaganda leaflets sent by North Korean defectors.

<a id="event-2020-06-20-4-0"></a>

**Archived source account.** U.S. President Donald Trump fires the United States Attorney for the Southern District of New York Geoffrey Berman, whose office had been investigating the president's personal lawyer, Rudy Giuliani.

Source citations (as archived): [Al Jazeera](<https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/06/drc-president-top-aide-20-year-jail-term-corruption-200620142844387.html>).

<a id="event-2020-06-20-5-1"></a>

Context: 2020 Belarusian presidential election.

**Archived source account.** Internet access is interrupted and hundreds are detained after mass protests break out in Belarus over the arrest of opposition candidate Viktar Babaryka, including reporters from Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty.

Context: Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on sports / COVID-19 pandemic in Australia, 2020 AFL season.

### 2020-06-21

[Pinned Wikipedia revision 1100566846](<https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Portal%3ACurrent%20events%2F2020%20June%2021&oldid=1100566846>).

#### Armed conflicts and attacks

<a id="event-2020-06-21-0-1"></a>

Context: 2020 Forbury Gardens stabbings.

**Archived source account.** The fatal mass stabbing yesterday at Forbury Gardens in Reading, United Kingdom, is declared by the police to have been a terrorist attack.

Source citations (as archived): [BBC News](<https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-england-berkshire-53127095>).

<a id="event-2020-06-21-0-3"></a>

Context: Yemeni Civil War.

**Archived source account.** Forces of the Southern Transitional Council (STC) seize control of the island of Socotra. President Abdrabbuh Mansur Hadi condemns it as a "full-fledged" coup, while the governor of the island condemns the United Arab Emirates and Saudi Arabia for "turning a blind eye".

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-yemen-security-separatists/yemen-separatists-seize-remote-socotra-island-from-saudi-backed-government-idUSKBN23S0DU?il=0>).

<a id="event-2020-06-21-0-5"></a>

Context: Afghan peace process.

**Archived source account.** The Afghan government accuses the Taliban of kidnapping about 60 civilians in the last week in the province of Daykundi. The Taliban deny the accusation and blames the government for civilian casualties during the past week. At least 26 women and children have been freed and elder tribal leaders are mediating for the release of the rest of abductees.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-afghanistan-taliban/afghan-taliban-kidnap-dozens-of-civilians-amid-peace-efforts-officials-say-idUSKBN23S0GZ?il=0>).

<a id="event-2020-06-21-0-7"></a>

Context: Somali Civil War.

**Archived source account.** Two bombs explode in front of a military official's house in Wanlaweyn, killing four people. In another attack, in Galmudug, three men drove a car packed with bombs against a checkpoint after ignoring orders to stop, killing three soldiers.

Source citations (as archived): [Al Jazeera](<https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/06/somalia-killed-bomb-attacks-200621112115099.html>).

<a id="event-2020-06-21-0-9"></a>

Context: Second Libyan Civil War, Egypt–Libya relations.

**Archived source account.** The Government of National Accord's Presidential Council says Egyptian president Abdel Fattah el-Sisi's threats to take military action in Libya constitutes "a declaration of war" on the country.

Source citations (as archived): [The Libya Observer](<https://www.libyaobserver.ly/news/presidential-council-says-sisis-threats-are-declaration-war-libya>).

#### Health and environment

<a id="event-2020-06-21-1-2"></a>

Context: COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in Spain.

**Archived source account.** The state of emergency in Spain officially finishes after more than 100 days.

Source citations (as archived): [The Guardian](<https://www.theguardian.com/world/2020/jun/20/spain-pm-urges-people-not-lower-guard-as-state-of-emergency-ends>).

<a id="event-2020-06-21-1-4"></a>

Context: COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in Brazil.

**Archived source account.** Brazil's Ministry of Health reports 641 more deaths from COVID-19, bringing the death toll in the country to over 50,000.

Source citations (as archived): [BBC News](<https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-latin-america-53132225>).

#### Law and crime

<a id="event-2020-06-21-2-1"></a>

Context: List of mass shootings in the United States in 2020.

**Archived source account.** One person is killed while eleven others are injured during a mass shooting in Minneapolis, Minnesota. The incident involved people shooting at one another.

Source citations (as archived): [The New York Times](<https://www.nytimes.com/2020/06/21/us/minneapolis-shooting.html>).

#### Politics and elections

Context: 2020 Serbian parliamentary election.

### 2020-06-22

[Pinned Wikipedia revision 1082362302](<https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Portal%3ACurrent%20events%2F2020%20June%2022&oldid=1082362302>).

#### Business and economy

<a id="event-2020-06-22-0-1"></a>

Context: Coronavirus recession, Immigration to the United States.

**Archived source account.** U.S. President Donald Trump suspends the entry of some skilled and seasonal workers entering the United States, claiming it will open jobs to citizens. Business groups criticize this move as stifling economic recovery.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-usa-immigration-workers/trump-suspends-entry-of-certain-foreign-workers-despite-business-opposition-idUSKBN23T2ZW>).

#### International relations

<a id="event-2020-06-22-1-1"></a>

Context: India–Nepal relations.

**Archived source account.** Nepalese authorities stop officials of the Water Resources Department of the Bihar government from carrying out infrastructural maintenance work in Indian territory along the India–Nepal border, claiming the area as part of its territory. The incident comes four days after the lower house of the Nepalese parliament approved a new map of the country that included Indian territory in the Indian state of Uttarakhand.

Source citations (as archived): [Times of India](<https://m.timesofindia.com/india/nepal-obstructing-bihar-govt-from-flood-prevention-related-work-bihar-minister-says-will-approach-mea/amp_articleshow/76507256.cms>).

<a id="event-2020-06-22-1-3"></a>

Context: China–United States relations.

**Archived source account.** The U.S. State Department adds four Chinese media organizations, including the public broadcasting service China Central Television, to its list of organizations participating in "foreign missions" due to their connections with the ruling Communist Party. They will be required to report all their employees and any real estate holdings to the American government.

Source citations (as archived): [Al Jazeera](<https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/06/restrict-chinese-media-outlets-deemed-propaganda-200622220638775.html>).

<a id="event-2020-06-22-1-4"></a>

**Archived source account.** China announces its decision to join the United Nations Arms Trade Treaty.

Source citations (as archived): [AFP](<https://www.thejakartapost.com/news/2020/06/22/china-to-join-un-arms-trade-treaty-enhance-world-peace.html>).

<a id="event-2020-06-22-1-5"></a>

**Archived source account.** Thousands of Palestinians and dozens of foreign diplomats attend a rally in Jericho to oppose Israel's plan to unilaterally annex the Jordan Valley and the settlements in the occupied West Bank.

Source citations (as archived): [Al Jazeera](<https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/06/thousands-palestinians-protest-israeli-annexation-plan-200622173919963.html>).

#### Law and crime

<a id="event-2020-06-22-2-0"></a>

**Archived source account.** A police officer of the New York City Police Department is suspended without pay after he is captured on camera using a chokehold against a 35-year-old man in Queens. The use of chokeholds by police was recently banned, both in New York City and the state of New York.

Source citations (as archived): [The Independent](<https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/americas/nypd-ricky-bellevue-chokehold-cop-suspended-police-officer-a9579661.html?utm_term=Autofeed&amp;utm_medium=Social&amp;utm_source=Twitter&amp;amp=1#Echobox=1592845009>).

<a id="event-2020-06-22-2-1"></a>

**Archived source account.** Two suspects are arrested in Oregon in connection to a mass shooting at a residence in Valhermoso Springs, Alabama, on June 4 that killed seven people.

Source citations (as archived): [WBRC](<https://www.wbrc.com/2020/06/22/morgan-county-authorities-fbi-updating-public-septuple-homicide/>).

#### Politics and elections

<a id="event-2020-06-22-3-1"></a>

Context: 2020 Kiribati presidential election.

**Archived source account.** Citizens in Kiribati head to the polls to elect their President. The main issue of the election is whether to maintain relations with China or Taiwan. Incumbent Taneti Maamau, who switched recognition from Taiwan to China last year, is facing candidate Banuera Berina who favors re-establishing relations with Taiwan.

Source citations (as archived): [RNZ](<https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/419528/kiribati-to-hold-presidential-election-today>).

#### Science and technology

<a id="event-2020-06-22-4-1"></a>

Context: Apple's transition to ARM processors.

**Archived source account.** Apple Inc. announces a transition of its personal computer products from using Intel processors to using ARM-based processors designed by Apple. Since 2006, the company has used Intel processors in its computer offerings.

Source citations (as archived): [The Verge](<https://www.theverge.com/2020/6/22/21295475/apple-mac-processors-arm-silicon-chips-wwdc-2020>).

#### Sports

<a id="event-2020-06-22-5-2"></a>

Context: 2020 NASCAR Cup Series / George Floyd protests § Sports industry.

**Archived source account.** NASCAR launches an investigation after a noose was found in the garage area of Bubba Wallace, the lone African-American driver in the series, at Talladega Superspeedway, in Talladega, Alabama, vowing to "eliminate \[those responsible\] from the sport". Wallace had recently successfully pushed NASCAR to enforce a five-year-old ban on the Confederate flag being displayed at its race tracks and properties. A plane pulling a banner with a Confederate flag and the phrase "Defund NASCAR" flew over the race track on June 21.

Source citations (as archived): [CTV News](<https://www.ctvnews.ca/sports/nascar-noose-found-in-bubba-wallace-garage-at-alabama-race-1.4994036>); [BBC News](<https://www.bbc.com/news/world-us-canada-53132933>).

<a id="event-2020-06-22-5-3"></a>

Context: 2020 NASCAR Cup Series / George Floyd protests § Sports industry.

**Archived source account.** The United States Department of Justice and Federal Bureau of Investigation launch their own investigations in order to determine whether criminal charges can be brought.

Source citations (as archived): [USA Today](<https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/nascar/2020/06/22/justice-department-fbi-investigate-noose-bubba-wallaces-garage/3235453001/>).

### 2020-06-23

[Pinned Wikipedia revision 1100567438](<https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Portal%3ACurrent%20events%2F2020%20June%2023&oldid=1100567438>).

#### Armed conflicts and attacks

<a id="event-2020-06-23-0-1"></a>

Context: Saudi Arabian-led intervention in Yemen.

**Archived source account.** The Houthis launch ballistic missiles and drones against Saudi Arabia, including its capital Riyadh. Saudi-led coalition spokesman Turki al-Maliki says that Saudi forces "managed to intercept and destroy" the missiles and drones. The military says that they destroyed "eight booby-trapped unmanned aircraft \[used by the Houthis\] to target civilian objects and civilians in the kingdom".

Source citations (as archived): [Al Jazeera](<https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/06/saudi-coalition-shoots-houthi-ballistic-missiles-drones-200623073541760.html>).

<a id="event-2020-06-23-0-3"></a>

Context: Somali Civil War (2009–present).

**Archived source account.** Two civilians are killed after a suicide bombing occurs at a Turkish military installation in Mogadishu, Turkey's largest overseas military base. Al-Shabaab claims responsibility.

Source citations (as archived): [The New York Times](<https://www.nytimes.com/2020/06/23/world/africa/somalia-turkey-suicide-bombing.html>).

#### Disasters and accidents

<a id="event-2020-06-23-1-1"></a>

Context: 2020 Oaxaca earthquake.

**Archived source account.** A major earthquake strikes southern Mexico, with its epicenter 15 miles (24.1km) northeast of Santa María Xadani, Oaxaca, resulting in the death of five people. It was measured at 7.4 magnitude and a tsunami warning was issued.

Source citations (as archived): [CNN](<https://www.cnn.com/2020/06/23/weather/mexico-earthquake-southern-coast-intl/index.html>).

#### Health and environment

<a id="event-2020-06-23-2-1"></a>

Context: COVID-19 vaccine.

**Archived source account.** Imperial College London administers the first dose of their proposed COVID-19 vaccine, which is undergoing a clinical trial.

Source citations (as archived): [Imperial College London](<https://www.imperial.ac.uk/news/198533/first-volunteer-receives-imperial-covid19-vaccine/>).

#### International relations

<a id="event-2020-06-23-3-1"></a>

Context: North Korea–South Korea relations.

**Archived source account.** Amid increasing tensions and in spite of warnings from the South Korean government, hundreds of thousands of anti-Kim leaflets are floated across the border by a group of North Korean defectors.

Source citations (as archived): [Associated Press](<https://apnews.com/7620633c882411741d16319db0fb4b58>).

#### Law and crime

<a id="event-2020-06-23-4-1"></a>

Context: Killing of Rayshard Brooks.

**Archived source account.** Fulton County authorities charge a woman with arson in relation to an Atlanta Wendy's restaurant being burnt down the day after police killed Rayshard Brooks there after he fled when they tried to arrest him for DUI. The woman's lawyer said she was Brooks' girlfriend.

Source citations (as archived): [The New York Post](<https://nypost.com/2020/06/23/woman-arrested-in-arson-of-wendys-where-rayshard-brooks-was-killed/>); [The New York Post](<https://nypost.com/2020/06/23/accused-wendys-arsonist-natalie-white-was-rayshard-brooks-girlfriend-lawyer/>).

<a id="event-2020-06-23-4-2"></a>

**Archived source account.** A court in Kyrgyzstan sentences former President Almazbek Atambayev to 11 years in prison on corruption charges, which he denies.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-kyrgyzstan-atambayev/kyrgyz-ex-president-sentenced-to-11-years-in-prison-idUSKBN23U1CS>).

<a id="event-2020-06-23-4-3"></a>

**Archived source account.** A court in Turkey sentences a former mayor of a Kurdish city and opposition member to 16 years in prison for "being a member of a terrorist group, abusing power and inciting to violence and hatred". The head of a local human rights organization says "all the charges against her are fabricated".

Source citations (as archived): [Al Arabiya](<https://english.alarabiya.net/en/News/middle-east/2020/06/23/Turkish-court-sentences-former-Kurdish-mayor-to-16-years-for-inciting-violence-.html>).

<a id="event-2020-06-23-4-4"></a>

**Archived source account.** American porn star Ron Jeremy is charged with the rape of three women and sexual assault of another.

Source citations (as archived): [The Guardian](<https://www.theguardian.com/society/2020/jun/23/ron-jeremy-rape-charges-los-angeles>).

#### Politics and elections

<a id="event-2020-06-23-5-1"></a>

Context: 2020 Kiribati presidential election.

**Archived source account.** Incumbent Taneti Maamau is re-elected as President of Kiribati with 26,053 votes to 17,866 votes by Banuera Berina, in a blow for Taiwan and its efforts to regain recognition from the Pacific country.

Source citations (as archived): [RNZ](<https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/419640/taneti-maamau-re-elected-president-of-kiribati-in-blow-for-taiwan>).

<a id="event-2020-06-23-5-3"></a>

Context: 2020 Malawian presidential election.

**Archived source account.** After the results of the last general election in Malawi were annulled by the country's Constitutional Court in February, new elections are held.

Context: 2020 Singaporean general election.

Context: 2020 Kentucky Democratic presidential primary, 2020 United States Senate election in Kentucky.

**Archived source account.** Voters in Kentucky head to the polls to nominate a Democrat to face Senate Majority leader Mitch McConnell. Former Vice President Joe Biden also won the state primary.

Source citations (as archived): [CNN](<https://www.cnn.com/2020/06/23/politics/kentucky-senate-democratic-primary/index.html>); [The Hill](<https://thehill.com/homenews/campaign/503576-biden-wins-kentucky-primary>).

Context: 2020 NASCAR Cup Series / George Floyd protests § Sports industry.

**Archived source account.** NASCAR and the Federal Bureau of Investigation conclude their investigation of the noose found in the garage area of Bubba Wallace, the lone African-American driver in the series, at Talladega Superspeedway. The investigation concluded the "noose" was in fact the garage door pull, and had not been touched or moved since early last fall.

#### Armed conflicts and attacks

Context: Second Libyan Civil War, Central Libya offensive (2020).

**Archived source account.** The speaker of the Libyan House of Representatives, Aguila Saleh Issa, asks Egypt to intervene in Libya if the armed forces of the Government of National Accord attempt to capture the city of Sirte.

#### Business and economy

<a id="event-2020-06-24-1-0"></a>

**Archived source account.** Segway Inc. announces that production of its personal transporter will end on July 15. Production began in 2001.

Source citations (as archived): [BBC News](<https://www.bbc.com/news/business-53160518>).

<a id="event-2020-06-24-1-1"></a>

**Archived source account.** Bayer AG announces it has agreed to pay US$10 billion to resolve thousands of lawsuits regarding claims that the Monsanto herbicide Roundup causes cancer. Court-appointed mediator Kenneth Feinberg says the deal is a "constructive and reasonable" resolution.

Source citations (as archived): [NBC News](<https://www.nbcnews.com/news/us-news/bayer-reaches-10-5-billion-settlement-roundup-cancer-lawsuits-n1232026>).

<a id="event-2020-06-24-1-2"></a>

**Archived source account.** Japanese manufacturing company Olympus announces it is exiting the camera business after 84 years, stating its financial losses caused by their inability to compete with smartphone cameras was a major factor in the decision.

#### International relations

<a id="event-2020-06-24-2-1"></a>

Context: North Korea–South Korea relations.

**Archived source account.** The North Korean state news agency KCNA reports that the country will suspend military action plans against the South after a meeting of the Central Military Commission presided by Kim Jong-un. North Korea had protested against defectors sending leaflets to the border, and Kim's sister Kim Yo-jong had threatened a military response.

Source citations (as archived): [Al Jazeera](<https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/06/korea-kim-suspends-plans-military-action-south-200624004316030.html>).

<a id="event-2020-06-24-2-3"></a>

Context: COVID-19 pandemic in Europe.

**Archived source account.** Ambassadors for EU member states meet today to develop criteria for reopening external borders to travelers on July 1. European Commission guidance is that non-EU countries whose COVID-19 status, e.g., the number of new infections, the trend in new infections, and testing and tracing, are comparable or better than the EU average will make the safe list. Other factors, such as reciprocity and links to the EU, will also be considered. Travelers from countries such as Brazil, Russia, and the United States may be barred based on these rules.

Source citations (as archived): [BBC News](<https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-53161447>); [The New York Times](<https://www.nytimes.com/2020/06/23/world/europe/coronavirus-EU-American-travel-ban.html>).

<a id="event-2020-06-24-2-5"></a>

Context: Iran–United States relations; United States–Venezuela relations.

**Archived source account.** U.S. Secretary of State Mike Pompeo announces sanctions on five Iranian ship captains who delivered fuel to Venezuela and reaffirms support for disputed President Juan Guaidó over Nicolás Maduro.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-venezuela-iran-gasoline/u-s-sanctions-five-iranian-ship-captains-for-bringing-oil-to-venezuela-pompeo-idUSKBN23V25I?il=0>).

Following the announcement, President Thaçi cancels his upcoming trip to the United States.

Source citations (as archived): [Sydney Morning Herald](<https://www.smh.com.au/world/europe/kosovo-s-president-indicted-for-war-crimes-withdraws-from-white-house-talks-20200625-p555wq.html>).
