#### Business and economy

<a id="event-2020-06-26-1-0"></a>

**Archived source account.** British-Dutch consumer company Unilever, owner of brands including Lipton and Dove, announces that they will suspend advertising on social media sites such as Facebook and Twitter for the rest of the year, saying that they have not been doing enough to counter "divisiveness and hate speech during this polarized election period in the U.S."

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-facebook-ads-boycott-unilever/unilever-to-stop-u-s-advertising-on-facebook-twitter-for-rest-of-year-idUSKBN23X2FW?il=0>).

<a id="event-2020-06-26-1-2"></a>

Context: Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic.

**Archived source account.** Intu Properties, the owner and operator of the United Kingdom's largest shopping centres such as the MetroCentre and Lakeside Shopping Centre, collapses into administration, following months of lockdown due to the COVID-19 pandemic.

Source citations (as archived): [BBC News](<https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/business-53195980>).

#### Health and environment

<a id="event-2020-06-26-2-2"></a>

Context: COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in Spain.

**Archived source account.** A University of Barcelona-led investigation uncovers traces of SARS-CoV-2 in frozen Barcelona sewage samples drawn on 12 March 2019, more than half a year before the first publicly confirmed case of COVID-19 in China.

Source citations (as archived): [El Mundo](<https://www.elmundo.es/ciencia-y-salud/ciencia/2020/06/26/5ef5e37321efa00c2c8b45b9.html>); [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/idUSKBN23X2HQ>).

<a id="event-2020-06-26-2-4"></a>

Context: COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in the United States.

**Archived source account.** The U.S. reports 39,972 more COVID-19 cases, the largest number of new cases in a single day.

Source citations (as archived): [USA Today](<https://eu.usatoday.com/story/news/health/2020/06/25/coronavirus-updates-texas-florida-report-rise-covid-19-cases/3258599001/>).

#### Law and crime

<a id="event-2020-06-26-3-1"></a>

Context: Glasgow hotel stabbings.

**Archived source account.** Six people are injured in a mass stabbing in central Glasgow, Scotland. The attacker was shot dead by police.

Source citations (as archived): [BBC News](<https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-scotland-glasgow-west-53195939>).

<a id="event-2020-06-26-3-3"></a>

Context: 2016 Turkish coup d'état attempt.

**Archived source account.** A court in Turkey sentences 121 people to life in prison for their role in the 2016 attempted coup. Eighty-six were sentenced to "aggravated" life imprisonment for "attempting to violate the constitution".

Source citations (as archived): [Al Arabiya](<https://english.alarabiya.net/en/News/middle-east/2020/06/26/In-Turkey-121-sentenced-to-life-in-prison-during-trial-for-2016-coup.html>).

<a id="event-2020-06-26-3-5"></a>

Context: Iran and state-sponsored terrorism.

**Archived source account.** A Danish court sentences a Norwegian-Iranian man to seven years in prison for spying on behalf of Iranian intelligence and for conspiring to assassinate the leader of the Arab Struggle Movement for the Liberation of Ahvaz. He will be expelled permanently from the country upon the end of his sentence.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-denmark-security-iran/norwegian-found-guilty-of-spying-for-iran-in-denmark-idUSKBN23X1EX?il=0>).

<a id="event-2020-06-26-3-6"></a>

**Archived source account.** A court in the United Kingdom sentences an 18-year-old man to 15 years in prison for attempted murder for throwing a six-year-old French boy off the roof of the Tate Modern art gallery in London in December. He was 17 at the time of the crime, and said he "wanted to be on the television news". The boy survived but suffered life-changing injuries.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-britain-crime-tate/teenager-who-threw-french-boy-from-london-art-gallery-roof-jailed-for-15-years-idUSKBN23X1H4?il=0>); [BBC News](<https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-england-53191161>); [CNN](<https://www.cnn.com/2020/06/26/uk/jonty-bravery-sentenced-intl-scli-gbr/index.html>).

<a id="event-2020-06-26-3-7"></a>

**Archived source account.** The Chief of Police of Mexico City, Omar García Harfuch, is injured but "out of danger" in an assassination attempt upon him. Two of his bodyguards and a passerby were killed. García Harfuch blamed the attack on the Jalisco New Generation Cartel (CJNG).

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-mexico-violence/mexico-city-police-chief-shot-and-injured-in-assassination-attempt-idUSKBN23X1T8?il=0>).

#### Politics and elections

<a id="event-2020-06-26-4-1"></a>

Context: George Floyd protests.

**Archived source account.** Employees at Whole Foods Market, an Amazon subsidiary, working in multiple U.S. locations are being sent home for refusing to take off Black Lives Matter face masks. Workers are protesting these actions.

Source citations (as archived): [Boston Globe](<https://www.bostonglobe.com/2020/06/25/business/whole-foods-workers-sent-home-wearing-black-lives-matter-masks/>); [Fox News](<https://www.foxnews.com/us/whole-foods-workers-protest-over-black-lives-matter-mask-policy>).

<a id="event-2020-06-26-4-3"></a>

Context: Statehood movement in the District of Columbia, Proposals for a 51st state in the United States.

**Archived source account.** The United States House of Representatives passes a bill that would make Washington, D.C. a U.S. state, with the exception of important government buildings. This legislation is unlikely to pass in the Republican-held United States Senate and President Donald Trump has expressed opposition to the matter.

Source citations (as archived): [CNBC](<https://www.cnbc.com/2020/06/26/house-passes-bill-to-make-washington-dc-the-51st-state.html>).

### 2020-06-27

[Pinned Wikipedia revision 1354549714](<https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Portal%3ACurrent%20events%2F2020%20June%2027&oldid=1354549714>).

#### Armed conflicts and attacks

<a id="event-2020-06-27-0-1"></a>

Context: June 2020 Afghanistan attacks; War in Afghanistan.

**Archived source account.** Two Afghanistan Independent Human Rights Commission workers are killed when a bomb attached to their vehicle explodes in Kabul. The Taliban denies responsibility and no other group has claimed responsibility. The attack is condemned by the United Nations.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-afghanistan-attacks-rights/two-afghan-human-rights-workers-killed-in-blast-in-kabul-idUSKBN23Y0H9?il=0>).

<a id="event-2020-06-27-0-3"></a>

Context: Insurgency in Cabo Delgado.

**Archived source account.** An ISIL-affiliated group attacks a town near billion-dollar gas projects managed by Total S.A. and Exxon Mobil in Mocímboa da Praia, Mozambique. An army spokesman reports that the armed forces suffered casualties in the attack.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-mozambique-insurgency/insurgents-stage-very-violent-attack-close-to-gas-projects-in-mozambique-idUSKBN23Y0OU?il=0>).

#### Arts and culture

<a id="event-2020-06-27-1-1"></a>

Context: Hinduism in Pakistan.

**Archived source account.** The government of Prime Minister Imran Khan approves a grant of Rs100 million for the construction of the first Hindu temple in the capital of Islamabad.

Source citations (as archived): [DAWN](<https://www.dawn.com/news/1565405/pm-approves-grant-for-construction-of-hindu-temple-in-islamabad>).

#### Health and environment

<a id="event-2020-06-27-2-1"></a>

Context: COVID-19 pandemic in India.

**Archived source account.** India surpasses 500,000 cases after reporting 18,552 new cases in the last 24 hours, the highest toll to date. India also reports a total 15,685 deaths from the disease.

Source citations (as archived): [AP News](<https://apnews.com/114bde59882c280e6e68682e0418af11>).

#### International relations

<a id="event-2020-06-27-3-1"></a>

Context: Libyan Civil War, Wagner Group.

**Archived source account.** Libya's international-recognized government, the Government of National Accord, calls for the United States and the European Union to impose sanctions on individuals and "mercenaries", after its National Oil Corporation stated that Russian mercenaries and other foreign actors had forced their way into the Sharara oilfield.

Source citations (as archived): [Al Jazeera](<https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/06/libya-calls-eu-sanctions-russian-mercenaries-backers-200627112137004.html>).

#### Law and crime

<a id="event-2020-06-27-4-1"></a>

Context: Red Bluff shooting.

**Archived source account.** An employee is killed and four others injured in a mass shooting at a Walmart distribution center in Red Bluff, California, United States. The shooter was then confronted by responding police officers and fatally shot during a shootout.

Source citations (as archived): [AP News](<https://apnews.com/a5ebbf3806e1abaa6cee11af80c415da>).

<a id="event-2020-06-27-4-3"></a>

Context: Breonna Taylor protests.

**Archived source account.** One person is killed and another injured when a gunman opened fire at people protesting the killing of Breonna Taylor in Louisville, Kentucky, United States.

Source citations (as archived): [AP News](<https://apnews.com/b31cb9fa8c18f9ec8d7ac66e13566543>).

#### Politics and elections

<a id="event-2020-06-27-5-1"></a>

Context: Hong Kong 1 July marches.

**Archived source account.** Police in Hong Kong ban the 1 July march for the first time in 17 years. In a letter of objection addressed to protest organizer and convenor of the Civil Human Rights Front (CHRF) Jimmy Sham, police cite "persisting social unrest" and vandalism. Chief Secretary Matthew Cheung rejects an appeal by the CHRF who have said they will appeal the ban.

Source citations (as archived): [Hong Kong Free Press](<https://hongkongfp.com/2020/06/27/breaking-hong-kong-police-ban-annual-pro-democracy-demo-for-first-time-in-17-years/>).

<a id="event-2020-06-27-5-3"></a>

Context: 2020 Icelandic presidential election.

**Archived source account.** Citizens of Iceland cast their vote in the latest presidential elections. Incumbent president Guðni Th. Jóhannesson is expected to be the clear winner of the election.

Source citations (as archived): [DW](<https://www.dw.com/en/icelands-incumbent-president-set-for-landslide-election-win/a-53963966>).

<a id="event-2020-06-27-5-5"></a>

Context: Irish government formation.

**Archived source account.** Following long negotiations, the new Irish government is voted into office by Dáil Éireann. The government is formed after a historic coalition deal between Fianna Fáil, Fine Gael and the Green Party. Fianna Fáil leader Micheál Martin takes office as Taoiseach (Prime Minister), with outgoing Taoiseach Leo Varadkar as Tánaiste (Deputy Prime Minister), due to return to the post in December 2022 as part of the coalition deal.

Source citations (as archived): [RTÉ](<https://www.rte.ie/news/politics/2020/0625/1149711-programme-for-government/>).

<a id="event-2020-06-27-5-7"></a>

Context: 2020 Malawian presidential election.

**Archived source account.** Lazarus Chakwera has been elected President with 58.57% of the votes.

Source citations (as archived): [Nyasa Times](<https://www.nyasatimes.com/chakwera-declared-winner-of-malawi-presidential-election-defeats-incumbent-mutharika/>).

### 2020-06-28

[Pinned Wikipedia revision 1082363566](<https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Portal%3ACurrent%20events%2F2020%20June%2028&oldid=1082363566>).

#### Arts and culture

<a id="event-2020-06-28-0-1"></a>

Context: List of name changes due to the George Floyd protests.

**Archived source account.** Princeton University says it will remove the name of former U.S. President Woodrow Wilson from its public policy school and a residential college, calling him "a racist". Christopher L. Eisgruber says that "Woodrow Wilson's racist thinking and policies make him an inappropriate namesake for a school or college whose scholars, students and alumni must stand firmly against racism in all its forms".

Source citations (as archived): [Al Jazeera](<https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/06/princeton-university-removes-president-wilson-school-200628110207282.html>).

#### Business and economy

<a id="event-2020-06-28-1-0"></a>

**Archived source account.** Following negotiations with creditors, Chesapeake Energy applies for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in the United States. It will seek to restructure its debts in order to continue operations. The company is experiencing cash flow and liquidity issues due to low energy prices and large amounts of debt.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-chesapeake-enrgy-bankruptcy/shale-pioneer-chesapeake-energy-files-for-bankruptcy-idUSKBN23Z0SS?il=0>).

#### Health and environment

<a id="event-2020-06-28-2-1"></a>

Context: COVID-19 pandemic.

**Archived source account.** The worldwide COVID-19 case total surpasses 10 million while the worldwide death total surpasses 500,000. The United States remains the leading nation in cases, accounting for over 25 percent of both cases and deaths worldwide.

Source citations (as archived): [NBC News](<https://www.nbcnews.com/news/world/global-covid-19-cases-reach-10-million-johns-hopkins-data-n1232353>); [Al Jazeera](<https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/06/global-coronavirus-death-toll-nears-500000-live-updates-200627234018796.html>).

#### International relations

<a id="event-2020-06-28-3-1"></a>

Context: Second Libyan Civil War, Libya–Sudan relations.

**Archived source account.** Sudan says it has detained 122 of its nationals, including eight children, who were heading to neighboring Libya to fight as "mercenaries". Sudanese Foreign Minister Asma Mohamed Abdalla says, "We cannot get involved in a conflict in any neighboring country."

Source citations (as archived): [Arab News](<https://www.arabnews.com/node/1696961/middle-east>).

#### Politics and elections

<a id="event-2020-06-28-4-1"></a>

Context: 2020 Icelandic presidential election.

**Archived source account.** Incumbent president Guðni Th. Jóhannesson wins re-election with 92% of the votes.

Source citations (as archived): [Euronews](<https://www.euronews.com/2020/06/27/iceland-s-incumbent-president-expected-to-win-second-term>).

<a id="event-2020-06-28-4-3"></a>

Context: 2020 Polish presidential election.

**Archived source account.** Voters in Poland head to the polls to elect their next president. The election had to be postponed once due to the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic.

Source citations (as archived): [DW](<https://www.dw.com/en/poland-heads-to-polls-to-elect-next-president/a-53968933>).

<a id="event-2020-06-28-4-4"></a>

Context: 2020 Polish presidential election.

**Archived source account.** Incumbent president Andrzej Duda wins the first round of voting. He will face Mayor of Warsaw Rafał Trzaskowski in a second-round runoff.

Source citations (as archived): [BBC News](<https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-europe-53215106>).

<a id="event-2020-06-28-4-6"></a>

Context: Reactions to the George Floyd protests.

**Archived source account.** The Mississippi Legislature votes to remove the Confederate battle flag from its 126-year-old state flag and to form a commission to redesign a new flag. Mississippi is the last U.S. state to display the Confederate battle emblem. The bill now heads to Governor Tate Reeves to sign into law.

Source citations (as archived): [NPR](<https://www.npr.org/2020/06/27/884306925/mississippi-lawmakers-clear-path-to-remove-confederate-emblem-from-state-flag>).

#### Sports

<a id="event-2020-06-28-5-1"></a>

Context: 2020 NFL season.

**Archived source account.** The New England Patriots reach an agreement to sign quarterback Cam Newton. He will replace the Patriots' longtime quarterback Tom Brady, who left the team in March.

Source citations (as archived): [AP](<https://apnews.com/ed0657530abaa336db7348229f418827>).

### 2020-06-29

[Pinned Wikipedia revision 1290825968](<https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Portal%3ACurrent%20events%2F2020%20June%2029&oldid=1290825968>).

#### Armed conflicts and attacks

<a id="event-2020-06-29-0-2"></a>

Context: War in Afghanistan / June 2020 Afghanistan attacks.

**Archived source account.** At least 23 civilians are killed when rockets hit a cattle market in Sangin, Helmand. The government and the Taliban blame each other for the attack.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-afghanistan-blast-taliban/blast-kills-23-afghans-at-a-cattle-market-in-southern-afghanistan-idUSKBN2401BN>).

<a id="event-2020-06-29-0-4"></a>

Context: 2020 Pakistan Stock Exchange attack.

**Archived source account.** An attack on the Pakistan Stock Exchange building in Karachi leaves at least seven people dead. The Balochistan Liberation Army (BLA) claims responsibility. However, the BLA's claim could not be independently verified.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-pakistan-attacks/seven-die-as-separatist-gunmen-attack-pakistan-stock-exchange-idUSKBN2400IS>).

#### Business and economy

<a id="event-2020-06-29-1-1"></a>

Context: Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic, Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on the arts and cultural heritage.

**Archived source account.** Cirque du Soleil files for bankruptcy in Canada and cuts 3,500 jobs.

Source citations (as archived): [CNN](<https://edition.cnn.com/2020/06/29/business/cirque-du-soleil-bankruptcy/index.html>).

#### Disasters and accidents

<a id="event-2020-06-29-2-0"></a>

**Archived source account.** At least 32 people die when their ferry collides with another vessel and sinks in the Buriganga River, near Bangladesh's capital Dhaka. There are still about 20 passengers missing.

Source citations (as archived): [BBC News](<https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-53190206>).

#### International relations

<a id="event-2020-06-29-3-1"></a>

Context: Iran–United States relations.

**Archived source account.** Iran issues an arrest warrant against U.S. President Donald Trump and asks Interpol for help. Tehran prosecutor Ali Alqasimehr accuses Trump and 30 others of "murder and terrorism charges" for the killing of Qasem Soleimani in January. Interpol refuses the request.

Source citations (as archived): [Al Jazeera](<https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/06/iran-issues-arrest-warrant-trump-asks-interpol-200629104710662.html>).

<a id="event-2020-06-29-3-3"></a>

Context: Censorship in India, China–India relations.

**Archived source account.** The Indian Ministry of Information Technology blocks 59 Chinese apps, including video sharing app TikTok, citing security and privacy concerns. The bans come as tensions mount between the two countries over the recent border skirmishes.

Source citations (as archived): [Times of India](<https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/business/india-business/centre-bans-59-mobile-apps-including-tik-tok-uc-browser-others/articleshow/76694828.cms>).

<a id="event-2020-06-29-3-5"></a>

Context: China–United States relations.

**Archived source account.** The United States formally revokes Hong Kong's special trade status; it is now seen as equivalent to mainland China.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-usa-hongkong-china-exports/u-s-ends-defense-exports-to-hong-kong-looking-to-more-restrictions-idUSKBN2402VY?il=0>).

#### Law and crime

<a id="event-2020-06-29-4-1"></a>

Context: Fillon affair.

**Archived source account.** Former Prime Minister of France François Fillon and his wife Penelope are found guilty in a fake jobs case, in which Penelope was paid €1.156 million for work she did not do as a parliamentary aide. François is sentenced to five years in prison, three of them suspended, and is barred from office for ten years; Penelope will also serve a three year suspended sentence.

Source citations (as archived): [BBC News](<https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-53217298>).

<a id="event-2020-06-29-4-3"></a>

Context: Golden State Killer.

**Archived source account.** Joseph James DeAngelo pleads guilty to all of the charges pressed against him, including 13 counts of first-degree murder.

Source citations (as archived): [The Sacramento Bee](<https://www.sacbee.com/news/local/article243868517.html>).

#### Science and technology

<a id="event-2020-06-29-5-1"></a>

Context: Social media use by Donald Trump.

**Archived source account.** Reddit bans approximately 2,000 communities for violating its rules on hate speech, including The\_Donald, which was dedicated to U.S. President Donald Trump and his supporters.

Source citations (as archived): [The New York Times](<https://www.nytimes.com/2020/06/29/technology/reddit-hate-speech.html>).

<a id="event-2020-06-29-5-2"></a>

Context: Social media use by Donald Trump.

**Archived source account.** Twitch suspends U.S. President Donald Trump's account due to "hateful conduct" from two videos from 2015 and 2016 in which he made comments about Mexicans, which were found to be offensive and in breach of their community guidelines.

Source citations (as archived): [The New York Times](<https://www.nytimes.com/2020/06/29/technology/twitch-trump-suspension-hateful-conduct.html>).

### 2020-06-30

[Pinned Wikipedia revision 1219268626](<https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Portal%3ACurrent%20events%2F2020%20June%2030&oldid=1219268626>).

#### Armed conflicts and attacks

<a id="event-2020-06-30-0-1"></a>

Context: Rohingya conflict.

**Archived source account.** Three military officers are found guilty of atrocities against the Rohingya by a court-martial in Myanmar. No details were provided on the perpetrators, their crimes, or their sentences.

Source citations (as archived): [Al Jazeera](<https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/06/myanmar-finds-troops-guilty-rohingya-atrocities-court-martial-200630101738034.html>).

<a id="event-2020-06-30-0-3"></a>

Context: Afghan peace process.

**Archived source account.** Taliban spokesman Suhail Shaheen says on Twitter that there was a videoconference on Monday between U.S. Secretary of State Mike Pompeo and Taliban official Mullah Baradar to discuss the peace process. The group reiterated its commitments to not attack American personnel, to engage in intra-Afghan talks and "not let anyone to use its soil to attack other countries". The meeting was confirmed by the U.S. State Department.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-afghanistan-taliban-usa/u-s-taliban-say-afghan-peace-effort-discussed-in-video-talks-idUSKBN24112P?il=0>).

<a id="event-2020-06-30-0-5"></a>

Context: Mali War.

**Archived source account.** The United Nations Security Council votes unanimously to extend the mandate of MINUSMA, the United Nations peacekeeping force in Mali, until June 30, 2021.

Source citations (as archived): [Xinhuanet](<http://www.xinhuanet.com/english/2020-06/30/c_139177413.htm>).

#### Arts and culture

<a id="event-2020-06-30-1-1"></a>

Context: List of monuments and memorials removed during the George Floyd protests.

**Archived source account.** A vandalized statue of former King Leopold II of Belgium is removed from public display in the city of Ghent amid anti-racism protests.

Source citations (as archived): [ABC News](<https://www.abc.net.au/news/2020-07-01/belgium-removes-king-leopold-congo-independence-black-lives/12408672>).

#### Disasters and accidents

<a id="event-2020-06-30-2-0"></a>

**Archived source account.** A large explosion at a medical clinic in Tehran, Iran, kills at least 19 people, mostly women, according to Iranian authorities. A gas leak is suspected as being the cause.

Source citations (as archived): [BBC News](<https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-middle-east-53239170>).

#### Health and environment

<a id="event-2020-06-30-3-3"></a>

Context: COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in the United States / COVID-19 pandemic in Georgia.

**Archived source account.** Savannah Mayor Van R. Johnson orders residents to wear masks in public as cases surge.

Source citations (as archived): [The Hill](<https://thehill.com/homenews/state-watch/505423-georgia-mayor-orders-residents-to-wear-masks-in-public>).

<a id="event-2020-06-30-3-5"></a>

Context: COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in the United States / COVID-19 pandemic in Massachusetts.

**Archived source account.** Massachusetts reports no COVID-19 deaths for the first time in months.

Source citations (as archived): [Boston Globe](<https://www.bostonglobe.com/2020/06/30/nation/mass-reports-zero-new-coronavirus-deaths-first-time-months/>).

<a id="event-2020-06-30-3-7"></a>

Context: COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in Mexico.

**Archived source account.** The COVID-19 death toll in Mexico reaches to 28,000, surpassing Spain.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-mexico-tally/mexico-coronavirus-death-toll-hits-28510-exceeding-spain-reuters-tally-idUSKBN24301W>).

<a id="event-2020-06-30-3-9"></a>

Context: COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in Fiji.

**Archived source account.** Fiji quarantines 160 peacekeeping soldiers who returned from the Middle East on Saturday after the army had expressed concern that some of the troops may have been in contact with infected people.

Source citations (as archived): [RNZ](<https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/420195/fijian-troops-under-strict-covid-19-watch>).

#### International relations

<a id="event-2020-06-30-4-1"></a>

Context: India–Pakistan relations; 2020 Pakistan Stock Exchange attack.

**Archived source account.** Prime Minister Imran Khan says "There is no doubt that India is behind the attack" on the Pakistan Stock Exchange yesterday. India rebuffs the accusation and says it had nothing to do with the assault.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-pakistan-attacks/pakistani-pm-says-no-doubt-that-india-was-behind-stock-exchange-attack-idUSKBN2411RB?il=0>).

<a id="event-2020-06-30-4-3"></a>

Context: Belgium–Democratic Republic of the Congo relations.

**Archived source account.** In a letter to President Felix Tshisekedi, King Philippe of Belgium addresses the atrocities in the Congo Free State under the rule of King Leopold II: "I would like to express my deepest regrets for the wounds of the past, the pain of today, which is rekindled by the discrimination all too present in our society."

Source citations (as archived): [The Guardian](<https://www.theguardian.com/world/2020/jun/30/belgian-king-philippe-expresses-profound-regrets-for-brutal-colonial-rule>).

<a id="event-2020-06-30-4-5"></a>

Context: Latvia–Russia relations.

**Archived source account.** Latvia bans seven channels belonging to Russian state-run news network RT, claiming it was trying to present the country as a failed state. Dmitry Kiselyov, head of the separate Russian state-run news agency Rossiya Segodnya, dismisses the claim and accuses the Latvian government of Russophobia in its ruling.

Source citations (as archived): [AP News](<https://apnews.com/0c6cf24233c7097d4d7bd89697894a60>).

#### Law and crime

<a id="event-2020-06-30-5-1"></a>

Context: 2017–2018 Iranian protests.

**Archived source account.** A court in Iran sentences former journalist and activist Ruhollah Zam to death for fueling anti-government unrest in late 2017 on social media. He was convicted of being corrupt on Earth.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-iran-journalist-verdict/iran-sentences-former-journalist-to-death-for-fuelling-unrest-idUSKBN2411Q8>).

<a id="event-2020-06-30-5-3"></a>

Context: 2020 boogaloo killings.

**Archived source account.** Facebook bans groups affiliated with the boogaloo movement, which was linked to a pair of attacks in California, US, that left two dead and three injured earlier this month and late last month.

Source citations (as archived): [AP](<https://nbc25news.com/news/nation-world/facebook-bans-violent-boogaloo-groups-not-the-term-itself>).

<a id="event-2020-06-30-5-4"></a>

**Archived source account.** Police in Vatican City raid the department in charge of the maintenance and restoration of St. Peter's Basilica. The raid came due to suspicion of corruption in the awarding of building contracts.

Source citations (as archived): [Al Jazeera](<https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/06/vatican-police-carry-raid-suspected-corruption-200630104123086.html>).

<a id="event-2020-06-30-5-5"></a>

**Archived source account.** Vietnam's civil aviation authority grounds all Pakistani pilots flying for Vietnamese airlines, as global aviation regulators respond to revelations by Pakistani authorities that more than 250 pilots obtaining licences fraudulently.

Source citations (as archived): [Al Jazeera](<https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/06/vietnam-suspends-pakistani-pilots-suspect-licences-200630071937493.html>).

#### Politics and elections

<a id="event-2020-06-30-6-1"></a>

Context: Hong Kong national security law.

**Archived source account.** China passes the controversial Hong Kong national security law.

Source citations (as archived): [The New York Times](<https://www.nytimes.com/2020/06/29/world/asia/china-hong-kong-security-law-rules.html>).

<a id="event-2020-06-30-6-2"></a>

Context: Hong Kong national security law.

**Archived source account.** The political party Demosistō of social activist Joshua Wong is disbanded following the passing of the law. Wong urges the international community to keep "speaking up for Hong Kong people".

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-hongkong-protests-wong/hong-kong-democracy-activist-group-led-by-joshua-wong-disbands-idUSKBN2410C6?il=0>).

<a id="event-2020-06-30-6-3"></a>

**Archived source account.** Demonstrations break out in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, following the shooting death of protest singer Hachalu Hundessa.

Source citations (as archived): [BBC News](<https://www.bbc.com/news/world-africa-53233531>).

<a id="event-2020-06-30-6-4"></a>

**Archived source account.** German Defence Minister Annegret Kramp-Karrenbauer orders the "partial dissolution" of the country's elite Kommando Spezialkräfte (KSK) special forces command over its suspected ties to the far-right. The KSK also has a "toxic leadership culture", according to the Defence Minister.

Source citations (as archived): [BBC News](<https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-europe-53237685>).

<a id="event-2020-06-30-6-5"></a>

**Archived source account.** Mississippi governor Tate Reeves signs a bill into legislation abandoning the state's flag.

Source citations (as archived): [The Washington Post](<https://www.washingtonpost.com/national/mississippi-flag-confederacy-removed/2020/06/30/f47df152-baed-11ea-8cf5-9c1b8d7f84c6_story.html>).

#### Sports

<a id="event-2020-06-30-7-1"></a>

Context: Reactions to the George Floyd protests.

**Archived source account.** The Premier League reaffirms its support of the Black Lives Matter movement, saying it was not political but moral support and that it was "aware of the risk posed by groups that seek to hijack popular causes and campaigns". It comes after one group, UKBLM, received widespread criticism for calling for the dismantling of capitalism, and tweeted "Free Palestine".

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://uk.reuters.com/article/uk-soccer-england-politics/premier-league-says-support-for-black-lives-matter-not-political-idUKKBN241262>).

<a id="event-2020-06-30-7-3"></a>

Context: Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on sports.

**Archived source account.** Minor League Baseball cancels its 2020 season due to the COVID-19 pandemic.

Source citations (as archived): [CNN](<https://www.cnn.com/2020/06/30/us/minor-league-baseball-spt-trnd/index.html>).


## July

### 2020-07-01

[Pinned Wikipedia revision 1219268641](<https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Portal%3ACurrent%20events%2F2020%20July%201&oldid=1219268641>).

#### Armed conflicts and attacks

<a id="event-2020-07-01-0-1"></a>

Context: Saudi Arabian-led intervention in Yemen; Iran–Saudi Arabia proxy conflict.

**Archived source account.** A Saudi-led coalition begins a military offensive against the Houthis, carrying out airstrikes against the capital Sanaa, as well as the provinces of Ma'rib, al-Jawf, al-Bayda, Hajjah and Saada. The local news describe the airstrikes as "violent" and reports scores of people injured. This is said to be the response to missile and drone attacks against Saudi Arabia from last week to last night.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-yemen-security-saudi/saudi-led-coalition-starts-military-operation-against-yemens-houthis-idUSKBN2426FU?il=0>).

<a id="event-2020-07-01-0-3"></a>

Context: Irapuato massacres.

**Archived source account.** Gunmen kill at least 24 people in a mass shooting at a drug rehabilitation center in Irapuato, Guanajuato, Mexico.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-mexico-violence/24-people-killed-in-attack-in-central-mexico-media-reports-idUSKBN2427M4>).

<a id="event-2020-07-01-0-5"></a>

Context: 2020 Oromia Clashes.

**Archived source account.** An Ethiopian military crackdown on protests in Oromia Region leaves 81 protesters dead, while several prominent politicians, such as Jawar Mohammed, have been detained. The protests began following the death of Oromo musician Hachalu Hundessa.

Source citations (as archived): [BBC News](<https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-africa-53243325>).

#### Arts and culture

<a id="event-2020-07-01-1-1"></a>

Context: Removal of Confederate monuments and memorials, List of monuments and memorials removed during the George Floyd protests.

**Archived source account.** The monument of Confederate General Stonewall Jackson is removed from Monument Avenue in Richmond, Virginia.

Source citations (as archived): [ABC News](<https://abcnews.go.com/US/wireStory/richmond-orders-removal-confederate-statues-city-land-71561398>).

<a id="event-2020-07-01-1-3"></a>

Context: Weinstein effect, Fox News controversies.

**Archived source account.** Fox News fires America's Newsroom anchor Ed Henry following allegations of sexual misconduct by a former employee.

Source citations (as archived): [CNN](<https://edition.cnn.com/2020/07/01/media/ed-henry-fired-fox-news/index.html>).

<a id="event-2020-07-01-1-4"></a>

**Archived source account.** The Finnish Air Force Command formally ends the use of the swastika in its imagery, according to the Air Force Command. However, the swastika will remain on some Air Force unit flags and decorations.

Source citations (as archived): [BBC News](<https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-europe-53249645>).

<a id="event-2020-07-01-1-5"></a>

**Archived source account.** The Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences, responding to recent criticism about the lack of racial diversity among the nominees in major Oscar award categories, invites 819 people to become new members. Of the invitees, 49% are from outside the US, 45% are women, and 36% are non-white.

Source citations (as archived): [BBC News](<https://www.bbc.com/news/entertainment-arts-53247124>).

#### Health and environment

<a id="event-2020-07-01-2-3"></a>

Context: COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in the United States / COVID-19 pandemic in California.

**Archived source account.** California Governor Gavin Newsom restricts the indoor operations of certain businesses in 19 counties for a minimum of three weeks to stop the spread of COVID-19.

Source citations (as archived): [Los Angeles Times](<https://www.latimes.com/california/story/2020-07-01/newsom-imposes-new-rollbacks-of-californias-coronavirus-reopening>).

<a id="event-2020-07-01-2-5"></a>

Context: COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in the United States / COVID-19 pandemic in Pennsylvania.

**Archived source account.** Pennsylvania Governor Tom Wolf says that masks will be required inside and outside.

Source citations (as archived): [The Hill](<https://thehill.com/homenews/state-watch/505494-pennsylvania-issues-order-requiring-people-to-wear-masks-in-public>).

<a id="event-2020-07-01-2-7"></a>

Context: COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in the United States / COVID-19 pandemic in Ohio.

**Archived source account.** Dayton becomes the first city in Ohio to mandate masks.

Source citations (as archived): [Cincinnati.com](<https://www.cincinnati.com/story/news/2020/07/01/coronavirus-ohio-dayton-first-major-ohio-city-mandate-masks/5359530002/>).

<a id="event-2020-07-01-2-9"></a>

Context: COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in the United States / COVID-19 pandemic in Florida.

**Archived source account.** Miami-Dade County is expected to mandate masks as it deals with surging cases.

Source citations (as archived): [Miami Herald](<https://www.miamiherald.com/news/coronavirus/article243931932.html>).

<a id="event-2020-07-01-2-11"></a>

Context: COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in Brazil.

**Archived source account.** The COVID-19 death toll in Brazil passes 60,000.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-brazil-tally/brazil-coronavirus-death-toll-passes-60000-as-pandemic-worsens-in-south-midwest-idUSKBN2427EB>).

<a id="event-2020-07-01-2-12"></a>

Context: COVID-19 pandemic.

**Archived source account.** The UN Security Council demands "immediate cessation of hostilities" in conflict zones around the world, due to the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic. These "durable humanitarian pauses", which do not apply to military operations against ISIL and Al-Qaeda, should begin immediately and be for at least 90 consecutive days to allow for delivery of humanitarian assistance and medical evacuations. This is the first resolution related to the COVID-19 pandemic that the council has passed.

Source citations (as archived): [NPR](<https://www.npr.org/sections/coronavirus-live-updates/2020/07/01/886079785/u-n-security-council-demands-cease-fire-in-conflict-areas-due-to-covid-19>).

#### International relations

<a id="event-2020-07-01-3-1"></a>

Context: France–Turkey relations.

**Archived source account.** France suspends its involvement in NATO's naval operation in the Mediterranean Sea enforcing an arms embargo on Libya, following an investigation into an incident between French and Turkish warships. France accuses the Turkish Naval Forces of harassing its Courbet warship, while attempting to inspect a Turkish civilian vessel suspected of breaching the arms embargo.

Source citations (as archived): [Al Jazeera](<https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/07/200701141138500.html>).

<a id="event-2020-07-01-3-3"></a>

Context: Hong Kong–United Kingdom relations, 2019–20 Hong Kong protests.

**Archived source account.** Prime Minister Boris Johnson says up to three million Hong Kong residents will be offered citizenship in the United Kingdom, following the passing of a controversial new national security law by China. Under the British government's plans, Hong Kongers will be able to settle in the UK for five years under political asylum, and after a further year will be able to apply for citizenship. Foreign Secretary Dominic Raab says there will be "no limits on numbers or quotas", due to the UK's "historic commitment to the people of Hong Kong".

Source citations (as archived): [BBC News](<https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-politics-53246899>).

<a id="event-2020-07-01-3-5"></a>

Context: Foreign relations of Taiwan, Foreign relations of Somaliland.

**Archived source account.** Taiwan announces it will mutually establish representative offices with the unrecognized breakaway state of Somaliland. While relations are not diplomatic at this point, further establishment of diplomatic relations would make Taiwan the first sovereign state to recognize Somaliland and the first new diplomatic ally that Taiwan has gained in 13 years.

Source citations (as archived): [Bloomberg News](<https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2020-07-01/taiwan-to-set-up-representative-office-in-breakaway-somaliland>).

#### Law and crime

<a id="event-2020-07-01-4-1"></a>

Context: 2019–20 Hong Kong protests.

**Archived source account.** Police in Hong Kong arrest over 300 people on the previously banned 1 July march and after the passing of the new national security law. The new law punishes crimes considered as subversion, terrorism and collusion with foreign forces with up to life in prison. It also allows extradition to the Mainland for trial.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-hongkong-protests/hong-kong-police-arrest-nearly-200-in-first-protest-under-new-security-law-idUSKBN2423Y2?il=0>).

<a id="event-2020-07-01-4-3"></a>

Context: Censorship in Turkey.

**Archived source account.** President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan vows tighter control over "immoral" social media following alleged insults to his daughter and son-in-law when they announced the birth of their fourth son on Twitter. Erdoğan specifically mentioned Twitter, YouTube and Netflix. Interior Minister Süleyman Soylu announced the arrest of a number of social media users for "insulting tweets".

Source citations (as archived): [Al Jazeera](<https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/07/turkey-erdogan-vows-social-media-controls-insults-family-200701112027760.html>).

<a id="event-2020-07-01-4-4"></a>

**Archived source account.** The Guardia di Finanza seizes over $1.2 billion (~€1 billion) worth of fenethylline tablets at a port in Salerno, Campania, Italy. It is believed that the amphetamines were manufactured by ISIL and originated in Syria. The haul, amounting to 14 metric tonnes of contraband, is the largest drug bust in history.

Source citations (as archived): [CNN](<https://www.cnn.com/2020/07/01/europe/isis-drug-seizure-italy-scli-intl/index.html>).

#### Sports

<a id="event-2020-07-01-5-0"></a>

**Archived source account.** After hospitalization in intensive care due to a sudden immune system disorder during a training camp in France, the situation of Dutch world champion short track speed skater Lara van Ruijven becomes critical.

Source citations (as archived): [NOS](<https://nos.nl/l/2338946>); [Telegraaf](<https://www.telegraaf.nl/sport/1704556717/toestand-van-ruijven-verslechtert-ze-vecht-voor-haar-leven>).

### 2020-07-02

[Pinned Wikipedia revision 1226057731](<https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Portal%3ACurrent%20events%2F2020%20July%202&oldid=1226057731>).

#### Armed conflicts and attacks

Context: Mali War.

**Archived source account.** Gunmen on motorbikes attack an ethnic Dogon village in Mopti Region, Mali, killing 32 villagers, according to local authorities.

<a id="event-2020-07-02-1-1"></a>

**Archived source account.** Casual Dining Group, which owns the Bella Italia and Café Rouge United Kingdom restaurant chains, collapses into administration with 1,900 immediate job losses.

Source citations (as archived): [BBC News](<https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/business-53270679>).

#### Disasters and accidents

<a id="event-2020-07-02-2-1"></a>

Context: 2020 Hpakant jade mine disaster.

**Archived source account.** At least 162 miners are killed by a landslide at a jade mining site in Hpakant, Kachin, Myanmar.

Source citations (as archived): [BBC News](<https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-53260834>).

<a id="event-2020-07-02-2-2"></a>

**Archived source account.** A fire and explosion hit a centrifuge production plant at a nuclear enrichment facility in Natanz, Iran. No deaths or injuries are reported.

Source citations (as archived): [AP](<https://apnews.com/50c3e7f6445ae99def6bdc65fbce6c42>).

#### Health and environment

<a id="event-2020-07-02-3-3"></a>

Context: COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in the United States / COVID-19 pandemic in New Mexico.

**Archived source account.** New Mexico Governor Michelle Lujan Grisham announces there will be $100 fines for people and businesses that do not wear masks.

Source citations (as archived): [The Hill](<https://thehill.com/changing-america/well-being/prevention-cures/505611-new-mexico-fining-100-to-those-who-dont-wear?amp>).

<a id="event-2020-07-02-3-5"></a>

Context: COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in the United States / COVID-19 pandemic in Kansas.

**Archived source account.** Kansas Governor Laura Kelly issues an executive order mandating citizens wear facemasks in public and at their workplace.

Source citations (as archived): [AP](<https://www.usnews.com/news/politics/articles/2020-07-02/kansas-governor-orders-masks-to-be-worn-in-public-at-work>).

<a id="event-2020-07-02-3-7"></a>

Context: COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in the United States / COVID-19 pandemic in Texas.

**Archived source account.** Texas Governor Greg Abbott orders citizens must wear face coverings when in public. This follows yesterday's reported state record daily high of more than 8,000 virus cases. Those who do not comply will receive an initial warning; those who refuse will face a fine of up to $250.

Source citations (as archived): [BBC News](<https://www.bbc.com/news/world-us-canada-53273281>).

<a id="event-2020-07-02-3-9"></a>

Context: COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in Oman.

**Archived source account.** Oman sees a jump of cases in a day, with 1,361 new cases and three deaths, reaching a total of 42,555 cases and 188 deaths. The Health Minister says that the country will boost its hospitals' capacity and intensive care units.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-oman/oman-boosts-hospital-capacity-as-coronavirus-cases-surge-idUSKBN2431XC?il=0>).

<a id="event-2020-07-02-3-10"></a>

**Archived source account.** The deaths of 275 elephants are confirmed in the Okavango Delta due to an unknown cause. Both poaching and anthrax have been ruled out by authorities.

Source citations (as archived): [CBS](<https://www.cbsnews.com/news/botswana-elephant-deaths-mystery-official-say-poaching-not-suspected-today-2020-07-02/>).

#### International relations

<a id="event-2020-07-02-4-2"></a>

Context: Venezuelan presidential crisis / United Kingdom–Venezuela relations.

**Archived source account.** In a case to decide who controls a $2 billion worth of gold from the Central Bank of Venezuela stored in the Bank of England, the High Court of Justice in London rules that the United Kingdom "unequivocally recognises Mr. Guaidó as President of Venezuela", refusing to give Nicolás Maduro access to the gold.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-venezuela-gold/uk-government-recognises-guaido-as-venezuelas-president-in-gold-dispute-judge-rules-idUSKBN2431FG?il=0>); [BBC News](<https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-latin-america-53262767>).

<a id="event-2020-07-02-4-4"></a>

Context: Venezuelan presidential crisis / United States–Venezuela relations, Iran–United States relations.

**Archived source account.** United States District Judge James E. Boasberg issues a warrant for the seizure of the more than 1.1 million barrels of gasoline in the four Iranian tankers en route to Venezuela.

Source citations (as archived): [Middle East Monitor](<https://www.middleeastmonitor.com/20200702-us-seeks-to-seize-gasoline-in-four-iran-tankers-bound-for-venezuela/>).

#### Law and crime

<a id="event-2020-07-02-5-0"></a>

**Archived source account.** In a Europe-wide operation, police penetrate EncroChat, a top-secret communications system used by criminals to sell drugs and plan attacks.

Source citations (as archived): [BBC News](<https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-53263310>).

<a id="event-2020-07-02-5-1"></a>

**Archived source account.** Nauru's President Lionel Aingimea announces tougher penalties for those convicted of sex offenses, including penalties on minors who, under the new law, will not have their age as a mitigating factor.

Source citations (as archived): [RNZ](<https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/420333/nauru-to-get-tough-on-sex-offenders>).

<a id="event-2020-07-02-5-2"></a>

**Archived source account.** British socialite Ghislaine Maxwell, former girlfriend of American financier and convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein, is arrested by the Federal Bureau of Investigation on suspicion of grooming victims of Epstein. She has also been charged with assisting Epstein's abuse of minors by helping to recruit and groom victims known to be underage.

Source citations (as archived): [BBC News](<https://www.bbc.com/news/world-us-canada-53268218>).

<a id="event-2020-07-02-5-3"></a>

**Archived source account.** A court in Pakistan orders that the four killers of The Wall Street Journal journalist Daniel Pearl remain in jail for at least three further months.

Source citations (as archived): [AFP](<https://english.alarabiya.net/en/News/asia/2020/07/02/Pakistani-court-orders-killers-of-WSJ-bureau-chief-to-remain-in-jail.html>).

#### Politics and elections

<a id="event-2020-07-02-6-1"></a>

Context: COVID-19 pandemic in New Zealand, Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on politics.

**Archived source account.** David Clark resigns as New Zealand's Minister of Health after security mistakes at quarantine facilities just days after the country had been declared free of COVID-19. Clark also received strong criticism for personally breaching lockdown rules twice. Prime Minister Jacinda Ardern had refused calls to sack the minister.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-newzealand/new-zealands-health-minister-resigns-after-coronavirus-criticism-idUSKBN24302W?il=0>).

<a id="event-2020-07-02-6-3"></a>

Context: 2019–20 Hong Kong protests.

**Archived source account.** Prominent pro-democracy camp politician and activist Nathan Law confirms he has safely fled Hong Kong, following the passage of a new national security law by China. He did not disclose which country he had fled to.

Source citations (as archived): [Deutsche Welle](<https://www.dw.com/en/hong-kong-activist-nathan-law-says-he-fled-city/a-54033256>).

#### Sports

<a id="event-2020-07-02-7-1"></a>

Context: Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on sports, 2019–20 NBA season.

**Archived source account.** The Los Angeles Clippers close their training facility after one of the players who is expected to play in Orlando tested positive for COVID-19.

Source citations (as archived): [Los Angeles Times](<https://www.latimes.com/sports/clippers/story/2020-07-02/clippers-close-training-facility-for-a-day-after-positive-covid-test>).

### 2020-07-03

#### Armed conflicts and attacks

Context: Mexican Drug War.

**Archived source account.** Mexican Army troops kill 12 drug cartel gunmen in Nuevo Laredo, Tamaulipas. In separate incidents, police kill five attackers in Torreón, Coahuila, and five police officers are shot dead in Guanajuato.

<a id="event-2020-07-03-0-3"></a>

Context: Mali War.

**Archived source account.** The Malian Armed Forces says nine troops were killed and two others wounded in an ambush by suspected jihadists in Mopti.

Source citations (as archived): [Al Jazeera](<https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/07/mali-soldiers-killed-ambush-army-200703174541788.html>).

<a id="event-2020-07-03-0-4"></a>

**Archived source account.** At least eight police officers are killed and five others injured in Uttar Pradesh, India, in an ambush as they were attempting to arrest a suspect for murder. The attack was carried out by several gunmen, two of whom were later killed by other officers.

<a id="event-2020-07-03-1-0"></a>

**Archived source account.** The University of Cambridge accepts the resignation of historian David Starkey and strips him of his honorary fellowship, following controversy over his remarks about slavery on a podcast.

Source citations (as archived): [BBC News](<https://www.bbc.com/news/entertainment-arts-53279273>).

<a id="event-2020-07-03-2-1"></a>

Context: 2020 China–India skirmishes § Economic response.

**Archived source account.** Indian Minister of Power R. K. Singh announces that India will halt the importation of US$2.8 billion worth of Chinese power equipment due to heightened tensions between the two nations.

#### Disasters and accidents

<a id="event-2020-07-03-3-1"></a>

Context: Sheikhupura train-van crash.

**Archived source account.** A passenger train collides with a van carrying Sikh pilgrims near Sheikhupura, Punjab, Pakistan, killing at least 21 people.

<a id="event-2020-07-03-3-2"></a>

**Archived source account.** An explosion at a fireworks factory in Hendek, Sakarya, Turkey, kills four people and injures 73 others.

Source citations (as archived): [AP](<https://apnews.com/2f36e6ba94f512f94ace91ef2451e0a9>).

#### Health and environment

<a id="event-2020-07-03-4-3"></a>

Context: COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in Asia / COVID-19 pandemic in Pakistan.

**Archived source account.** Foreign Minister Shah Mahmood Qureshi tests positive for COVID-19.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-pakistan/pakistani-foreign-minister-tests-positive-for-covid-19-idUSKBN24428W?il=0>).

<a id="event-2020-07-03-4-5"></a>

Context: COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in Asia / COVID-19 pandemic in Saudi Arabia.

**Archived source account.** Saudi Arabia surpasses 200,000 cases after reporting 4,193 infections in the past 24 hours while the death toll jumps to 1,802.

Source citations (as archived): [Al Arabiya](<https://english.alarabiya.net/en/coronavirus/2020/07/03/Coronavirus-cases-in-Saudi-Arabia-surpass-200-000-with-4-193-new-COVID-19-detected-.html>).

<a id="event-2020-07-03-4-7"></a>

Context: COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in Europe.

**Archived source account.** The European Union approves the use of the drug remdesivir to treat severe cases of COVID-19.

Source citations (as archived): [DW](<https://www.dw.com/en/coronavirus-latest-eu-approves-covid-19-drug-remdesivir/a-54034549>).

<a id="event-2020-07-03-4-9"></a>

Context: COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in Brazil.

**Archived source account.** An investigation led by the Federal University of Santa Catarina uncovers traces of SARS-CoV-2 in Florianópolis sewage samples drawn on November 27, 2019, two months earlier than the first official confirmed case of COVID-19 in the Americas on January 21, 2020, and much earlier than the first reported case in Brazil at the end of February.

Source citations (as archived): [CGTN](<https://news.cgtn.com/news/2020-07-03/COVID-19-virus-found-in-November-sewage-water-samples-in-Brazil-RORhEVcqYw/index.html>); [Web24](<https://www.web24.news/u/2020/07/scientists-say-the-new-coronavirus-has-been-in-southern-brazil-since-november.html>).

<a id="event-2020-07-03-4-10"></a>

**Archived source account.** UNICEF and the government of New Zealand pledge funding to Kiribati to target the high mortality rate among infants. The Pacific nation has a record of one in 25 children dying before the age of one due to preventable diseases.

Source citations (as archived): [RNZ](<https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/420433/kiribati-unicef-and-nz-join-forces-for-child-health>).

<a id="event-2020-07-03-4-11"></a>

**Archived source account.** German lawmakers agree to a deal to end nuclear power by 2022 and the use of coal by 2038.

Source citations (as archived): [AP](<https://www.seattletimes.com/business/germany-finalizing-plan-to-phase-out-coal-energy/>).

#### International relations

<a id="event-2020-07-03-5-1"></a>

Context: Libya–Russia relations.

**Archived source account.** Russian Foreign Affairs Minister Sergey Lavrov announces that Russia will re-open its embassy in Libya.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.usnews.com/news/world/articles/2020-07-03/russia-to-reopen-embassy-in-libya-ifax-cites-foreign-minister>).

<a id="event-2020-07-03-5-3"></a>

Context: 2020 Polish presidential election, Germany–Poland relations.

**Archived source account.** Polish president Andrzej Duda accuses Germany of meddling in the country's presidential election after the tabloid Fakt, owned by German publisher Axel Springer, reported yesterday that he pardoned a man convicted of pedophilia.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-poland-election-germany/polish-president-accuses-german-owned-tabloid-of-election-meddling-idUSKBN2442G5?il=0>).

#### Law and crime

<a id="event-2020-07-03-6-1"></a>

Context: Assassination of Jamal Khashoggi.

**Archived source account.** An Istanbul court begins an in absentia trial of 20 Saudi Arabians they accuse of involvement in the killing of Jamal Khashoggi.

Source citations (as archived): [Al Jazeera](<https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/07/turkish-court-open-jamal-khashoggi-murder-trial-200702105835749.html>).

<a id="event-2020-07-03-6-3"></a>

Context: St Paul's Cathedral bomb plot.

**Archived source account.** British Muslim convert Safiyya Shaikh is sentenced to life imprisonment for plotting to suicide bomb St Paul's Cathedral in the City of London.

Source citations (as archived): [BBC News](<https://bbc.co.uk/news/uk-53264640>).

<a id="event-2020-07-03-6-4"></a>

**Archived source account.** Scotland's Court of Session fines Greenpeace £80,000 for breaching an injunction against the occupation of a Transocean oil rig in the North Sea.

Source citations (as archived): [The Guardian](<https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2020/jul/03/judge-fines-greenpeace-80000-over-north-sea-oil-rig-occupation>).

#### Politics and elections

<a id="event-2020-07-03-7-1"></a>

Context: 2019–20 Hong Kong protests.

**Archived source account.** China appoints Zheng Yanxiong to head up the newly formed Office for Safeguarding National Security of the CPG in the HKSAR; Yanxiong is best known for his suppression of protests in Wukan in 2011.

Source citations (as archived): [BBC News](<https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-china-53275405>).

<a id="event-2020-07-03-7-3"></a>

Context: Politics of France.

**Archived source account.** Jean Castex is appointed Prime Minister of France by President Emmanuel Macron following the resignation of Édouard Philippe and amid speculation of a possible cabinet reshuffle.

Source citations (as archived): [CNBC](<https://www.cnbc.com/2020/07/03/french-prime-minister-resigns-amid-speculation-of-wider-government-reshuffle.html>); [Politico](<https://www.politico.eu/article/macron-appoints-jean-castex-as-french-prime-minister/>).

<a id="event-2020-07-03-7-4"></a>

**Archived source account.** Philippine President Rodrigo Duterte signs the Anti-Terrorism Act into law, repealing the Human Security Act signed in 2007.

Source citations (as archived): [The New York Times](<https://www.nytimes.com/2020/07/03/world/asia/duterte-antiterrorism-law-philippines.html>); [Al Jazeera](<https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/07/philippine-president-approves-widely-opposed-anti-terror-law-200703144213179.html>).

#### Sports

<a id="event-2020-07-03-8-0"></a>

**Archived source account.** The Athletics Integrity Unit announces the ban of Kenyan runner Wilson Kipsang Kiprotich from athletics for four years after missing multiple doping tests.

Source citations (as archived): [AP](<https://www.charlotteobserver.com/sports/article243983772.html>).

<a id="event-2020-07-03-8-1"></a>

**Archived source account.** The Washington Redskins and the Cleveland Indians are reviewing their names in response to the ongoing George Floyd protests.

Source citations (as archived): [NPR](<https://www.npr.org/sections/live-updates-protests-for-racial-justice/2020/07/03/887087674/washington-redskins-say-team-name-will-undergo-a-thorough-review>).

#### Armed conflicts and attacks

<a id="event-2020-07-04-0-1"></a>

Context: Somali Civil War.

**Archived source account.** A remote-controlled mine detonates in Baidoa, Somalia, killing five people and injuring 10.

Source citations (as archived): [Xinhua](<http://www.xinhuanet.com/english/2020-07/04/c_139188359.htm>).

<a id="event-2020-07-04-0-2"></a>

Context: Somali Civil War.

**Archived source account.** A suicide car bomber detonates at a checkpoint in Mogadishu, Somalia, injuring at least five people.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-somalia-blast/suicide-car-bomber-hits-checkpoint-at-somalias-mogadishu-port-idUSKCN24506D>).

<a id="event-2020-07-04-0-4"></a>

Context: Territorial disputes in the South China Sea, China–United States relations.

**Archived source account.** The USS Nimitz and the USS Ronald Reagan participate in dual-carrier operations and exercises in the disputed South China Sea.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.nbcnews.com/news/world/u-s-sends-carriers-south-china-sea-during-chinese-military-n1232899>).

<a id="event-2020-07-04-0-6"></a>

#### Arts and culture

<a id="event-2020-07-04-1-1"></a>

Context: List of monuments and memorials removed during the George Floyd protests.

**Archived source account.** Black Lives Matter protesters tear down the Statue of Christopher Columbus in Baltimore, Maryland, and throw it into the city's Inner Harbor. Baltimore City Council President Brandon Scott had previously called for the statue to be removed.

Source citations (as archived): [CNN](<https://edition.cnn.com/2020/07/05/us/baltimore-protests-christopher-columbus-statue-trnd/index.html>).

<a id="event-2020-07-04-1-2"></a>

**Archived source account.** President Donald Trump announces the building of National Garden of American Heroes through executive order, which will consist of statues of notable American political figures, activists, businesspeople, and pop culture icons.

Source citations (as archived): [CBS News](<https://www.cbsnews.com/news/watch-live-trump-to-deliver-4th-of-july-remarks-at-mount-rushmore/>).

#### Business and economy

<a id="event-2020-07-04-2-2"></a>

Context: Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic / Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom.

**Archived source account.** Pubs and barbershops are allowed to re-open in England for the first time since March.

Source citations (as archived): [NBC](<https://www.nbcnews.com/news/world/pubs-england-reopen-despite-lingering-coronavirus-fears-n1232798>).

<a id="event-2020-07-04-2-4"></a>

Context: Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic / Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic in the United States.

**Archived source account.** Donald Trump signs an extension of the Paycheck Protection Program to extend the filing deadline to August 8.

Source citations (as archived): [AP](<https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/donald-trump/trump-signs-extension-covid-relief-ppp-fund-businesses-n1232908>).

#### Disasters and accidents

<a id="event-2020-07-04-3-0"></a>

**Archived source account.** Heavy rains and mudslides occur in Kumamoto Prefecture, Kyushu, Japan. At least 14 residents of a nursing home in Kuma are feared dead after they are found "in cardio-respiratory arrest", according to prefecture Governor Ikuo Kabashima. Another 10 people are missing and dozens stranded on rooftops.

Source citations (as archived): [Al Jazeera](<https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/07/heavy-rains-trigger-floods-mudslides-southern-japan-200704082235367.html>).

<a id="event-2020-07-04-3-1"></a>

**Archived source account.** A fire is reported at a power plant in the city of Ahvaz, in south-western Iran, while a chlorine gas leak injures 70 workers at a petrochemicals plant near Bandar-e Emam Khomeyni. The incidents come after a string of other unexplained blazes and explosions at Iranian facilities.

Source citations (as archived): [The Guardian](<https://www.theguardian.com/world/2020/jul/04/fire-breaks-out-at-power-station-in-iran>).

<a id="event-2020-07-04-3-2"></a>

**Archived source account.** A Siberian tiger kills a zookeeper at Zürich Zoo in Zürich, Switzerland.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://uk.reuters.com/article/uk-swiss-tiger/siberian-tiger-kills-zookeeper-in-zurich-idUKKBN2450L2?il=0>).

#### Health and environment

<a id="event-2020-07-04-4-2"></a>

Context: COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in Spain.

**Archived source account.** The Catalan government locks down the county of Segrià, with 200,000 inhabitants, due to a major outbreak, becoming the first confinement after the end of the state of emergency.

Source citations (as archived): [Daily Mirror](<https://www.mirror.co.uk/news/world-news/breaking-spain-locks-down-area-22300476>).

<a id="event-2020-07-04-4-4"></a>

Context: COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in Iran.

**Archived source account.** President Hassan Rouhani announces new measures to curb the spread of the virus, including mandatory wearing of masks in covered public areas.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-iran/iran-imposes-new-curbs-as-coronavirus-toll-rises-idUSKBN2450DD>).

<a id="event-2020-07-04-4-6"></a>

Context: COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 drug development.

**Archived source account.** The World Health Organization suspends its trials of the malaria drug hydroxychloroquine and combination of HIV drug lopinavir/ritonavir after they fail to reduce mortality in infected patients.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-who-drugs/who-halts-hydroxychloroquine-hiv-drugs-in-covid-trials-after-failure-to-reduce-death-idUSKBN2450OJ?il=0>).

#### International relations

<a id="event-2020-07-04-5-1"></a>

Context: North Korea–United States relations.

**Archived source account.** North Korean First Vice-Foreign Minister Choe Son-hui says her country has "no interest" in a face-to-face meeting with the United States unless the U.S. discards its "hostile" policies toward North Korea.

Source citations (as archived): [Al Jazeera](<https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/07/korea-talks-plan-bolton-hints-october-surprise-200704094348905.html>).

Context: Canada–China relations.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-china-hongkong-canada/china-rebukes-canada-over-criticism-of-hong-kong-security-law-idUSKBN2450G9>).

<a id="event-2020-07-04-6-0"></a>

**Archived source account.** Phoenix, Arizona police officers threaten, shoot and kill a man inside a parked car in an incident captured on bystander video, sparking protests in the city. Police say he pointed a gun at them first.

Context: LGBT rights in Poland.

**Archived source account.** President of Poland Andrzej Duda announces that he will propose a constitutional amendment to outlaw LGBT adoption in Poland.

Source citations (as archived): [The Guardian](<https://www.theguardian.com/world/2020/jul/04/poland-president-plans-to-forbid-adoption-by-same-sex-couples>).

Source citations (as archived): [RT](<https://www.rt.com/news/493811-dark-matter-hydrogen-fast-telescope/>).

### 2020-07-05

[Pinned Wikipedia revision 1087457349](<https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Portal%3ACurrent%20events%2F2020%20July%205&oldid=1087457349>).

#### Armed conflicts and attacks

<a id="event-2020-07-05-0-1"></a>

Context: Somali Civil War.

**Archived source account.** A local politician is abducted and killed by Al-Shabaab militants in Bal'ad, Middle Shabelle, Somalia.

Source citations (as archived): [Voice of America](<https://www.voanews.com/africa/al-shabab-militants-abduct-kill-somali-lawmaker>).

<a id="event-2020-07-05-0-3"></a>

Context: American-led intervention in Iraq (2014–2021).

**Archived source account.** A Katyusha rocket falls in the Green Zone of Baghdad, Iraq, injuring a child and damaging a house. Iraqi security forces also thwart another rocket launched at Camp Taji, which houses U.S. troops. Also, a MIM-104 Patriot defense system shoots down a missile launched against the U.S. embassy.

Source citations (as archived): [Al Arabiya](<https://english.alarabiya.net/en/News/middle-east/2020/07/05/Rocket-attack-on-Baghdad-Green-Zone-injures-child-damages-house.html>).

<a id="event-2020-07-05-0-5"></a>

Context: Second Libyan Civil War.

**Archived source account.** The Government of National Accord (GNA) warns of a "response in the right place and at the right time" after a "foreign air force" bombed the Al-Watiya Air Base in an overnight air raid, according to the GNA's Deputy Defence Minister Salah al-Namrush. Al-Namrush did not specify which foreign air force was behind the raid, which is believed to have targeted a Turkish anti-aircraft missile system.

Source citations (as archived): [Al Jazeera](<https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/07/libya-gov-vows-response-base-hit-foreign-air-force-200705183314172.html>).

<a id="event-2020-07-05-0-7"></a>

Context: Hachalu Hundessa riots.

**Archived source account.** The death toll amid civil unrest in Oromia Region, Ethiopia, rises to 166 people, including 11 security personnel. More than 1,000 people have been arrested.

Source citations (as archived): [BBC News](<https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-africa-53298845>).

Context: COVID-19 pandemic in India.

**Archived source account.** The government extends the lockdown in the city of Agra and delays the reopening of the Taj Mahal for tourists and visitors after a spike in COVID-19 cases in the country.

<a id="event-2020-07-05-3-1"></a>

Context: 2020 Kyushu floods.

**Archived source account.** The death toll from floods in Kumamoto Prefecture, Japan, rises to 20 and 14 people remain missing. Prime Minister Shinzo Abe meets with a disaster task force team to step up rescue efforts. Meanwhile, weather agencies warn people to remain alert as more rains are predicted.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-japan-floods/flood-death-toll-hits-20-as-japan-warned-of-more-rainfall-idUSKBN24604A>).

### 2020-07-06

[Pinned Wikipedia revision 1277894467](<https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Portal%3ACurrent%20events%2F2020%20July%206&oldid=1277894467>).

#### Armed conflicts and attacks

<a id="event-2020-07-06-0-0"></a>

**Archived source account.** A group of unknown assailants assassinate prominent Iraqi historian and government advisor Hisham al-Hashimi near his home in Zayouna, Baghdad. No group has claimed responsibility for his killing.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://uk.reuters.com/article/uk-iraq-security/gunmen-kill-prominent-iraqi-analyst-and-advisor-officials-idUKKBN2472KA?il=0>).

#### Business and economy

<a id="event-2020-07-06-1-0"></a>

**Archived source account.** Two lawyer groups file petitions to the Philippine Supreme Court to question the constitutionality of the recent anti-terrorism law. Also, prominent pro-democracy activists Joshua Wong and Agnes Chow appear in court. Wong pleads not guilty to inciting others to participate in an unlawful assembly last year while Chow pleads guilty to similar charges.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-hongkong-protests/hong-kong-court-denies-bail-to-first-person-charged-under-new-law-idUSKBN2470YH>).

#### Armed conflicts and attacks

<a id="event-2020-07-08-0-1"></a>

Context: Internal conflict in Myanmar.

**Archived source account.** Amnesty International says it has conducted a report which says that Myanmar's armed forces "have killed civilians, including children in indiscriminate air attacks" in Rakhine and Chin states, urging the United Nations Security Council to launch a war crimes investigation. Myanmar has been fighting the separatist Arakan Army in the region. The government did not immediately respond to calls for comment.

Source citations (as archived): [Al Jazeera](<https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/07/myanmar-air-raids-killed-children-amount-war-crimes-200707194910335.html>).

Context: Insurgency in the Maghreb.

**Archived source account.** At least 180 bodies have been found in mass graves in Djibo, Burkina Faso, where soldiers are fighting jihadists. It is suspected that the government forces were involved in mass extrajudicial executions.

Source citations (as archived): [BBC News](<https://www.bbc.com/news/world-africa-53333366>).

<a id="event-2020-07-08-0-5"></a>

Context: July 2020 Afghanistan attacks.

**Archived source account.** A suicide bomber kills three people when he drives a military vehicle packed with explosives near the provincial governor's residence in Kandahar, Afghanistan. The Taliban claims responsibility.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-afghanistan-attacks/taliban-suicide-bomber-kills-three-as-violence-rises-despite-peace-push-idUSKBN2491SP>).

<a id="event-2020-07-08-0-7"></a>

Context: Insurgency in Jammu and Kashmir.

**Archived source account.** Local Bharatiya Janata Party leader Sheikh Wazeem Bari and two members of his family are shot dead in Bandipore district, Jammu and Kashmir. Senior Ministry of Home Affairs official K. Vijay Kumar blames the Islamic terrorist group Jaish-e-Mohammed.

Source citations (as archived): [Hindustan Times](<https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-news/bjp-leader-his-father-and-brother-shot-dead-in-kashmir-cops-arrest-his-security-guards/story-UsqR5iWYycDNLGmNGOBwiP.html>).

#### Armed conflicts and attacks

<a id="event-2020-07-09-0-1"></a>

Context: Afghan peace process, War in Afghanistan.

**Archived source account.** An Afghan government spokesman says it will continue to release Taliban prisoners though disagreement prevails over the release of some 600 of them that are considered a "threat to national security". The Taliban could not be reached for comment and it is not clear whether they are willing to accept to start talks based on the list of prisoners set to be freed.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-usa-afghanistan-taliban-prisoners/afghanistan-to-release-prisoners-from-taliban-list-in-push-for-talks-idUSKBN24A17D>).

Context: Insurgency in the Sahel.

**Archived source account.** The United States says it is "deeply concerned" about abuses by state security forces in the Sahel and threatens to cut aid to the G5 nations that form a coalition in the area – Burkina Faso, Mali, Mauritania, Niger, and Chad – if those issues are not addressed. The U.S. also welcomes a summit to be held between the G5 nations and France and Spain.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-sahel-security-usa/u-s-warns-aid-at-risk-unless-alleged-abuses-in-west-africas-sahel-region-addressed-idUSKBN24A223?il=0>).

<a id="event-2020-07-09-1-3"></a>

Context: COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in Asia / COVID-19 pandemic in the Philippines.

He goes on to claim that following the examples of the United States', Brazil's and others' "bold actions" would result in "pandemonium", and the potential resultant spike in COVID-19 cases would land the nation in "deep shit".

Source citations (as archived): [Vice](<https://www.vice.com/en_us/article/pky359/philippines-deep-shit-follows-trump-bolsonaro-reopening-duterte>).

<a id="event-2020-07-09-1-5"></a>

Context: COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in Asia / COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia.

**Archived source account.** Indonesia announced the biggest daily rise of 2,657 new COVID-19 cases, taking the nationwide tally to 70,736. West Java reported the highest surge with 962 cases. This significant increase comes from the Army’s Officer Candidate School (Secapa) cluster.

Source citations (as archived): [WREX](<https://wrex.com/2020/07/09/german-intel-warns-against-giving-data-to-chinese-tech-firms/#:~:text=BERLIN%20(AP)%20%E2%80%94%20Germany&#x27;s%20domestic,the%20hands%20of%20China&#x27;s%20government.&amp;text=The%20head%20of%20the%20BfV,can%20only%20warn%20against%20this.%E2%80%9D>).

Mazars USA, LLP that lower courts had not properly assessed the separation of powers between Congress and the President when the House of Representatives attempted to similarly subpoena his tax returns.

#### Business and economy

<a id="event-2020-07-10-2-1"></a>

Context: Boycott Chinese products, China–India relations.

**Archived source account.** The Indian government asks e-commerce platforms such as Amazon and Flipkart to display the country of origin on new products listed by sellers on their sites by August 1 and items that were already being sold by October 1 without stipulating a mandatory deadline. The move comes during heightened tensions between India and China following the 2020 China–India skirmishes and a campaign to boycott Chinese-origin products in India.

Source citations (as archived): [The Economic Times](<https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/economy/foreign-trade/display-country-of-origin-by-aug-1-govt-to-ecomm/articleshow/76864214.cms>).

Context: Enlargement of the eurozone.

**Archived source account.** The European Central Bank accepts Bulgaria and Croatia into the European Exchange Rate Mechanism, a mandatory stage for countries that wish to adopt the euro. This is the currency bloc's first major expansion in half a decade.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-eurozone-economy-croatia-bulgaria/bulgaria-croatia-take-vital-step-to-joining-euro-idUSKBN24B2JM?il=0>).

<a id="event-2020-07-10-2-4"></a>

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-pakistan-airlines-usa/u-s-bans-pakistan-international-airlines-flights-over-pilot-concerns-idUSKBN24A3HV?il=0>).

#### Disasters and accidents

<a id="event-2020-07-10-3-0"></a>

**Archived source account.** Venice, Italy, tests the MOSE system of 78 mobile floodgates for the first time. Construction of MOSE was authorized by Comitatone, the city's Venetian Lagoon committee, in April 2003. Commissioner Elisabetta Spitz said the project still needs another 18 months of testing. In November 2019, Venice was hit by the worst floods in half a century.

<a id="event-2020-07-10-3-1"></a>
