<a id="event-2020-07-27-3-13"></a>

Context: COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in Asia / COVID-19 pandemic in Vietnam.

**Archived source account.** After three residents tested positive for COVID-19, Vietnam announces it will evacuate 80,000 people, mostly domestic tourists, from Da Nang. The evacuation will span at least four days and involve roughly 100 domestic flights per day.

Source citations (as archived): [Sky News](<https://news.sky.com/story/vietnam-evacuating-80-000-people-from-city-after-three-positive-coronavirus-tests-12037025>).

<a id="event-2020-07-27-3-16"></a>

Context: COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in Oceania / COVID-19 pandemic in Australia.

**Archived source account.** Victoria reports its record number of new COVID-19 cases so far, with 532 cases in the last 24 hours, as well as six deaths. This number also made it Australia's highest one day increase of new cases.

Source citations (as archived): [ABC News Australia](<https://www.abc.net.au/news/2020-07-27/victoria-records-more-than-500-news-coronavirus-cases/12493886>).

<a id="event-2020-07-27-3-17"></a>

Context: COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in Oceania / COVID-19 pandemic in Australia.

**Archived source account.** New South Wales reports 17 new cases of COVID-19. Of these, eight are returning travellers in hotel quarantine and another nine are locally transmitted, including one case under investigation.

<a id="event-2020-07-27-3-19"></a>

Context: COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in Oceania / COVID-19 pandemic in Papua New Guinea.

Source citations (as archived): [RNZ](<https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/422152/png-capital-goes-into-lockdown-as-covid-surges>).

<a id="event-2020-07-27-3-21"></a>

Context: COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in Belgium.

**Archived source account.** Belgium announces the unveiling of drastic social distancing measures aimed at avoiding a new lockdown. These measures include restricting social contact outside every household to five people over the next four weeks and limiting crowds at public events to 100 people indoors and 200 people outdoors. This measure will take effect next Wednesday.

Source citations (as archived): [France24](<https://www.france24.com/en/20200727-belgium-tightens-covid-19-restrictions-to-avoid-another-lockdown-amid-rise-in-cases>).

<a id="event-2020-07-27-3-22"></a>

Context: COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in Belgium.

**Archived source account.** Antwerp imposes a curfew from 11.30 p.m. to 6 a.m and the mandatory wearing of face masks in public spaces should a distance of 1.5 meters between individuals not be observed.

Source citations (as archived): [The Washington Post](<https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/europe/belgium-implements-drastic-plan-to-avoid-another-lockdown/2020/07/27/0f9268e8-d01e-11ea-826b-cc394d824e35_story.html>).

#### International relations

<a id="event-2020-07-27-4-1"></a>

Context: China–Philippines relations.

**Archived source account.** Philippine President Rodrigo Duterte says he has no choice but to treat the disputes in the South China Sea diplomatically because the alternative is to "go to war with China", defending a government decision not to press a ruling that went in favor of the Philippines. Separately, Duterte claimed China may offer vaccines “on credit” if not as a donation and grants package.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-philippines-politics-southchinasea/philippines-duterte-says-cannot-confront-china-over-maritime-claims-idUSKCN24S110>); [Asia Times](<https://asiatimes.com/2020/07/duterte-trots-out-tired-tropes-in-key-speech/>).

<a id="event-2020-07-27-4-3"></a>

Context: China–India relations, Boycott China.

**Archived source account.** The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology of the Government of India bans 47 Chinese-origin apps on the grounds that these apps were clones of banned apps made by Chinese companies to circumvent bans. The ban comes less than a month after 59 apps were banned in June, including TikTok and Helo, as the government deemed them a "threat to national security". India also begins investigating over 250 Chinese apps over user privacy violations including popular Tencent-backed gaming app PlayerUnknown's Battlegrounds. The bans comes in the wake of a movement to boycott Chinese products in India following the 2020 China-India skirmishes.

Source citations (as archived): [India Today](<https://www.indiatoday.in/india/story/pubg-alibaba-xiaomi-to-be-banned-india-prepares-list-of-over-250-chinese-apps-1704814-2020-07-27>).

<a id="event-2020-07-27-4-5"></a>

Context: Libyan Civil War (2014–present).

**Archived source account.** The United Nations Support Mission in Libya announces it will begin an audit of the central banks of the internationally-recognized Government of National Accord and the rival House of Representatives, saying it is a “critical step” in eventually uniting both factions.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-libya-security-cenbank/u-n-announces-start-of-libya-central-bank-audit-idUSKCN24S280?il=0>).

**Archived source account.** Monday's regularly scheduled baseball games between the Baltimore Orioles and Miami Marlins, and the New York Yankees and Philadelphia Phillies, are postponed because 14 members of the Marlins traveling party, including 12 players, tested positive for COVID-19. Tuesday's Orioles-Marlins game is also postponed; the status of the second Yankees-Phillies game will be announced later. Miami just finished a three-game series in Philadelphia this past weekend. Before Sunday’s series finale, Miami learned that four of its players had tested positive and adjusted its lineup accordingly.

<a id="event-2020-07-28-4-1"></a>

Context: 1Malaysia Development Berhad scandal.

**Archived source account.** Former Malaysian Prime Minister Najib Razak is found guilty by the Malaysian High Court and sentenced to 12 years' imprisonment and fined RM210 million (US$47 million). The High Court convicted Najib on all seven counts of abuse of power, money laundering and criminal breach of trust over misappropriating over RM42 million (US$ 10 million) from 1Malaysia Development Berhad's former subsidiary SRC International to his personal bank accounts.

Source citations (as archived): [Malay Mail](<https://www.malaymail.com/news/malaysia/2020/07/28/high-court-finds-najib-guilty-of-misappropriation-of-rm42m-src-internationa/1888749>); [BBC News](<https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-53563065>); [Channel News Asia](<https://www.channelnewsasia.com/news/asia/malaysia-najib-razak-1mdb-trial-verdict-guilty-12967036>).

Context: George Floyd protests in Australia.

**Archived source account.** The New South Wales Police arrests six people, including organizer Paddy Gibson, at a Black Lives Matter rally in Sydney; five of those were handed penalty infringement notices. They arrested them because they were breaching a public health order.

Source citations (as archived): [ABC News Australia](<https://www.abc.net.au/news/2020-07-28/sydney-black-lives-matter-protesters-detained/12498034>).

**Archived source account.** Following massive public backlash, Public Safety Minister Bill Blair announces a public inquiry will be held over the law enforcement response to the rampage in Nova Scotia, Canada, last April, which left 23 dead, including the gunman.

Source citations (as archived): [Global News](<https://globalnews.ca/news/7224747/nova-scotia-mps-inquiry-mass-shooting/>).

<a id="event-2020-07-28-4-6"></a>

Tai in a Facebook post called it the "end of academic freedom" in the city.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-hongkong-security/hong-kong-university-sacks-veteran-democracy-activist-idUSKCN24T1VN?il=0>).

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-chile-politics/chiles-president-pinera-removes-interior-foreign-defense-ministers-idUSKCN24T2MX?il=0>).

### 2020-07-29

#### Armed conflicts and attacks

<a id="event-2020-07-29-0-1"></a>

Context: Yemeni Civil War, Saudi Arabian-led intervention in Yemen; Yemeni peace process.

**Archived source account.** The separatist Southern Transitional Council (STC) announces it is giving up its aspiration of self-rule in Yemen to implement a stalled peace deal brokered by Saudi Arabia. A spokesman for the group says they have "achieved their goal". The STC believes in establishing an independent state in southern Yemen similar to the one that existed between 1967 and 1990.

Source citations (as archived): [AP](<https://apnews.com/c0d8d226b7c8c655f34afe830d90c8c4>).

<a id="event-2020-07-29-0-3"></a>

**Archived source account.** The U.S. imposes further sanctions on Syrian President Bashar al-Assad and his 19-year-old son Hafez, and warns that it will also sanction anyone who engages with the government in Damascus. Kelly Craft, U.S. ambassador to the United Nations, says the sanctions are not intended to harm civilians and that they do not target humanitarian aid.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-mideast-crisis-syria-usa/u-s-slaps-sanctions-on-syria-in-push-for-assad-to-end-war-idUSKCN24U2F7?il=0>).

#### International relations

<a id="event-2020-07-29-5-1"></a>

Context: Fiji–United States relations.

**Archived source account.** Fiji's opposition parties urge the government to reconsider its decision of closing Fiji's embassy in the United States, the European Union, and other countries, and blame Chinese influence in the Pacific.

Source citations (as archived): [RNZ](<https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/422305/fiji-urged-to-reconsider-closing-us-embassy>).

<a id="event-2020-07-29-5-3"></a>

Context: Belarus–Russia relations.

**Archived source account.** Belarusian security forces arrest 32 members of the private military company Wagner Group at a sanitarium near Minsk in an overnight raid. All those detained are Russian nationals, according to authorities. President Alexander Lukashenko convenes an emergency meeting with his security council, and instructs the Chairman of the State Security Committee to ask Russia for an official explanation.

Source citations (as archived): [The Guardian](<https://www.theguardian.com/world/2020/jul/29/belarus-says-dozens-of-russians-arrested-ahead-of-presidential-election>).

#### Law and crime

<a id="event-2020-07-29-6-2"></a>

Context: George Floyd protests / George Floyd protests in Minneapolis–Saint Paul.

**Archived source account.** A masked, umbrella-wielding man accused of helping incite riots and looting in the aftermath of the death of George Floyd is identified.

Source citations (as archived): [ABC News](<https://abcnews.go.com/US/man-helped-ignite-george-floyd-riots-identified-white/story?id=72051536>).

<a id="event-2020-07-29-6-4"></a>

Context: George Floyd protests / George Floyd protests in Portland, Oregon.

**Archived source account.** Oregon Governor Kate Brown announces that federal agents deployed to Portland, including all Customs and Border Protection and Immigration and Customs Enforcement officers, will start withdrawing tomorrow, per her conversation with Vice President Mike Pence.

Source citations (as archived): [Business Insider](<https://www.businessinsider.com/federal-agents-to-leave-portland-oregon-governor-kate-brown-2020-7?utm_source=notification&amp;utm_medium=referral>).

<a id="event-2020-07-29-6-6"></a>

Context: George Floyd protests / George Floyd protests in Wisconsin.

**Archived source account.** Two women, Kerida O’Reilly (33) and Samantha Hamer (26), are charged for attacking Wisconsin State Senator Tim Carpenter outside the Wisconsin State Capitol building in Madison.

Source citations (as archived): [The Hill](<https://thehill.com/blogs/blog-briefing-room/news/509678-two-women-arrested-in-beating-of-wisconsin-state-senator-at>).

<a id="event-2020-07-29-6-8"></a>

Context: Censorship in Turkey.

**Archived source account.** The Grand National Assembly of Turkey passes a new social media regulation bill that requires foreign sites to appoint Turkish-based representatives to help monitor content, and will punish companies that don't comply with fines and throttling bandwidth.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-turkey-security-socialmedia/turkey-passes-law-to-regulate-social-media-content-idUSKCN24U0EN?il=0>).

<a id="event-2020-07-29-6-10"></a>

Context: Blasphemy in Pakistan.

**Archived source account.** A man accused of blasphemy under a new controversial law is shot dead by a gunman in the courtroom while he was standing trial for allegedly insulting Islam. The victim was part of the Ahmadiyya faith, a minority Islamic sect that Pakistan declared non-Muslim in 1974 for regarding its founder as a prophet. The suspect was a former member.

Source citations (as archived): [DW](<https://www.dw.com/en/pakistan-man-accused-of-blasphemy-shot-dead-at-court-trial/a-54365714>).

<a id="event-2020-07-29-6-11"></a>

**Archived source account.** A man accused of attacking pro-democracy Hong Kong activist and convener of the Civil Human Rights Front Jimmy Sham says he was offered a HK$2 million bounty to "cripple" him in last year's attack.

Source citations (as archived): [South China Morning Post](<https://www.scmp.com/news/hong-kong/law-and-crime/article/3095205/hk2-million-bounty-was-offered-cripple-hong-kong>).

<a id="event-2020-07-29-6-12"></a>

**Archived source account.** Moroccan journalist and human rights activist Omar Radi is arrested and charged with rape and aiding foreign spies. The charges come after Amnesty International reported that the Moroccan government was using Israeli spyware to spy on dissidents like him.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-morocco-justice/morocco-arrests-dissident-journalist-on-rape-and-spy-charges-idUSKCN24U2V0?il=0>).

#### Disasters and accidents

<a id="event-2020-07-30-2-2"></a>

Context: 2020 Atlantic hurricane season / Hurricane Isaias.

**Archived source account.** Hurricane Isaias is expected to head towards Florida, prompting the state to close their COVID-19 test sites. The hurricane has made landfall in Puerto Rico, causing landslides, flooding, and power outages.

Source citations (as archived): [CBS News](<https://www.cbsnews.com/news/tropical-storm-isaias-puerto-rico-us-mainland/>); [CNN](<https://amp.cnn.com/cnn/2020/07/30/weather/tropical-storm-isaias-forecast-puerto-rico-florida/index.html>).

**Archived source account.** An explosion destroys a restaurant in Kōriyama, Japan, killing one person and injuring another 18. A gas leak is suspected to be the cause of the accident.

Context: United States Marine Corps.

**Archived source account.** One Marine is killed and one Sailor and seven additional Marines went missing when their Amphibious Assault Vehicle sinks near San Clemente Island off the coast of Southern California. They were from the 15th Marine Expeditionary Unit, stationed at Marine Corps Base Camp Pendleton, San Diego County. This is the third major AAV accident involving Camp Pendleton Marines since 2011.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-usa-marine/massive-search-under-way-off-california-for-8-missing-u-s-marines-one-dead-idUSKCN24W1QG>); [AP](<https://apnews.com/9816c0b6abcf7773f77b6caceb0f7356>).

#### Law and crime

<a id="event-2020-07-30-5-1"></a>

Context: Agbudu shooting.

**Archived source account.** A mass shooting in Kogi State, Nigeria leaves 14 people dead and another six injured. Thirteen of the fatalities were member of the same family. Police said that a long-standing row over land rights is suspected to be the motive behind the attack.

Source citations (as archived): [The Guardian Nigeria](<https://guardian.ng/news/gunmen-kill-family-of-13-in-kogi-state/>).

<a id="event-2020-07-30-5-3"></a>

**Archived source account.** St. Louis County prosecutor Wesley Bell announces that Darren Wilson, the Ferguson police officer that shot and killed Michael Brown, will not be charged.

<a id="event-2020-07-30-5-4"></a>

Reed's father told reporters after the verdict he is planning to appeal directly to Russian President Vladimir Putin.

Source citations (as archived): [Al Jazeera](<https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/07/russia-jails-marine-trevor-reed-police-assault-200730104547653.html>).

Source citations (as archived): [Al Jazeera](<https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/07/uganda-poacher-killed-rare-gorilla-11-years-jail-200730112507761.html>).

### 2020-07-31

[Pinned Wikipedia revision 1083175781](<https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Portal%3ACurrent%20events%2F2020%20July%2031&oldid=1083175781>).

#### Armed conflicts and attacks

<a id="event-2020-07-31-0-1"></a>

Context: 2020 Chaman border clash.

**Archived source account.** Twenty-two people are killed in clashes between Afghan civilians and Pakistani military forces. Fifteen people died and 80 others injured in Kandahar after Pakistani soldiers attacked civilian areas, while seven people were killed and 31 others injured in Pakistan when a crowd trying to enter Afghanistan became unruly and attacked military installations. The Afghan government warns of action if Pakistan "continues its rocket attacks", while the Pakistani military says it opened fire in self-defense, returning fire to the Afghan side.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-pakistan-afghanistan-clashes/afghanistan-and-pakistan-say-22-die-in-border-clashes-idUSKCN24W1AB?il=0>).

<a id="event-2020-07-31-1-2"></a>

Context: Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic, COVID-19 recession / COVID-19 pandemic in Spain.

**Archived source account.** The Spanish economy suffers a historically large fall in the second quarter of 18.5% of GDP and enters in recession, making Spain the Eurozone country most economically devastated by the pandemic.

Source citations (as archived): [El Mundo](<https://www.elmundo.es/economia/macroeconomia/2020/07/31/5f23c253fc6c8346718b4585.html>).

Context: Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic, COVID-19 recession.

**Archived source account.** Eurozone suffers an unprecedented 12.1% drop in GDP and enters in technical recession.

Source citations (as archived): [Euronews](<https://www.euronews.com/2020/07/31/coronavirus-euro-area-economy-shrinks-by-12-1-biggest-drop-on-record>).

**Archived source account.** James Murdoch, the younger son of media mogul Rupert Murdoch, resigns from the board of News Corporation citing "disagreements over editorial content... (and) some strategic decisions." News Corp owns media in Australia, the United Kingdom and the United States.

Source citations (as archived): [BBC News](<https://www.bbc.com/news/business-53617966>).

#### Armed conflicts and attacks

<a id="event-2020-08-03-0-3"></a>

Context: War in Afghanistan / August 2020 Afghanistan attacks / Jalalabad prison attack.

**Archived source account.** The military retake a prison in Jalalabad, Nangarhar that came under attack yesterday by ISIL, resulting in a mass jailbreak and shootout between Afghan forces and jihadists that ended today. At least 29 people are killed and 50 injured, among them civilians, prisoners, guards and Afghan security forces.

Source citations (as archived): [AP](<https://apnews.com/a6e54b22ba067b2d0fc89e9be4c27fb1>).

<a id="event-2020-08-03-0-5"></a>

Context: Israeli–Syrian ceasefire line incidents during the Syrian Civil War, Israeli involvement in the Syrian Civil War.

**Archived source account.** Israeli Air Force helicopters strike Syrian military observation posts, intelligence collection systems, anti-aircraft batteries and command-and-control bases in Quneitra Governorate, in response to yesterday's incident along the Purple Line border fence in the Golan Heights, in which four militants were killed after attempting to plant an IED where Israeli soldiers patrol.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-israel-syria-violence/israeli-aircraft-hit-syria-after-squad-tried-to-bomb-border-fence-military-says-idUSKBN24Y0RP?il=0>).

#### Arts and culture

<a id="event-2020-08-03-1-0"></a>

Georg Ratzinger, in Bavaria. His personal secretary, Archbishop George Ganswein, states "the health conditions are not of particular concern, except for those of a 93 year old who is going through a painful, but not serious, disease."

<a id="event-2020-08-03-2-0"></a>

**Archived source account.** Italian Prime Minister Giuseppe Conte inaugurates the new replacement for the original Ponte Morandi bridge, two years after its collapse, amidst the ongoing pandemic in the country. Italian President Sergio Mattarella and bridge architect Renzo Piano attend the ceremony.

Source citations (as archived): [The New York Times](<https://www.nytimes.com/2020/08/03/world/europe/genoa-italy-new-bridge.html>); [The Architect's Newspaper](<https://www.archpaper.com/2020/08/renzo-pianos-saint-george-bridge-inaugurated-in-genoa-italy/>).

#### Disasters and accidents

<a id="event-2020-08-03-3-2"></a>

Context: 2020 Atlantic hurricane season / Hurricane Isaias.

**Archived source account.** Isaias regains hurricane strength with maximum winds of 75 mph (120 km/h) after leaving 2-4 inches of precipitation and causing minor power outages along the Florida coast. The storm is moving north-northeast at 16 mph (26 km/h), and is expected to make landfall in eastern North Carolina early Tuesday and then continue along the Mid-Atlantic coast heading toward the northeastern states. The storm surge will cause normally dry areas near the coast to be flooded with rising waters before moving inland.

Source citations (as archived): [NPR](<https://www.npr.org/2020/08/03/898620721/tropical-storm-isaias-expected-to-make-landfall-as-a-hurricane-in-carolinas>); [National Hurricane Center](<https://www.nhc.noaa.gov/text/refresh/MIATCPAT4+shtml/040000.shtml>).

<a id="event-2020-08-03-6-1"></a>

Context: Internet censorship in Thailand.

**Archived source account.** Thailand's digital minister threatens action against Facebook for not complying with the government request to restrict content that is illegal in the country, including insults of King Vajiralongkorn. Facebook responded by disabling English-to-Thai automatic translations.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-thailand-facebook/thai-minister-threatens-facebook-with-legal-action-over-restriction-requests-idUSKBN24Z1RA?il=0>).

Context: Monarchy of Spain, Corruption in Spain.

**Archived source account.** The Spanish Royal Household announces that Emeritus King Juan Carlos I has informed King Felipe VI that he is leaving the country motivated by "the public repercussion that certain past events are generating". His finances are being judicially investigated by a Swiss judge and the Spanish Prosecutor's Office for alleged financial dealings from Haramain high-speed railway construction and his accounts in tax havens.

Source citations (as archived): [El Mundo](<https://www.elmundo.es/espana/2020/08/03/5f26ec90fc6c832f068b45a3.html>); [The Washington Post](<https://www.washingtonpost.com/politics/amid-a-financial-scandal-former-spanish-king-juan-carlos-i-says-he-is-leaving-spain-to-live-in-another-country/2020/08/03/0df33322-d5a6-11ea-a788-2ce86ce81129_story.html>); [BBC News](<https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-53642283>).

This also would apply to any others that happen in the wake of a statewide emergency or disaster directive.

<a id="event-2020-08-03-8-0"></a>

**Archived source account.** Two anonymous sources confirm to Reuters that the classified United Kingdom–United States trade documents leaked ahead of the UK parliamentary election last year was caused by Russian hacking of the email account of former UK International Trade Secretary Liam Fox. They declined to name which Russian group or organisation they believed was responsible, but said the attack bore the hallmarks of a government-backed operation.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://uk.reuters.com/article/uk-britain-russia-hack-exclusive/exclusive-papers-leaked-before-uk-election-in-suspected-russian-operation-were-hacked-from-ex-trade-minister-sources-idUKKBN24Z1UL>).

#### Business and economy

<a id="event-2020-08-04-0-1"></a>

Context: Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on airlines.

**Archived source account.** UK-based airline Virgin Atlantic declares itself bankrupt and files for Chapter 15 bankruptcy protection in New York amid a decline in international flights during the COVID-19 pandemic.

Source citations (as archived): [The Guardian](<https://www.theguardian.com/business/2020/aug/04/virgin-atlantic-files-for-bankruptcy-as-covid-continues-to-hurt-airlines>).

#### Disasters and accidents

<a id="event-2020-08-04-1-1"></a>

Context: 2020 Beirut explosions.

**Archived source account.** Several explosions in the port of Beirut, Lebanon, kill more than 70 people, injure more than 4,000 others and send shock waves that damage homes as far as 10 kilometers (6 miles) away. Prime Minister Hassan Diab, whose wife and daughter are among the injured, declares Wednesday a national day of mourning. The shockwave was felt in a few nearby countries.

Source citations (as archived): [BBC News](<https://www.bbc.com/news/world-middle-east-53656220>).

<a id="event-2020-08-04-1-2"></a>

Context: 2020 Beirut explosions.

**Archived source account.** Finnish diplomats confirm that Finland's Embassy in Beirut, located 2km from the port, has been "destroyed". No Finnish casualties are known at this time, according to Deputy Ambassador Aki Kauppinen. Prime Minister Sanna Marin confirmed the embassy premises have been "badly damaged".

Source citations (as archived): [Newsnow Finland](<https://newsnowfinland.fi/finland-international/report-finnish-embassy-in-beirut-destroyed-by-blast>).

<a id="event-2020-08-04-1-3"></a>

**Archived source account.** Heavy rains cause floods and landslides in Gapyeong, South Korea, killing at least 14 people and forcing the evacuation of more than 1,000. The rains have also battered China, Thailand, India and Myanmar. Neighboring North Korea warns of possible floods, while the New Zealand government reports the deaths of three of its citizens in the South Korean floods.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-southkorea-floods/south-korea-floods-landslides-kill-14-idUSKCN2500AZ?il=0>).

<a id="event-2020-08-04-1-4"></a>

**Archived source account.** Searchers have located the United States Marine Corps Assault Amphibious Vehicle that sank near San Clemente Island, off the coast of Southern California, on 30 July 2020. Eight Marines and one sailor of the 15th Marine Expeditionary Unit from Marine Corps Base Camp Pendleton, San Diego County died in the "ship-to-shore" training exercise. Recovery efforts will begin by the end of the week.

Source citations (as archived): [NBC San Diego](<https://www.nbcsandiego.com/news/local/marine-corps-finds-sunken-aav-remains-of-troops-killed-in-southern-california-training-mishap/2378800/>).

<a id="event-2020-08-04-2-2"></a>

Context: COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in the Philippines.

**Archived source account.** The Philippines posts a single-day Southeast Asian record, with 6,352 new COVID-19 cases reported in the last 24 hours, as well as 11 deaths. More than 66,000 people have recovered.

<a id="event-2020-08-04-3-0"></a>

Former Liberian President Ellen Johnson Sirleaf posted a tweet in favor of the opposition.

<a id="event-2020-08-05-5-1"></a>

Context: 2020 Sri Lankan parliamentary election.

**Archived source account.** Sri Lanka holds parliamentary elections after the parliament was dissolved by president Gotabaya Rajapaksa in March. Originally scheduled to be held in April, the election was postponed twice due to the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic.

Source citations (as archived): [The Guardian](<https://www.theguardian.com/world/2020/aug/05/sri-lanka-election-vote-coronavirus-rajapaksa>).

<a id="event-2020-08-05-5-3"></a>

Context: Croatia–Serbia relations.

**Archived source account.** Croatia marks the 25th anniversary of Operation Storm, a military victory against the proto-state of Serbian Krajina that ended the Croatian War of Independence. The ceremony in the town of Knin, former capital of Serbian Krajina, was for the first time ever attended by an ethnic Serb political representative, Deputy Prime Minister Boris Milošević.

Source citations (as archived): [Al Jazeera](<https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/08/croatia-marks-25-years-war-tolerance-message-200805085400673.html>).

<a id="event-2020-08-05-5-5"></a>

Context: Taiwan–United States relations, China–United States relations.

**Archived source account.** United States Secretary of Health and Human Services Alex Azar travels to Taiwan for a multi-day official visit. He is the highest-ranking U.S. official to visit the country in 40 years after the U.S. stopped recognising Taiwan in 1979 and has had unofficial ties since then. The PRC, which claims Taiwan as a breakaway province, condemns the visit.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-taiwan-usa/u-s-health-chief-to-be-highest-ranking-official-in-decades-to-visit-taiwan-angering-china-idUSKCN25105B?feedType=mktg&amp;feedName=healthNews&amp;WT.mc_id=Partner-Google>).

<a id="event-2020-08-05-5-6"></a>

**Archived source account.** Vanuatu's former prime minister, Charlot Salwai, is referred to the Supreme Court to stand trial for alleged corruption. His lawyer says he is confident they will win the case.

Source citations (as archived): [RNZ](<https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/422849/former-vanuatu-pm-confident-of-beating-corruption-charges>).

#### Science and technology

<a id="event-2020-08-05-6-1"></a>

Context: Artemis program.

**Archived source account.** SpaceX Starship prototype SN5 successfully carries out a 150 m flight test at the SpaceX South Texas Launch Site.

Source citations (as archived): [BBC News](<https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/science-environment-53659702>).

<a id="event-2020-08-05-6-2"></a>

**Archived source account.** Google shuts down 2,500 channels on its video sharing platform YouTube that were linked to Chinese disinformation. The channels generally posted "spammy, non-political content", but a small subset touched on politics, the company said.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-cyber-google-disinformation/google-pulls-2500-china-linked-youtube-channels-over-disinformation-idUSKCN251384?il=0>).

Source citations (as archived): [UConn Huskies](<https://uconnhuskies.com/news/2020/8/5/uconn-football-announces-cancellation-of-2020-season-due-to-risks-associated-with-covid-19.aspx>); [ESPN](<https://www.espn.com/college-football/story/_/id/29600577/uconn-becomes-1st-fbs-team-cancel-football-season-due-coronavirus>).

[Pinned Wikipedia revision 1273224829](<https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Portal%3ACurrent%20events%2F2020%20August%206&oldid=1273224829>).

#### Armed conflicts and attacks

<a id="event-2020-08-06-0-1"></a>

Context: Saudi Arabian-led intervention in Yemen, Saudi Arabian–Yemeni border conflict.

**Archived source account.** Saudi state news agency SPA says Saudi Armed Forces shot down an explosive-laden drone launched against Saudi territory from Al Hudaydah Governorate, on Yemen's Red Sea coast. The Houthis report a Saudi air strike on Saada Governorate.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-yemen-security-saudi/saudi-coalition-says-it-shot-down-houthi-drone-heading-for-kingdom-idUSKCN2521FX>).

#### Business and economy

<a id="event-2020-08-06-1-1"></a>

Context: Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic.

**Archived source account.** The Philippine economy falls into recession for the first time in 29 years after the economy shrank by 16.5% in the April to June quarter from the same period last year, which is the biggest slump in the government's quarterly GDP data dating back to 1981.

Source citations (as archived): [CNA](<https://www.channelnewsasia.com/news/business/philippine-economy-dives-into-recession-in-worst-slump-on-record-12994870>).

<a id="event-2020-08-06-1-3"></a>

Context: China–United States trade war.

**Archived source account.** Invoking the International Emergency Economic Powers Act, U.S. President Donald Trump issues several executive orders barring firms and American citizens from trading and doing financial transactions with Chinese technology companies ByteDance and Tencent, effectively banning their respective apps TikTok and WeChat within the United States. The orders are set to go into effect in 45 days.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://uk.reuters.com/article/us-usa-wechat-trump/trump-issues-bans-on-chinas-tiktok-wechat-stoking-tension-with-beijing-idUKKCN25304R>).

<a id="event-2020-08-06-1-5"></a>

Context: Trump tariffs.

**Archived source account.** Trump implements a tariff of 10% on aluminum imports from Canada, pursuant to Section 232 of the US Trade Expansion Act. The United States previously imposed tariffs on Canadian steel and aluminum in 2018 citing national security concerns, before removing them last year as part of the USCMA Free Trade Agreement. Prime Minister of Canada Justin Trudeau vows "dollar-for-dollar" countermeasures.

Source citations (as archived): [CBC](<https://www.cbc.ca/news/business/trump-aluminum-tariff-1.5677036>).

#### Disasters and accidents

<a id="event-2020-08-06-2-1"></a>

Context: 2020 Beirut explosions, 2019–2020 Lebanese protests.

**Archived source account.** Security forces fired tear gas to disperse dozens of anti-government protesters in Beirut calling for the Lebanese government's resignation near the parliament building. Several people were wounded in the clashes.

Source citations (as archived): [Al Jazeera](<https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/08/lebanon-orders-house-arrest-officials-beirut-blast-live-200805230752876.html>).

Context: COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in Europe / COVID-19 pandemic in Germany.

Context: Belarus–United States relations, 2020 Belarusian presidential election.

**Archived source account.** Belarusian President Alexander Lukashenko says security forces have arrested "a number of" U.S. citizens, just days before the country goes to the polls for a presidential election. In the speech, Lukashenko claims Belarus is the victim of a "hybrid war", and that "we should expect dirty tricks from any side".

Source citations (as archived): [Ekathimerini](<https://www.ekathimerini.com/255573/gallery/ekathimerini/news/greece-and-egypt-sign-agreement-on-exclusive-economic-zone>); [Anadolu Agency](<https://www.aa.com.tr/en/europe/greece-egypt-violate-turkeys-libyas-rights/1934121>).

#### Law and crime

<a id="event-2020-08-06-5-1"></a>

Context: Canada–China relations.

**Archived source account.** A court in China sentences a Canadian man to death on drug charges. His alleged accomplice receives life imprisonment. Police had confiscated 120 kilograms (266 pounds) of ketamine from the defendant's home. He is the third Canadian citizen to receive the death sentence for drug smuggling since Canadian authorities arrested Huawei executive Meng Wanzhou in late 2018 on an extradition request from the United States.

Source citations (as archived): [AP](<https://apnews.com/7569c5df2c3f32f92e57a7771cef660a>).

<a id="event-2020-08-06-5-2"></a>

Source citations (as archived): [BBC News](<https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-northern-ireland-53686763>).

<a id="event-2020-08-06-5-3"></a>

**Archived source account.** Former Saudi Ministry of the Interior official Saad bin Khalid Al Jabry accuses Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman of attempting to assassinate him in Canada, where he currently lives in exile, two weeks after the assassination of dissident journalist Jamal Khashoggi. The would-be assassins, believed to be the Tiger Squad, were stopped at Toronto Pearson International Airport after Canadian border officials became suspicious of them following interviews.

Source citations (as archived): [BBC News](<https://www.bbc.com/news/world-middle-east-53677869>).

#### Armed conflicts and attacks

<a id="event-2020-08-08-0-2"></a>

Context: Somali Civil War / 2020 Mogadishu army base bombing.

**Archived source account.** A suicide bombing at a military base in Mogadishu kills at least eight people and injures fourteen others. Jihadist group al-Shabaab claims responsibility.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-somalia-blast/blast-rocks-military-base-in-somali-capital-at-least-eight-dead-idUSKCN2540E4>).

<a id="event-2020-08-08-0-4"></a>

Context: 2019–2020 Lebanese protests, aftermath of the 2020 Beirut explosions.

**Archived source account.** Riot police fire tear gas at protesters trying to make their way into parliament, amid increasing anger at the government's handling of this week's explosions in Beirut and deteriorating economic situation in the country. More than 728 people were wounded in the clashes, sixty-three of whom were taken to hospitals, while a policeman was killed.

#### Armed conflicts and attacks

Afghan President Ashraf Ghani says he will sign the order and that doing this, the Afghan government complies with the Taliban demand of freeing prisoners to start intra-Afghan peace talks.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-afghanistan-taliban/afghanistan-to-release-400-hard-core-taliban-to-start-peace-talks-idUSKCN25507I>).

Nasser. The company plans to uphold its promise of paying out US$75 billion in annual dividends in spite of this.

#### Politics and elections

<a id="event-2020-08-09-5-1"></a>

Context: 2020 Belarusian presidential election, 2020 Belarusian protests.

**Archived source account.** Citizens of Belarus head to the polls to elect the country's president. Long-ruling Alexander Lukashenko is challenged by Sviatlana Tsikhanouskaya after her husband and pro-democracy activist Siarhei Tsikhanouski was jailed and banned from the vote like other prominent opposition figures. Protesters and journalists were also detained in the weeks leading to the election.

Source citations (as archived): [DW](<https://www.dw.com/en/belarus-heads-to-polls-to-elect-next-president/a-54500994>).

<a id="event-2020-08-09-5-2"></a>

Context: 2020 Belarusian presidential election, 2020 Belarusian protests.

**Archived source account.** A state television exit poll shows President Alexander Lukashenko winning 79.7% of the vote. These results have been dismissed by the main opposition candidate Sviatlana Tsikhanouskaya, who criticized them has "massively rigged".

Source citations (as archived): [BBC News](<https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-europe-53707011>); [The Guardian](<https://www.theguardian.com/world/2020/aug/10/belarus-opposition-candidate-rejects-election-result-protests-svetlana-tikhanovskaya-lukashenko>).

<a id="event-2020-08-09-5-3"></a>

Context: 2020 Belarusian presidential election, 2020 Belarusian protests.

**Archived source account.** Lukashenko, in power since 1994, declares a landslide victory against the opposition, as riot police clash with protesters in the capital Minsk. Protests in reaction to the disputed results have been reported in at least 20 other Belarusian cities. Fifty civilians and thirty-nine police officers were injured, while at least 3,000 protesters are arrested across the country, one-third of them in Minsk.

Source citations (as archived): [BBC News](<https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-53717834>); [The Guardian](<https://www.theguardian.com/world/2020/aug/09/belarus-election-lukashenko-landslide-victory-fixing-claims>).

Context: 2020 Belarusian presidential election, 2020 Belarusian protests.

<a id="event-2020-08-10-2-1"></a>

Jugnauth adds the nation lacks the skills and resources needed to relocate the wrecked vessel, and that the nation will likely never recover from the ecological damage done by the spill.

Source citations (as archived): [BBC News](<https://www.bbc.com/news/world-africa-53722701>); [CBS](<https://www.cbsnews.com/news/mauritius-oil-spill-disaster-satellite-images/>).

Context: 2020 Volgograd explosion.

Source citations (as archived): [The Independent](<https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/europe/russia-explosion-volgograd-today-blast-injuries-gas-station-a9663636.html>).

<a id="event-2020-08-10-2-6"></a>

**Archived source account.** A gas explosion in Baltimore, Maryland, United States, leaves at least one dead and four injured. Homes were damaged or destroyed.

<a id="event-2020-08-10-2-8"></a>

Context: August 2020 Midwest derecho.

**Editorial account; source review complete.** National Weather Service accounts date the Midwest derecho to August 10, 2020, identify four deaths, and give a later estimated cost above USD 11 billion. The Des Moines account records a 104 mph instantaneous wind measurement. The damage total is retrospective and approximate, rather than a final same-day tally.

Editorial date: 2020-08-10. Checked: 2026-10-21. Complete wording review: preserve the archived rounded figure while distinguishing a later estimate and an instantaneous wind reading.

Evidence: [National Weather Service Indianapolis](<https://www.weather.gov/ind/2020derechoanniv>); [National Weather Service Des Moines](<https://www.weather.gov/dmx/2020derecho>).

Original source account: A powerful derecho with winds over 100 mph sweeps across the Midwestern United States and leaves four dead and causes $11 billion USD in damage.

The original source entry had no attached citation; independent evidence is supplied above.

Source citations (as archived): [BBC News](<https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-politics-53773914>).

<a id="event-2020-08-13-3-5"></a>

Context: Travel restrictions related to the COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in Europe / COVID-19 pandemic in Italy.

**Archived source account.** Italian Health Minister Roberto Speranza signs an order requiring anyone arriving from Croatia, Greece, Spain, and Malta to be tested for COVID-19 in an attempt to avoid a spike of new cases in the country. The country is also banning travellers from Colombia over concerns of new infections.

Source citations (as archived): [Swiss Info](<https://www.swissinfo.ch/eng/italy-orders-covid-tests-on-travellers-from-greece--spain--croatia--malta/45964418>); [Euronews](<https://www.euronews.com/2020/08/13/italy-introduces-mandatory-covid-19-testing-for-tourists-returning-from-summer-holidays>).

<a id="event-2020-08-13-3-7"></a>

Context: Iran–Saudi Arabia relations.

**Archived source account.** The Saudi ambassador to the United Nations, Abdul Aziz al-Wasel, calls for an extension of the arms embargo on Iran saying that Iran "smuggles weapons to militias to disturb the peace in the Middle East".

Source citations (as archived): [Al Arabiya](<https://english.alarabiya.net/en/News/gulf/2020/08/13/Saudi-Arabian-ambassador-to-Switzerland-calls-for-Iran-arms-embargo-extension.html>).

<a id="event-2020-08-13-3-9"></a>

Context: Hezbollah foreign relations.

**Archived source account.** Lithuania labels Hezbollah a terrorist organization and bans its members from entering the country, according to a statement by the office of the foreign minister.

Source citations (as archived): [Al Arabiya](<https://english.alarabiya.net/en/News/middle-east/2020/08/13/Lithuania-recognizes-Hezbollah-as-terrorist-organization-after-Beirut-explosion.html>).

<a id="event-2020-08-13-3-11"></a>

Context: Greek–Turkish relations.

**Archived source account.** France deploys two Dassault Rafale fighter jets and the frigate La Fayette to the eastern Mediterranean because of tensions between Greece and Turkey over oil and gas exploration in disputed waters. French President Emmanuel Macron says the French military will monitor the situation.

Source citations (as archived): [BBC News](<https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-53767792>).

<a id="event-2020-08-13-3-13"></a>

Context: Foreign relations of Israel, Arab–Israeli peace projects.

**Archived source account.** The United States, Israel and the United Arab Emirates announce in a joint statement that Israel and the UAE will establish normalized diplomatic relations, in exchange for Israeli suspension of plans to annex occupied West Bank territory.

Source citations (as archived): [BBC News](<https://www.bbc.com/news/world-middle-east-53770859>).

#### Law and crime

<a id="event-2020-08-13-4-2"></a>

Context: Face masks during the COVID-19 pandemic in the United States / COVID-19 pandemic in Georgia.

**Archived source account.** Georgia Governor Brian Kemp drops his lawsuit against Atlanta Mayor Keisha Lance Bottoms over the city's mask mandate.

Source citations (as archived): [ABC News](<https://abcnews.go.com/Health/wireStory/georgia-governor-drop-lawsuit-atlanta-mask-mandate-72355332>).

#### Politics and elections

<a id="event-2020-08-13-5-1"></a>

Context: 2020 Belarusian protests.

**Archived source account.** A 25-year-old man from the city of Gomel becomes the second protester killed since protests in Belarus against the government began. He died while in police custody, according to his family.

Source citations (as archived): [The Guardian](<https://www.theguardian.com/world/2020/aug/13/belarus-protests-25-year-old-man-dies-in-police-custody-alexander-vikhor>).

<a id="event-2020-08-13-5-2"></a>

Context: 2020 Belarusian protests.

**Archived source account.** The UN High Commissioner for Human Rights Michelle Bachelet condemns the use of violence by Belarusian authorities against protesters, and calls for the release of all political prisoners in the country.

Source citations (as archived): [BBC News](<https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-europe-53760453>).

<a id="event-2020-08-13-5-3"></a>

Context: 2020 Belarusian protests.

**Archived source account.** Belarusian women form human chains to condemn a crackdown on protests over the disputed election.

Source citations (as archived): [BBC News](<https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-53761747>).

<a id="event-2020-08-13-5-4"></a>

Context: 2020 Belarusian protests.

**Archived source account.** Factory workers from state-run factories joined the protest. Tens of thousands of people protested for the fifth day in a row against the election results. The protesters marched through Minsk and formed human chains.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-belarus-election/go-away-state-factory-workers-join-protests-against-belarus-president-idUSKCN25925Z?feedType=mktg&amp;feedName=topNews&amp;WT.mc_id=Partner-Google>).

<a id="event-2020-08-13-5-6"></a>

Context: 2019–2020 Lebanese protests, aftermath of the 2020 Beirut explosions.

**Archived source account.** Parliament approves a state of emergency in Beirut and grants the military sweeping powers, such as declaring curfews, preventing public gatherings and censoring the media, as well as referring civilians to military courts over alleged security breaches. Human rights groups criticize the decision.

Source citations (as archived): [AP](<https://apnews.com/4434959ad39d1f2f189eb6442d590930>).

<a id="event-2020-08-13-5-8"></a>

Context: 2020 Bolivian general election.

**Archived source account.** The interim government of Bolivia confirms that the elections will be held on October 18. Anyone who tries to change the date may face penalties. Opposition parties called to have the elections sooner after the elections earlier this year were postponed because of COVID-19. Protesters have blocked streets and protested calling for the elections to take place sooner, after it was announced in July. The European Union and United Nations support the new election date.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-bolivia-election-protest/bolivia-confirms-presidential-election-for-october-18-despite-calls-for-earlier-date-idUSKCN25A015>).

<a id="event-2020-08-13-5-10"></a>

Context: Politics of North Korea.

**Archived source account.** Kim Tok-hun is named the new Premier, succeeding Kim Jae-ryong.

Source citations (as archived): [Shine](<https://www.shine.cn/news/world/2008144147/>).

### 2020-08-14

[Pinned Wikipedia revision 1083337183](<https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Portal%3ACurrent%20events%2F2020%20August%2014&oldid=1083337183>).

#### Armed conflicts and attacks

<a id="event-2020-08-14-0-1"></a>

Context: Insurgency in Jammu and Kashmir, Revocation of the special status of Jammu and Kashmir.

**Archived source account.** Islamist insurgents kill at least two police officers and injured another in Srinagar, Jammu and Kashmir, India. The attack comes days after the first anniversary of the revocation of Kashmir’s constitutional autonomy.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-india-kashmir/militants-kill-two-police-in-kashmir-ahead-of-indias-independence-day-idUSKCN25A0R3>).

<a id="event-2020-08-14-0-3"></a>

Context: Moro conflict.

**Archived source account.** Moro National Liberation Front chairman Nur Misuari surrenders Abduljihad Susukan, a sub-commander of the ISIL-affiliated Abu Sayyaf militant group, to the Philippine National Police in Davao City, following the latter's involvement in the 2015 Roseller Lim and Samal Island kidnappings and beheadings. Susukan surrendered to Misuari in April 2020.

Source citations (as archived): [AP](<https://www.cbc.ca/news/world/militant-linked-beheading-canadians-surrenders-philippines-1.5686159>).

#### Arts and culture

<a id="event-2020-08-14-1-2"></a>

Context: Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on the arts and cultural heritage / COVID-19 pandemic in the United States, COVID-19 pandemic in New York City.

**Archived source account.** New York Governor Andrew Cuomo says that museums and cultural institutions in New York City will be allowed to reopen on August 24 at a 25% capacity.

Source citations (as archived): [The New York Times](<https://www.nytimes.com/2020/08/14/arts/design/nyc-museums-reopening-virus.html>).

#### Disasters and accidents

<a id="event-2020-08-14-2-2"></a>

Context: 2020 wildfire season / 2020 California wildfires.

**Archived source account.** The Lake Fire in Santa Clarita and Palmdale grows to over 10,000 acres, prompting evacuations in the Lake Hughes area.

Source citations (as archived): [CBS News](<https://www.cbsnews.com/news/lake-fire-california-north-los-angeles-evacuation-orders/>).

#### Health and environment

<a id="event-2020-08-14-3-3"></a>

Context: COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in Europe / COVID-19 pandemic in France.

**Archived source account.** France reports 2,846 new COVID-19 cases in the last 24 hours, as well as more than 12,300 new cases this week, making it the highest number of cases since the lockdown was eased in May.

Source citations (as archived): [The New York Times](<https://www.nytimes.com/reuters/2020/08/14/world/europe/14reuters-health-coronavirus-france-casualties.html>); [The Telegraph](<https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/2020/08/14/second-wave-looms-france-reports-12000-new-coronavirus-cases/>).

<a id="event-2020-08-14-3-4"></a>

Context: COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in Europe / COVID-19 pandemic in France.

**Archived source account.** The government declares Paris and Marseilles as "active zones", or high-risk zones. The move allows local authorities in those designated areas to impose restrictions.

Source citations (as archived): [DW](<https://www.dw.com/en/coronavirus-france-declares-paris-marseille-high-risk-zones/a-54565032>).

<a id="event-2020-08-14-3-6"></a>

Context: COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in Europe / COVID-19 pandemic in Spain.

**Archived source account.** Amid an alarming increase in COVID-19 cases, the government of Spain closes all nightclubs and bans smoking in public sites in the event that the social distancing is not assured.

Source citations (as archived): [CBS News](<https://www.cbsnews.com/news/coronavirus-spain-bans-public-smoking-closes-discos-france-eyes-restric>); [Politico](<https://www.politico.eu/article/spain-bans-smoking-shuts-nightclubs-under-new-coronavirus-restrictions/>).

<a id="event-2020-08-14-3-8"></a>

Context: COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in Europe / COVID-19 pandemic in Greece.

**Archived source account.** Greece announces that they would limit public gatherings to 50 people and impose a midnight curfew on bars and restaurants in Athens and other areas. This measure is to last until August 24 in parts of the country where infection numbers have risen.

Source citations (as archived): [Greek Reporter](<https://greece.greekreporter.com/2020/08/14/greece-announces-strict-new-measures-against-coronavirus-pm-admonishes-youth/>).

<a id="event-2020-08-14-3-10"></a>

Context: COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in New Zealand.

**Archived source account.** Prime Minister Jacinda Ardern announces that the current Alert Level settings will be extended for another 12 days.

Source citations (as archived): [Newshub](<https://www.newshub.co.nz/home/new-zealand/2020/08/coronavirus-jacinda-ardern-extends-auckland-s-lockdown-rest-of-new-zealand-at-alert-level-2.html>).

<a id="event-2020-08-14-3-12"></a>

Context: COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in the Philippines.

**Archived source account.** Education Secretary Leonor Briones suspends the commencement of the 2020–21 academic year for primary and secondary schools until October 5 due to the continuous rise of cases in the country.

Source citations (as archived): [Kyodo News](<https://mainichi.jp/english/articles/20200814/p2g/00m/0in/154000c>).

#### International relations

<a id="event-2020-08-14-4-3"></a>

Context: Travel restrictions related to the COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in Europe / COVID-19 pandemic in Germany, COVID-19 pandemic in Spain.

**Archived source account.** Germany declares all of Spain except for the Canary Islands a high risk region following a spike of COVID-19 cases in the country. Designations as risk regions are typically followed by the German Foreign Ministry warning against touristic travel to those areas and mean people returning from those areas face a test or two weeks' compulsory quarantine.

Source citations (as archived): [France 24](<https://www.france24.com/en/20200814-germany-puts-most-of-spain-on-covid-19-quarantine-list>).

<a id="event-2020-08-14-4-5"></a>

Context: Belarus–Lithuania relations, 2020 Belarusian presidential election, 2020 Belarusian protests.

**Archived source account.** Lithuania becomes the first EU state to openly reject the legitimacy of Alexander Lukashenko as President of Belarus. Lithuanian President Gitanas Nausėda says "We can not call Mister Lukashenko legitimate because there were no free democratic elections in Belarus".

Source citations (as archived): [Urdu Point](<https://www.urdupoint.com/en/world/lithuanian-leader-says-lukashenko-lost-legiti-1001348.html>).

<a id="event-2020-08-14-4-7"></a>

Context: Sanctions on Iran.

**Archived source account.** The United Nations Security Council has resoundingly rejected a United States bid to extend a global arms embargo on Iran. In a Security Council vote, United States only got support from the Dominican Republic for its resolution to indefinitely extend the arms embargo on Iran, leaving it far short of the minimum nine "yes" votes required for adoption. Eleven members on the 15-member body, including France, Germany and the United Kingdom, abstained while Russia and China opposed extending the ban but did not need to use their vetoes.

Source citations (as archived): [Al Jazeera](<https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/08/fail-loses-bid-extend-arms-embargo-iran-200815010505938.html>); [The Guardian](<https://www.theguardian.com/world/2020/aug/14/us-iran-un-arms-embargo-nuclear-deal>).

#### Law and crime

<a id="event-2020-08-14-5-1"></a>

Context: 2020 Belarusian protests.

**Archived source account.** Amnesty International says "widespread torture" is taking place inside detention centres in Belarus, with more than 6,700 people detained since protests against Lukashenko broke out following the disputed presidential election result. Amnesty International says detainees described being stripped naked, beaten and threatened with rape. The BBC also reports evidence of torture, including at the Okrestina detention centre in Minsk.

Source citations (as archived): [CNN](<https://edition.cnn.com/2020/08/14/europe/belarus-torture-allegations-intl-hnk/index.html>); [BBC News](<https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-europe-53773534>).

<a id="event-2020-08-14-5-3"></a>

Context: 2020 Thai protests.

**Archived source account.** Thai police arrest a student leader over an anti-government protest last month. The student was arrested in the outskirts of Bangkok while traveling to a protest. Human Rights Watch reports that he will be charged with breaching multiple laws. Police declined to comment when contacted by Reuters.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-thailand-protests/thai-police-arrest-another-leader-of-student-protests-rights-group-says-idUSKCN25A1HQ?il=0>).

<a id="event-2020-08-14-5-4"></a>

**Archived source account.** The United States Department of Justice says Yale University is illegally discriminating against White Americans and Asian Americans in its undergraduate admissions process, following a two-year investigation into the university. A Yale spokeswoman "categorically" denies the federal accusations.

Source citations (as archived): [BBC News](<https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-us-canada-53774075>).

#### Politics and elections

<a id="event-2020-08-14-6-1"></a>

Context: 2020 Bulgarian protests.

**Archived source account.** Prime Minister Boyko Borisov pledges to resign if the nation's National Assembly passes his motion to call for a constituent assembly to change the nation's constitution.

Source citations (as archived): [The New York Times](<https://www.nytimes.com/reuters/2020/08/14/world/europe/14reuters-bulgaria-constitution.html>).

<a id="event-2020-08-14-6-3"></a>

Context: Politics of Equatorial Guinea.

**Archived source account.** Prime Minister Francisco Pascual Obama Asue presents his resignation and that of his entire government without making public the reason. President Teodoro Obiang claims that "he has not met the programmatic objectives, which has undoubtedly caused this crisis situation that today requires us to take urgent measures".

Source citations (as archived): [La Vanguardia](<https://www.lavanguardia.com/internacional/20200814/482809291988/dimite-bloque-gobierno-primer-ministro-guinea-ecuatorial.html>).

#### Sports

<a id="event-2020-08-14-7-1"></a>

Context: 2019–20 UEFA Champions League, FC Barcelona 2–8 FC Bayern Munich.

**Archived source account.** In association football, FC Bayern Munich become the first team to score eight goals in a UEFA Champions League knockout match after doing so against FC Barcelona in a quarter-finals match that ended 8–2. FC Barcelona suffer one of their worst defeats in history, having conceded eight goals for the first time since 1946.

Source citations (as archived): [AP](<https://sports.inquirer.net/401410/rock-bottom-barca-reeling-after-8-2-humiliation-by-bayern>).

### 2020-08-15

[Pinned Wikipedia revision 1167489256](<https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Portal%3ACurrent%20events%2F2020%20August%2015&oldid=1167489256>).

#### Business and economy

<a id="event-2020-08-15-0-1"></a>

Context: Argentine debt restructuring.

**Archived source account.** The government approves a proposed deal with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) to restructure around $65 billion in foreign government bonds, following President Alberto Fernández's successful negotiations with creditors and the International Monetary Fund the previous week after the country defaulted in May. The government plans to submit the proposal to the SEC on August 17.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-argentina-debt-proposal/argentina-approves-revised-debt-offer-set-for-sec-filing-idUSKCN25C04M>).

<a id="event-2020-08-15-0-3"></a>

Context: COVID-19 pandemic in Europe.

**Archived source account.** The MSC Grandiosa disembarks from Genoa, Italy, on a seven-day cruise in the Mediterranean Sea, the first major cruise ship to sail in the Sea in almost five months because of the COVID-19 pandemic.

Source citations (as archived): [BBC News](<https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-53802045>).

#### Disasters and accidents

<a id="event-2020-08-15-1-1"></a>

Context: MV Wakashio oil spill.

**Archived source account.** The Japanese bulk carrier Wakashio, which stranded on a reef in Mauritius last month, breaks in half. Approximately 1,000 tonnes of oil spilled into the ocean. Most of the oil had been pumped out before the ship broke in half in the afternoon. Around 166 tonnes of oil remained after the break, and authorities are working to remove it. Scientists call it the biggest environmental disaster ever in Mauritius. France says it will help with the cleanup. Japan's ministry of environment announced that it will send officials and other specialists to look at the damage.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-mauritius-environment-japan/japanese-ship-involved-in-mauritius-oil-spill-breaks-apart-idUSKCN25B09K>).

<a id="event-2020-08-15-1-2"></a>

**Archived source account.** Two lighter vessels capsize in the Bay of Bengal, near the island of Bhasan Char in Bangladesh. The country's Inland Water Transport Authority report that 13 crew members from one vessel en route to the Narayanganj District from Chittagong are missing, while all 12 crew members from the other vessel were rescued.

Source citations (as archived): [Anadolu Agency](<https://www.aa.com.tr/en/asia-pacific/bangladesh-13-missing-12-rescued-as-vessels-capsize/1943371>).

#### Health and environment

<a id="event-2020-08-15-2-3"></a>

Context: COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in Europe / COVID-19 pandemic in Denmark.

**Archived source account.** Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen mandates the wearing of face masks on all public transport in the country, effective August 22, in an effort to control the spread of the virus.

Source citations (as archived): [AFP](<https://www.dailysabah.com/world/europe/denmark-makes-masks-compulsory-on-public-transport-as-covid-19-cases-rise>).

<a id="event-2020-08-15-2-5"></a>

Context: COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in Europe / COVID-19 pandemic in France.

**Archived source account.** The daily number of new COVID-19 cases in France tops 3,000 for the first time since lockdown eased.

Source citations (as archived): [France 24](<https://www.france24.com/en/20200815-france-reports-post-lockdown-peak-with-3-310-new-covid-19-cases-in-24-hours>).

<a id="event-2020-08-15-2-7"></a>

Context: COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in Europe / COVID-19 pandemic in Malta.

**Archived source account.** Malta reports 72 new COVID-19 cases in the last 24 hours. It is the highest single increase in new cases in the country since the pandemic began.

Source citations (as archived): [Times of Malta](<https://timesofmalta.com/articles/view/record-number-of-new-covid-19-cases-72-test-positive.812052.amp>).

<a id="event-2020-08-15-2-9"></a>

Context: COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in Europe / COVID-19 pandemic in the Republic of Ireland.

**Archived source account.** Ireland reports 200 new cases but no deaths in the last 24 hours. This is the highest number of daily cases since May.

Source citations (as archived): [The Irish Times](<https://www.irishtimes.com/news/ireland/irish-news/coronavirus-200-new-cases-reported-in-largest-daily-total-since-may-1.4331414>).

<a id="event-2020-08-15-2-11"></a>

Context: COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in Europe / COVID-19 pandemic in Russia, COVID-19 vaccine.

**Archived source account.** Russia announces the production of the first batch of its Sputnik V vaccine.

Source citations (as archived): [Hindustan Times](<https://www.hindustantimes.com/world-news/russia-produces-first-batch-of-covid-19-vaccine-sputnik-v-report/story-4Xj57TsCDanapDJ1vhbacI.html>).

<a id="event-2020-08-15-2-14"></a>

Context: COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in Asia / COVID-19 pandemic in South Korea.

**Archived source account.** South Korea reports 166 new cases of COVID-19. From that number, 139 were traced to Seoul and Gyeonggi Province and a significant portion of them were linked to cluster infections involving churchgoers. It is the highest number of reported new cases since March 11.

Source citations (as archived): [Kyodo News](<https://english.kyodonews.net/news/2020/08/6ff6f6d2d075-s-korea-reports-166-new-coronavirus-cases-biggest-rise-since-march.html>).

<a id="event-2020-08-15-2-15"></a>

Context: COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in Asia / COVID-19 pandemic in South Korea.

**Archived source account.** After a spike in new cases, the government decides to tighten social distancing measures in Seoul and surrounding areas. Many measures that are to be implemented include restricting numbers of gatherings and sports events played behind closed doors.

<a id="event-2020-08-15-2-17"></a>

Context: COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in Asia / COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia.

**Archived source account.** Minister of State Owned Enterprises and chief of the COVID-19 recovery team, Erick Thohir, announces that the government would bar foreign visitors until the completion of a vaccine. Indonesian scientists are testing a COVID-19 vaccine with Sinovac Biotech, which Thohir says is likely to be completed next year.

Source citations (as archived): [Kyodo News](<https://english.kyodonews.net/news/2020/08/caf0d420850f-indonesia-to-close-doors-to-foreign-tourists-until-vaccine-found.html>).

<a id="event-2020-08-15-2-20"></a>

Context: COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in Africa / COVID-19 pandemic in Algeria.

**Archived source account.** Algeria begins to reopen their mosques, beaches, cafes, and parks five months after their lockdown.

Source citations (as archived): [ABC News](<https://abcnews.go.com/Health/wireStory/algeria-reopens-mosques-beaches-month-lockdown-72394752>).

<a id="event-2020-08-15-2-22"></a>

Context: COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in Africa / COVID-19 pandemic in South Africa.

**Archived source account.** President Cyril Ramaphosa announces a plan to ease nearly all restrictions on the economy from August 17, including lifting a controversial ban on the sale of alcohol and tobacco that had been imposed in July, as infections peak.

Source citations (as archived): [BBC News](<https://www.bbc.com/news/world-africa-53795339>).

#### International relations

<a id="event-2020-08-15-3-2"></a>

Context: Travel restrictions related to the COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in the Netherlands.

**Archived source account.** The government of the Netherlands issues a travel warning advising the public not to travel to some places, including Paris, the region surrounding Marseilles, Brussels, Ibiza and Mallorca. The warnings come as a response to an increase in new cases in Spain, France and Belgium.

Source citations (as archived): [NL Times](<https://nltimes.nl/2020/08/15/new-travel-warnings-brussels-ibiza-madrid-paris-report>).

<a id="event-2020-08-15-3-4"></a>

Context: Aftermath of the 2020 Belarusian presidential election.

**Archived source account.** The leaders of the Baltic states, Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania, issue a joint statement calling on Belarus to hold a new "free and fair" election with international observers.

Source citations (as archived): [RFE/RL](<https://www.rferl.org/a/baltic-states-urge-new-election-in-belarus-call-for-eu-sanctions/30785103.html>).

<a id="event-2020-08-15-3-6"></a>

Context: Poland–United States relations.

**Archived source account.** U.S. Secretary of State Mike Pompeo and Polish Defence Minister Mariusz Błaszczak sign an agreement in Warsaw to redeploy about 1,000 U.S. troops from Germany to Poland so as to bring the total to 5,500. The agreement also includes a potential increase to 20,000 U.S. troops if Poland is under threat.

Source citations (as archived): [BBC News](<https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-europe-53792019>).

<a id="event-2020-08-15-3-8"></a>

Context: Israel and the United Nations.

**Archived source account.** Israeli Foreign Minister Gabi Ashkenazi condemns the UN Security Council's decision not to extend an arms embargo on Iran. Ashkenazi argues that Iran "will lead to further Middle East instability".

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-usa-iran-un-israel/israel-condemns-u-n-decision-not-to-extend-iran-arms-embargo-idUSKCN25B0VI?il=0>).

<a id="event-2020-08-15-3-10"></a>

Context: Afghanistan–France relations, Afghan peace process.

**Archived source account.** Amidst the release of "hardcore" Taliban prisoners, the French government asks the Afghan government not to release those involved in the killing of French citizens.

#### Law and crime

<a id="event-2020-08-15-4-2"></a>

Context: George Floyd protests / George Floyd protests in Georgia.

<a id="event-2020-08-15-4-6"></a>

Context: 2020 Thai protests.

**Archived source account.** Student activist Parit Chiwarak is released on bail after being arrested on Friday for co-organising a rally in July. He was charged with violating the COVID-19 measures and breaching internal security. Protests have been taking place in Thailand since July against the government. Parit Chiwarak has said he will continue to protest against the government and for reforms in the Thai monarchy.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-thailand-protests-idUSKCN25B0FI>).

<a id="event-2020-08-15-4-7"></a>

The royal decree was issued to commemorate the birthday of the King, on July 28, to "illustrate the king's clemency". The pair now serve life in prison.

Source citations (as archived): [BBC News](<https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-england-53771925>).

Context: 2020 Belarusian protests.

#### Politics and elections

<a id="event-2020-08-16-4-5"></a>

Context: COVID-19 pandemic / Protests over responses to the COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in Europe / COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom / Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on education.

**Archived source account.** Hundreds of GCE Advanced Level students protest outside the Department for Education headquarters in London demanding for a reassessment of their final-year performance by the Ofqual, which has used an algorithm to assess students' performances in lieu of the exams that were cancelled due to the COVID-19 pandemic. Critics claim the Ofqual's algorithm to be "flawed" as the grades issued differ significantly from those predicted by teachers. Education Secretary Gavin Williamson had issued a statement clarifying that students may use their teacher's predicted grades or results from any trial exam, although the Ofqual issued a separate statement favouring teacher evaluations over trial exams. Students are requesting for an intervention from Prime Minister Boris Johnson.

Source citations (as archived): [AP](<https://www.scmp.com/news/world/europe/article/3097588/british-prime-minister-boris-johnson-under-fire-amid-growing>).

Protesters claim that such restrictions are an attempt by the government to curtail people's freedoms.

The Trump administration has viewed Huawei as "an arm of the Chinese Communist Party's surveillance state."
