<a id="event-2020-08-17-6-8"></a>

Context: 2020 Belarusian protests.

**Archived source account.** Addressing workers at a truck factory, Lukashenko states that there will be no fresh elections "until you kill me", he warns. He urges people to let people who want to work to work amid a general strike. He is booed and jeered by the crowd.

Source citations (as archived): [Sky News](<https://news.sky.com/story/belarus-uk-condemns-appalling-violence-against-protesters-and-does-not-accept-results-of-election-12050864>); [Politico](<https://www.politico.eu/article/belarus-protests-alexander-lukashenko-jeered-by-workers/>).

<a id="event-2020-08-17-6-9"></a>

Context: 2020 Belarusian protests.

**Archived source account.** The Belarusian state media National State Television and Radio Company of Belarus headquarters in Minsk is reportedly emptied after staff members walked out and joined the general strike. State television is still on air but only showing an empty studio with music playing in the background.

Source citations (as archived): [DW](<https://www.dw.com/en/belarus-television-broadcasts-empty-studio-as-state-media-joins-general-strike/a-54593079>).

<a id="event-2020-08-17-6-11"></a>

Context: 2020 United States presidential election.

**Archived source account.** The 2020 Democratic National Convention begins, running until Thursday. Former Vice President Joe Biden and Senator Kamala Harris are expected to be officially nominated for their party's choice for President and Vice President, respectively, in the upcoming election.

Source citations (as archived): [NPR](<https://www.npr.org/2020/08/15/902507449/the-democratic-national-convention-starts-monday-heres-what-you-need-to-know>).

<a id="event-2020-08-17-6-12"></a>

Context: 2020 United States presidential election.

**Archived source account.** In a show of bipartisan support for the Democrats national ticket, four longtime Republicans gave speeches: former Ohio governor John Kasich, former New Jersey governor Christine Whitman, former New York congresswoman Susan Molinari, and Quibi CEO Meg Whitman.

Source citations (as archived): [USA Today](<https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/politics/2020/08/17/dnc-former-republican-governors-and-gop-congresswoman-set-speak-for-biden/5600304002/>).

<a id="event-2020-08-17-6-14"></a>

Context: 2020 United States Postal Service crisis.

**Archived source account.** Congressional Democrats have announced investigations and hearings into allegations of widespread mail delays ahead of the coming 2020 United States presidential election, which many expect will see a surge in mail-in voting due to the ongoing pandemic. House Speaker Nancy Pelosi is calling the House of Representatives back from recess several weeks early in order to consider legislation to address the crisis.

Source citations (as archived): [The Hill](<https://thehill.com/homenews/house/512258-pelosi-calls-for-house-to-return-this-week-over-usps-issues>); [Axios](<https://www.axios.com/pelosi-house-postal-service-bbce98bd-6fe5-4640-995d-6061d4767940.html>).

### 2020-08-18

[Pinned Wikipedia revision 1294856381](<https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Portal%3ACurrent%20events%2F2020%20August%2018&oldid=1294856381>).

#### Armed conflicts and attacks

<a id="event-2020-08-18-0-1"></a>

Context: 2020 Malian protests, 2020 Malian coup d'état.

**Archived source account.** Gunfire and a mutiny take place at a military base in Kati, Koulikoro, Mali. Soldiers arrest senior military officers as the government deploys troops to the area.

Source citations (as archived): [AP](<https://apnews.com/54737684e3e2a84f9b44656de7343e56>).

<a id="event-2020-08-18-0-2"></a>

Context: 2020 Malian protests, 2020 Malian coup d'état.

**Archived source account.** The Office de Radiodiffusion-Télévision du Mali (ORTM) headquarters in the capital Bamako are evacuated amid reports of a coup attempt. The French and Norwegian embassies urge their citizens to remain indoors after being notified of mutiny in the Armed Forces.

Source citations (as archived): [DW](<https://www.dw.com/en/possible-coup-underway-in-mali/a-54608009>).

<a id="event-2020-08-18-0-3"></a>

Context: 2020 Malian protests, 2020 Malian coup d'état.

**Archived source account.** Two security forces later confirm to Reuters that President Ibrahim Boubacar Keïta and Prime Minister Boubou Cissé have been detained by the mutinying forces. The two men are believed to have been transported to Kati.

Source citations (as archived): [France 24](<https://www.france24.com/en/20200818-ecowas-calls-on-mali-soldiers-to-end-the-mutiny>); [Anadolu Agency](<https://www.aa.com.tr/en/africa/gunshots-heard-at-military-camp-near-mali-capital/1945667>); [Al Jazeera](<https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/08/gunfire-heard-mali-army-base-warnings-mutiny-200818111723901.html>).

<a id="event-2020-08-18-0-4"></a>

Context: 2020 Malian protests, 2020 Malian coup d'état.

**Archived source account.** Bamako and the Presidential Palace is reportedly under the control of coup forces with tanks and other military vehicles on the streets. Anti-government protesters set fire to a Ministry of Justice building, while hundreds of opposition supporters gather on the streets to celebrate the coup.

Source citations (as archived): [BBC News](<https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-africa-53825673>).

<a id="event-2020-08-18-0-5"></a>

Context: 2020 Malian protests, 2020 Malian coup d'état.

**Archived source account.** The European Union's High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy Josep Borrell condemns the attempted coup, rejecting any anticonstitutional change and calls for dialogue. He also announces that contacts are being made to decide the international community's response.

Source citations (as archived): [European Union](<https://eeas.europa.eu/headquarters/headquarters-homepage/84191/mali-d%C3%A9claration-du-haut-repr%C3%A9sentantvice-president-josep-borrell-sur-la-tentative-de-coup-d_fr>).

<a id="event-2020-08-18-0-7"></a>

Context: Islamic terrorism in Europe; Terrorism in Germany.

**Archived source account.** Three motorcyclists are rammed and left seriously wounded on a motorway in Berlin, Germany during a vehicle-ramming attack. The perpetrator is arrested and identified as an Islamic extremist.

Source citations (as archived): [BBC News](<https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-53832113>).

<a id="event-2020-08-18-0-10"></a>

Context: War in Afghanistan / August 2020 Afghanistan attacks.

**Archived source account.** 14 rockets strike Kabul, wounding ten people. The rockets mostly struck the diplomatic "Green Zone", which is home to several embassies and the NATO Resolute Support headquarters. Two suspects were arrested in connection with the attack, which the Taliban has denied responsibility for.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://uk.reuters.com/article/uk-afghanistan-attack/rocket-attack-in-kabul-wounds-at-least-10-triggers-embassy-lockdowns-idUKKCN25E0HV>).

<a id="event-2020-08-18-0-12"></a>

Context: Russian military intervention in the Syrian Civil War.

**Archived source account.** A Russian major general is killed and two others are injured by a roadside bomb in Syria while en route to Hmeimim Air Base from Deir ez-Zor.

Source citations (as archived): [Anadolu Agency](<https://www.aa.com.tr/en/middle-east/russian-major-general-killed-in-explosion-in-syria/1945894>).

#### Disasters and accidents

<a id="event-2020-08-18-1-1"></a>

Context: 2020 California wildfires.

**Archived source account.** California Governor Gavin Newsom declares a state of emergency to ensure the state receives vital resources as at least 27 wildfires are raging across the state, exacerbating a stifling heat wave.

Source citations (as archived): [NBC News](<https://www.msn.com/en-us/news/weather/california-declares-state-of-emergency-as-it-fights-fires-extreme-weather/ar-BB187s7o?ocid=msedgdhp>).

<a id="event-2020-08-18-1-3"></a>

Context: 2020 Masbate earthquake.

**Archived source account.** A 6.6-magnitude earthquake hits Cataingan, Masbate, Philippines, with at least one person reported to have been killed.

Source citations (as archived): [The Independent](<https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/asia/philippines-earthquake-today-masbate-cataingan-death-toll-a9675236.html>).

#### Health and environment

<a id="event-2020-08-18-2-3"></a>

Context: COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in Europe / COVID-19 pandemic in France.

**Archived source account.** France is slated to make face masks mandatory for all shared spaces in offices and factories where there is more than one employee present. The measure is set to begin on September 1.

Source citations (as archived): [BBC News](<https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-53817383>).

<a id="event-2020-08-18-2-5"></a>

Context: COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in Europe / COVID-19 pandemic in Germany.

**Archived source account.** Chancellor Angela Merkel rules out easing further COVID-19-related public health restrictions amidst a rise in new cases.

Source citations (as archived): [France 24](<https://www.france24.com/en/20200818-merkel-rules-out-easing-coronavirus-rules-as-german-cases-spike>).

<a id="event-2020-08-18-2-7"></a>

Context: COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in Europe / COVID-19 pandemic in the Republic of Ireland.

**Archived source account.** Ireland "significantly" tightens restrictions after a rapid increase in the number of COVID-19 cases over the past two weeks. All businesses are told to let employees work from home, new limits are placed on outdoor gatherings, and the government warns people to avoid public transport. The new rules will be in place until at least September 13.

Source citations (as archived): [Sky News](<https://news.sky.com/story/coronavirus-ireland-significantly-tightens-restrictions-in-fight-to-control-covid-19-outbreaks-12051912>).

<a id="event-2020-08-18-2-9"></a>

Context: COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in Europe / COVID-19 pandemic in Russia.

**Archived source account.** Prime Minister Mikhail Mishustin announces that Energy Minister Alexander Novak has tested positive for COVID-19.

Source citations (as archived): [Anadolu Agency](<https://www.aa.com.tr/en/latest-on-coronavirus-outbreak/russian-energy-minister-tests-positive-for-covid-19/1945324>).

<a id="event-2020-08-18-2-11"></a>

Context: COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in Australia, COVID-19 vaccine.

**Archived source account.** Prime Minister Scott Morrison announces that his country has signed a deal with the British-Swedish pharmaceutical company AstraZeneca to manufacture a vaccine against COVID-19 that the company is developing with the Oxford Vaccine Group. The vaccine is currently in Phase III efficacy trials and AstraZeneca says it is targeting a formulation of results by the end of the year. Morrison states that the deal also allows citizens to receive immediate and free access to the vaccines, if successful.

Source citations (as archived): [AFP](<https://www.scmp.com/news/asia/australasia/article/3097866/coronavirus-australia-will-manufacture-vaccine-and-give-it>).

<a id="event-2020-08-18-2-13"></a>

Context: COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in Lebanon.

**Archived source account.** The acting government reimposes a curfew for two weeks amid a spike in COVID-19 infections.

Source citations (as archived): [Al Arabiya](<https://english.alarabiya.net/en/coronavirus/2020/08/18/Coronavirus-Lebanon-reimposes-lockdown-amid-COVID-19-spike>).

#### International relations

<a id="event-2020-08-18-3-2"></a>

Context: Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on the military / South Korea–United States relations, Korean conflict.

**Archived source account.** The United States Armed Forces resume joint military exercises with the Republic of Korea Armed Forces after several COVID-19 cases were confirmed at United States Forces Korea bases since February.

Source citations (as archived): [AFP](<https://www.manilatimes.net/2020/08/18/news/latest-stories/us-south-korea-begin-joint-military-drills-after-virus-delay/757179/>).

<a id="event-2020-08-18-3-4"></a>

Context: Belarus–Lithuania relations, 2020 Belarusian protests.

**Archived source account.** Lithuanian MPs approve economic sanctions against Belarus over the contested presidential elections. Lithuanian Foreign Minister Linas Linkevičius says Lithuania is "sending a strong message to the world" and refuses to recognize Alexander Lukashenko as President.

Source citations (as archived): [AP](<https://apnews.com/4308f39f7fd8e40ad4f7d551fa53f9cb>).

#### Law and crime

<a id="event-2020-08-18-4-1"></a>

Context: Assassination of Rafic Hariri.

**Archived source account.** The Special Tribunal for Lebanon finds Salim Ayyash, a senior member of Lebanese militant group Hezbollah, guilty of assassinating former Prime Minister Rafic Hariri in Beirut in 2005, following a five-year trial.

Source citations (as archived): [The Guardian](<https://www.theguardian.com/world/2020/aug/18/hezbollah-member-found-guilty-over-killing-rafik-hariri-lebanon>).

<a id="event-2020-08-18-4-3"></a>

Context: 2010 G20 Toronto summit protests.

**Archived source account.** The Toronto Police Service agrees to pay compensation of C$16.5 million (US$12.5M) to about 1,100 protesters who were wrongfully arrested in the city during the 2010 G20 summit.

Source citations (as archived): [The Guardian](<https://www.theguardian.com/world/2020/aug/18/g20-protesters-toronto-police-canada>).

<a id="event-2020-08-18-4-5"></a>

Context: MV Wakashio oil spill.

**Archived source account.** Police in Mauritius arrest the Captain of the ship which spilled huge amounts of petrol off the coast of the country, causing a major environmental disaster.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-mauritius-environment/mauritius-arrests-captain-of-stricken-japanese-oil-tanker-idUSKCN25E1UV?il=0>).

<a id="event-2020-08-18-4-6"></a>

**Archived source account.** Papua New Guinea police officers shoot and kill 11 prisoners after a mass jailbreak on Friday. At least 34 prisoners remain at large.

Source citations (as archived): [RNZ](<https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/423817/eleven-prisoners-killed-during-mass-jailbreak-in-png>).

#### Politics and elections

<a id="event-2020-08-18-5-1"></a>

Context: 2020 United States Postal Service crisis.

**Archived source account.** U.S. Postmaster General Louis DeJoy, in response to politicians' criticism that proposed changes to U.S. mail services could slow the handling of mail-in ballots, suspends all mail service changes until after the November election. He also said there will be no changes to retail hours at post offices, mail collection boxes will remain where they are, and no mail processing facilities will be closed. A number of states, including Washington and New York, said they are planning legal moves to block the Postal Service changes.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-usa-election-post-office/trumps-postmaster-general-pauses-service-cuts-after-mail-in-ballots-outcry-idUSKCN25E1Q2>).

<a id="event-2020-08-18-5-3"></a>

Context: Politics of Equatorial Guinea.

**Archived source account.** President Teodoro Obiang appoints Obama Asue as Prime Minister again, four days after he resigned generating criticism from the opposition.

Source citations (as archived): [La Vanguardia](<https://www.lavanguardia.com/politica/20200818/482902011935/obama-asue-designado-de-nuevo-como-primer-ministro-de-guinea-ecuatorial.html>).

### 2020-08-19

[Pinned Wikipedia revision 1083371678](<https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Portal%3ACurrent%20events%2F2020%20August%2019&oldid=1083371678>).

#### Armed conflicts and attacks

<a id="event-2020-08-19-0-1"></a>

Context: 2020 Malian protests, 2020 Malian coup d'état.

**Archived source account.** President Ibrahim Boubacar Keïta announces his resignation on state television.

Source citations (as archived): [AP](<https://apnews.com/54737684e3e2a84f9b44656de7343e56>).

<a id="event-2020-08-19-0-2"></a>

Context: 2020 Malian protests, 2020 Malian coup d'état.

**Archived source account.** The soldiers who ousted Keïta promise fresh elections within a "reasonable" time. A spokesman for the mutineers says they acted "to prevent further chaos in Mali" while Colonel Ismaël Wagué invited civil society and political parties to join a peaceful transition.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-mali-security/mali-soldiers-promise-election-as-region-seeks-way-out-of-coup-crisis-idUSKCN25F0NB>).

<a id="event-2020-08-19-0-3"></a>

Context: 2020 Malian protests, 2020 Malian coup d'état.

**Archived source account.** The new military rulers announce the closure of all border crossings and impose a night-time curfew until further notice.

Source citations (as archived): [BBC News](<https://www.bbc.com/news/world-africa-53830348>).

<a id="event-2020-08-19-0-4"></a>

Context: 2020 Malian protests, 2020 Malian coup d'état.

**Archived source account.** The United Nations Security Council unanimously approves a resolution condemning the coup and calling on the soldiers to return to their barracks and release all detainees.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-mali-security-un/u-n-security-council-condemns-mutiny-in-mali-urges-soldiers-return-to-barracks-idUSKCN25F2FY?il=0>).

<a id="event-2020-08-19-0-5"></a>

Context: 2020 Malian protests, 2020 Malian coup d'état.

**Archived source account.** The African Union suspends Mali's membership in response to the coup. The suspension will last until "constitutional order is restored".

Source citations (as archived): [France 24](<https://www.france24.com/en/20200819-mali-coup-leaders-face-international-condemnation-au-suspends-membership>).

<a id="event-2020-08-19-0-6"></a>

Context: 2020 Malian protests, 2020 Malian coup d'état.

**Archived source account.** In an evening transmission, Col. Assimi Goita declares himself the new leader of Mali and urges citizens to return to work.

Source citations (as archived): [AP](<https://www.apnews.com/bcc4875ece4dffff7392c73a9e521bd0>).

#### Business and economy

<a id="event-2020-08-19-1-0"></a>

**Archived source account.** The U.S. Treasury Department blacklists two Emirati companies for conducting business with Iranian airline Mahan Air, which itself is blacklisted for its close ties with the Iranian Revolutionary Guards.

Source citations (as archived): [New Indian Express](<https://www.newindianexpress.com/world/2020/aug/19/us-blacklists-uae-firms-for-supporting-boycotted-iranian-airline-mahan-air-2185664.html>).

#### Disasters and accidents

<a id="event-2020-08-19-2-1"></a>

Context: 2020 California wildfires.

**Archived source account.** Thousands in the San Francisco Bay Area flee their homes after several quick-moving wildfires, apparently sparked by lightning and the heatwave, sweep into the region. Around 50 structures have burned down with another 50 damaged in Vacaville. This group of fires, called the LNU Lightning Complex, has grown to 46,000 uncontained acres.

Source citations (as archived): [BBC News](<https://www.bbc.com/news/world-us-canada-53840437>).

<a id="event-2020-08-19-2-2"></a>

**Archived source account.** At least 45 migrants, including five children, die in a shipwreck off Libya. In addition, 37 other people are rescued by local fishermen.

Source citations (as archived): [BBC News](<https://www.bbc.com/news/world-africa-53842742>).

#### Health and environment

<a id="event-2020-08-19-3-3"></a>

Context: COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in Europe / COVID-19 pandemic in France.

**Archived source account.** Toulouse becomes the first major city in France to make face masks compulsory in all outdoor areas. The new rules will take effect on Friday and apply from 7:00 a.m. to 3:00 a.m. local time for all people ages 12 and up, including those on bikes and kick-scooters.

Source citations (as archived): [The Telegraph](<https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/2020/08/19/toulouse-becomes-first-major-french-city-impose-blanket-mask/>).

<a id="event-2020-08-19-3-4"></a>

Context: COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in Europe / COVID-19 pandemic in France.

**Archived source account.** France registers 3,776 new cases in the last 24 hours, marking a new post-lockdown peak and bringing the total to 225,043.

Source citations (as archived): [France 24](<https://www.france24.com/en/20200819-france-daily-covid-19-cases-hit-new-post-lockdown-high>).

<a id="event-2020-08-19-3-6"></a>

Context: COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in Europe / COVID-19 pandemic in Italy.

**Archived source account.** Italy reports 642 new COVID-19 cases in the last 24 hours, which is the highest number of reported cases since May 23, when the lockdown was eased.

Source citations (as archived): [ANSA](<https://www.ansa.it/english/news/2020/08/19/coronavirus-sharp-rise-in-cases-642-7-more-dead_9c139172-7158-49f3-aea8-331d62ee3a92.html>); [Yahoo News UK](<https://uk.news.yahoo.com/italy-covid-19-lockdown-rise-in-cases-coronavirus-180738411.html>).

<a id="event-2020-08-19-3-8"></a>

Context: COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in Europe / COVID-19 pandemic in Spain.

**Archived source account.** Spain registers its highest number of new cases since the end of the lockdown in June, with 3,715 new cases reported in the last 24 hours.

Source citations (as archived): [The Times](<https://www.thetimes.co.uk/article/spain-coronavirus-cases-at-new-high-since-end-of-lockdown-p5rbbwmm0>).

<a id="event-2020-08-19-3-11"></a>

Context: COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in Asia / COVID-19 pandemic in Iran.

**Archived source account.** Iran surpasses 20,000 deaths by COVID-19, the highest toll in the Middle East.

Source citations (as archived): [AP](<https://www.apnews.com/63eea48e390cbd55effcad562def89d9>).

<a id="event-2020-08-19-3-13"></a>

Context: COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in Asia / COVID-19 pandemic in South Korea.

**Archived source account.** South Korea reports its highest daily rise in COVID-19 cases since early March, with 297 new cases being reported in the last 24 hours. Nearly 90% of the new cases appeared in Seoul Capital Area, where 166 of them are linked to the Sarang Jeil Church.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-southkorea/south-korea-warns-of-nationwide-coronavirus-risk-as-church-outbreaks-spread-idUSKCN25F05N>).

<a id="event-2020-08-19-3-14"></a>

Context: COVID-19 pandemic.

**Archived source account.** Fiji declares an outbreak of dengue fever and leptospirosis amidst the COVID-19 pandemic. Health minister Ifereimi Waqainabete says that between January and July, 3,300 cases of dengue fever and 1,000 of leptospirosis were reported.

Source citations (as archived): [RNZ](<https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/423925/fiji-declares-dengue-and-leptospirosis-outbreak>).

<a id="event-2020-08-19-3-15"></a>

**Archived source account.** The California Department of Public Health reports the state's first case of plague in five years at South Lake Tahoe. The patient, believed to have been bitten by an infected flea, is under medical care recovering at home. The CDC says that America sees between one and 17 cases annually.

Source citations (as archived): [CBS News](<https://www.cbsnews.com/news/south-tahoe-california-bubonic-plague-resident-tests-positive/>); [Yahoo\!](<https://www.yahoo.com/lifestyle/california-first-plague-case-5-years-182518943.html>).

#### International relations

<a id="event-2020-08-19-4-2"></a>

Context: Travel restrictions related to the COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in Finland.

**Archived source account.** Finland imposes "Europe's tightest" border restrictions on several countries which it had considered safe destinations to stop the spread of COVID-19. Travel from most EU member states, as well as Japan and Iceland, will be limited to essential trips starting August 24, with people returning from those countries required to self-quarantine for two weeks.

Source citations (as archived): [Yle](<https://yle.fi/uutiset/osasto/news/finland_brings_back_border_checks_for_travellers_eases_impact_for_border_communities/11501293>); [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/health-coronavirus-finland-travel/finland-returns-travel-restrictions-for-several-countries-idUSL8N2FL1C6>).

<a id="event-2020-08-19-4-4"></a>

Context: Belarus–European Union relations.

**Archived source account.** The European Union formally rejects the result of the latest presidential election in Belarus, which saw Alexander Lukashenko re-elected with over 80% of the vote. The European Commission announces it will reroute €53 million away from the Belarusian government to civil society.

Source citations (as archived): [Sky News](<https://news.sky.com/story/eu-threatens-belarus-sanctions-as-it-rejects-election-result-12052472>).

<a id="event-2020-08-19-4-6"></a>

Context: Norway–Russia relations.

**Archived source account.** The Norwegian Ministry of Foreign Affairs confirms it has expelled a diplomat from the Russian embassy in Oslo for alleged espionage. The embassy claims the expelled individual was their deputy trade representative who was arrested by Norwegian police on August 20 during a meeting with a suspected spy. The embassy protested to the Norwegian foreign ministry, calling the arrest "a violation of the diplomat status." The ministry, however, has not disclosed the identity of the Russian diplomat nor that of the suspected spy.

Source citations (as archived): [Al Jazeera](<https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/08/norway-expels-russian-diplomat-arresting-suspected-spy-200819114414375.html>).

#### Law and crime

<a id="event-2020-08-19-5-1"></a>

Context: Christianity in Iran.

**Archived source account.** A court in Iran upholds the sentences of five Christian citizens who were charged with spreading Christianity and acting against national security by organizing and running house churches.

Source citations (as archived): [Al Arabiya](<https://english.alarabiya.net/en/News/middle-east/2020/08/19/Iran-upholds-prison-sentences-of-five-Christians.html>).

<a id="event-2020-08-19-5-2"></a>

**Archived source account.** U.S. Attorney General William Barr, in a letter to UK Home Secretary Priti Patel, declares that Alexanda Kotey and El Shafee Elsheikh, members of "The Beatles" ISIL cell, will not be given the death penalty if found guilty. Prior attempts by the United States to get the UK Home Office to cooperate on the terrorists' prosecution had been stymied due to the latter's long-standing policy of refusing to extradite citizens or aid in their prosecution if the death penalty was sought.

Source citations (as archived): [BBC News](<https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-53837724>).

<a id="event-2020-08-19-5-3"></a>

**Archived source account.** A 41-year-old Eritrean man from Switzerland faces trial in Germany for allegedly pushing an eight-year-old boy and his mother onto the tracks of an Intercity Express train at the Frankfurt central station in July; the boy was killed, but his mother survived. A psychiatric assessment showed that the man suffered from an episode of schizophrenia and had "at least a considerably reduced ability" to control his actions. The incident triggered reactions from across the German federal government, who have called for a review of the country's immigration policies.

<a id="event-2020-08-21-5-5"></a>

Context: Afghanistan–Pakistan relations.

**Archived source account.** The Pakistani Foreign Ministry reveals that it on August 18 placed financial sanctions on dozens of Taliban members, including chief negotiator Mullah Abdul Ghani Baradar, and deputy head and Haqqani network leader Sirajuddin Haqqani. The sanctions were placed to avoid placing the country on the Financial Action Task Force blacklist.

Source citations (as archived): [Al Jazeera](<https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/08/pakistan-sanctions-taliban-avoid-global-finance-blacklist-200822151917665.html>).

#### Law and crime

<a id="event-2020-08-21-6-0"></a>

**Archived source account.** A court in Zimbabwe denies, for the third time, bail to opposition politician and activist Jacob Ngarivhume after ruling he "could be a danger to the public if released", over protests he organized last month. His lawyer says he is "stunned" by the court's decision.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-zimbabwe-protests/zimbabwe-politician-who-called-for-protests-denied-bail-for-third-time-idUSKBN25H1IQ?il=0>).

<a id="event-2020-08-21-6-1"></a>

Source citations (as archived): [Xinhua](<http://www.xinhuanet.com/english/2020-08/21/c_139307841.htm>).

<a id="event-2020-08-21-6-2"></a>

**Archived source account.** American actress Lori Loughlin is sentenced to two months in prison and her husband, fashion designer Mossimo Giannulli, is sentenced to five months in prison for their role in the college admissions scandal.

Source citations (as archived): [Los Angeles Times](<https://www.latimes.com/california/story/2020-08-21/lori-loughlin-mossimo-giannulli-college-admissions-scandal-sentencing>).

<a id="event-2020-08-21-6-3"></a>

**Archived source account.** Former California police officer Joseph James DeAngelo, also known as the Golden State Killer, receives multiple consecutive life sentences without parole in the county superior court in Sacramento. DeAngelo pleaded guilty in June to 13 counts of first-degree murder in exchange for taking the death penalty off the table.

Source citations (as archived): [ABC News](<https://abcnews.go.com/US/living-witness-teen-dads-murder-confronts-golden-state/story?id=72473195>).

<a id="event-2020-08-21-6-4"></a>

**Archived source account.** The press office of deposed Bolivian President Evo Morales rejects a criminal complaint filed this week by the Ministry of Justice accusing him of trafficking and raping a 16-year-old girl, claiming it was part of a "dirty war" waged by the interim government.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-bolivia-morales-complaint/morales-office-denounces-sex-complaint-as-dirty-war-by-interim-government-idUSKBN25I0P1?il=0>).

<a id="event-2020-08-21-7-2"></a>

Context: Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on politics / COVID-19 pandemic in the Republic of Ireland.

**Archived source account.** Irish Agriculture Minister Dara Calleary resigns after attending a golf dinner with more than 80 people, which came a day after Dublin announced a tightening of lockdown restrictions. Gardaí are now investigating possible breaches of COVID-19 regulations on the event.

Source citations (as archived): [BBC News](<https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-53859988>).

<a id="event-2020-08-21-7-4"></a>

Context: Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on politics / COVID-19 pandemic in Kenya, protests over responses to the COVID-19 pandemic.

**Archived source account.** Police arrest anti-corruption protesters in Nairobi for allegedly disobeying social distancing measures. Protesters, however, claim the arrests were an attempt by authorities to silence dissent and report that police have used tear gas to disperse the crowds.

Source citations (as archived): [AP](<https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/africa/kenyan-police-teargas-anti-corruption-protesters-in-nairobi/2020/08/21/bb4cd452-e3ab-11ea-82d8-5e55d47e90ca_story.html>).

<a id="event-2020-08-21-7-6"></a>

Context: 2019–2020 Iraqi protests.

**Archived source account.** Protesters in the southern city of Basra set fire to a local parliament office after gathering to demand the resignation of governor Asaad Al Eidani for the killing of two activists last week.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-iraq-security/protesters-set-fire-to-parliament-office-in-iraqs-basra-idUSKBN25H2EG?il=0>).

<a id="event-2020-08-21-7-7"></a>

**Archived source account.** Doctors treating Russian anti-corruption activist and opposition leader Alexei Navalny in Omsk refute claims that Navalny was poisoned before his flight from Tomsk to Moscow the previous day, citing that tests had shown no trace of any poison in his body. German Chancellor Angela Merkel has offered to transfer Navalny to Berlin for further treatment by sending an air ambulance to Omsk, but doctors have refused to discharge him, saying Navalny is in an "unstable" condition. Navalny's spokeswoman Kira Yarmysh claim the refusal is a ploy to hide the poisoning and "put his life at risk".

Source citations (as archived): [AFP](<https://www.ndtv.com/world-news/russian-opposition-leader-poisned-no-trace-of-poison-found-in-navalny-tests-says-doctor-2283059>).

[Pinned Wikipedia revision 1179236515](<https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Portal%3ACurrent%20events%2F2020%20August%2022&oldid=1179236515>).

#### Armed conflicts and attacks

<a id="event-2020-08-22-0-2"></a>

Context: War in Afghanistan / Afghan peace process, August 2020 Afghanistan attacks.

**Archived source account.** At least 14 security forces are killed across Afghanistan in attacks in Takhar, Badakhshan, and Kabul. The Taliban claims responsibility for the first two attacks but denies involvement in Kabul's. The group reiterated that it will not enter peace talks with the government until all prisoners are released.

Source citations (as archived): [Al Jazeera](<https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/08/afghanistan-14-security-forces-killed-attacks-200822111402959.html>).

<a id="event-2020-08-22-0-4"></a>

Context: 2020 Democratic Republic of the Congo massacres.

**Archived source account.** Suspected Islamist militants kill 13 people during raids on two villages in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, the army and a village chief report. It is the latest of such attacks that the United Nations says may be war crimes. The Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) have killed more than 1,000 people since 2019, according to UN figures.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-congo-violence/suspected-islamist-militants-kill-13-in-eastern-congo-villages-idUSKBN25I0D1>).

<a id="event-2020-08-22-0-6"></a>

Context: Colombian conflict.

**Archived source account.** Three massacres kill 28 people, in Arauca, Cauca, and Nariño. These complete a week with five massacres, adding up to more than 33 this year. Gangs are believed to be responsible for nearly 80 percent of massacres in Colombia this year, the vast majority of them occurring in departments with illegal coca-producing enclaves.

Source citations (as archived): [Colombia Reports](<https://colombiareports.com/colombia-ends-terrifying-week-with-three-massacres-in-one-day/>); [Buenos Aires Times](<https://www.batimes.com.ar/news/latin-america/united-nations-condemns-spike-in-colombia-massacres.phtml>).

#### Disasters and accidents

<a id="event-2020-08-22-1-1"></a>

Context: 2020 Atlantic hurricane season.

**Archived source account.** Two simultaneous tropical storms, Laura and Marco, threaten Gulf Coast residents in the coming days. Laura is currently over Puerto Rico, while Marco is making its way through the Yucatan Channel. This would mark the first time in over 60 years in which two tropical storms were active simultaneously in the Gulf of Mexico.

Source citations (as archived): [CNN](<https://edition.cnn.com/2020/08/22/weather/tropical-storm-laura-marco-atlantic-gulf-forecast-saturday/index.html>); [CNN2](<https://www.cnn.com/2020/08/21/weather/atlantic-tropical-development-forecast-friday/index.html>).

<a id="event-2020-08-22-1-3"></a>

Context: COVID-19 pandemic in Peru.

**Archived source account.** At least 13 people are killed after police raid a nightclub in Lima for breaching restrictions that were imposed in response to the pandemic. Police report that a stampede occurred as patrons tried to escape, resulting in casualties, while others were killed due to asphyxiation.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.hindustantimes.com/world-news/at-least-13-crushed-to-death-as-peru-police-raid-clandestine-club-party/story-uaK8UsOuw1TbJqeSUQbjaJ.html>).

<a id="event-2020-08-22-1-4"></a>

**Archived source account.** A cargo aircraft crashes upon takeoff from Juba International Airport in Juba, South Sudan, en route to the cities of Aweil and Wau, killing at least 17 people.

Source citations (as archived): [Xinhua](<http://www.xinhuanet.com/english/2020-08/22/c_139310179.htm>).

<a id="event-2020-08-22-3-0"></a>

**Archived source account.** A 90-minute meeting held between delegates representing the Economic Community of West African States and leaders of the recent coup d'état in Mali over a return to civilian rule is cut short to 20 minutes for unknown reasons.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-mali-security/malis-coup-leaders-meet-mediators-seeking-return-to-civilian-rule-idUSKBN25I0FI?il=0>).

#### Law and crime

<a id="event-2020-08-22-4-2"></a>

Context: George Floyd Protests / George Floyd protests in Portland, Oregon.

**Archived source account.** Department of Homeland Security officers force demonstrators out of a plaza near Multnomah County Justice Center as dueling demonstrations in Portland, Oregon by right-wing and left-wing protesters turn violent. Images show hundreds of people involved, many of them wearing helmets and carrying makeshift shields. Some demonstrators appeared to use pepper spray and at least one person appeared to pull a gun, but no arrests have been made so far.

Source citations (as archived): [NBC News](<https://www.nbcnews.com/news/us-news/portland-protest-turns-violent-federal-police-clear-plaza-n1237784>).

<a id="event-2020-08-22-4-4"></a>

Context: George Floyd Protests / George Floyd protests in Michigan.

**Archived source account.** Forty people are arrested while protesting Operation Legend in Detroit. Police also used tear gas and pepper spray on the crowd of about 100 people.

Source citations (as archived): [WDIV](<https://www.clickondetroit.com/news/local/2020/08/23/dozens-of-protesters-on-woodward-avenue-tear-gassed-arrested-downtown/>).

<a id="event-2020-08-22-4-5"></a>

**Archived source account.** Sudanese prime minister Abdalla Hamdok says that Sudan is ready to cooperate with the International Criminal Court (ICC) to facilitate the international body access to alleged war criminals over the Darfur War, including former ruler Omar al-Bashir.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-sudan-politics/sudan-ready-to-cooperate-with-icc-over-darfur-says-pm-idUSKBN25I0P3?il=0>).

#### Politics and elections

<a id="event-2020-08-22-5-2"></a>

Context: Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on politics / COVID-19 pandemic in the United States, 2020 United States Postal Service crisis.

**Archived source account.** In a 257–150 vote, the House of Representatives approves a bill that would reverse changes to the operations of the Postal Service implemented by Postmaster General Louis DeJoy, amid a series of backlogs and delays in the delivery of mail following his appointment in June. The bill also aims to provide the agency financial support worth $25 billion in preparation for an expected surge in postal voting in the upcoming election due to the pandemic.

Source citations (as archived): [AP](<https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/1325827/us-house-passes-bill-to-reverse-changes-blamed-for-mail-delays>).

Context: 2020 Ivorian presidential election.

**Archived source account.** Incumbent President Alassane Ouattara is formally chosen by his party, the Rally of the Republicans, to run for a third term in the October election. However, opposition and civil society groups claim the move is unconstitutional, as the Constitution limits a president to only two terms.

Source citations (as archived): [France 24](<https://www.france24.com/en/20200822-ivory-coast-rejects-election-bids-of-ex-president-gbagbo-ex-rebel-leader-soro>).

<a id="event-2020-08-22-5-6"></a>

Context: 2020 Northern Territory general election.

**Archived source account.** Australia's Northern Territory re-elects the incumbent Labor Party government.

Source citations (as archived): [ABC](<https://www.abc.net.au/news/2020-08-24/nt-labor-and-michael-gunner-to-form-majority-government/12586980>).

<a id="event-2020-08-22-5-7"></a>

**Archived source account.** Alexei Navalny is admitted to the Charité hospital in Berlin, Germany, following a medical evacuation flight from Omsk, Russia. The chairman of the Cinema for Peace Foundation, which organized the evacuation, says the comatose Russian opposition leader is in a "stable condition".

Source citations (as archived): [CNN](<https://edition.cnn.com/2020/08/21/europe/alexey-navalny-germany-flight-intl-hnk/index.html>).

#### Armed conflicts and attacks

<a id="event-2020-08-23-0-2"></a>

Context: War in Afghanistan / August 2020 Afghanistan attacks.

**Archived source account.** Seven civilians are killed by a roadside bomb in Jaghatū, Ghazni. The Governor of Paktia, Mohammad Halim Fidai, survives an assassination attempt. No group claimed responsibility for either incident.

Source citations (as archived): [Al Jazeera](<https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/08/civilians-killed-roadside-bomb-afghanistan-200823110917678.html>).

<a id="event-2020-08-23-0-4"></a>

Context: Second Libyan Civil War.

**Archived source account.** A spokesman for Khalifa Haftar's Libyan National Army (LNA) rejects a ceasefire proposed by the Government of National Accord (GNA) and says it is a "marketing stunt". He says GNA forces are mobilising in different fronts in the country and the LNA will defend from any attack on its positions around Sirte and Jufra. Yesterday, the High Council of State, which advises the GNA, rejected dialogue with Haftar.

Source citations (as archived): [Al Jazeera](<https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/08/haftar-rejects-gna-call-libya-ceasefire-200823173428282.html>).

<a id="event-2020-08-23-1-1"></a>

Context: 2020 Atlantic hurricane season.

**Archived source account.** Hurricane warnings are issued for the state of Louisiana and parts of Mississippi as it is expected that Tropical Storm Marco will become a hurricane later today. Meanwhile, Tropical Storm Laura is also advancing toward the United States after leaving torrential rain in parts of Haiti and the Dominican Republic. The Louisiana Governor John Bel Edwards requests a federal emergency declaration; Mississippi Governor Tate Reeves declares a state of emergency.

Source citations (as archived): [The Guardian](<https://www.theguardian.com/world/2020/aug/23/marco-laura-us-coast-hurricanes-forecast-tropical-storms-louisiana-mississippi>); [ABC News](<https://abcnews.go.com/US/marco-laura-forecast-hit-us-hurricanes/story?id=72551197>).

<a id="event-2020-08-23-1-2"></a>

Context: 2020 Atlantic hurricane season.

**Archived source account.** Marco becomes a hurricane and is expected to make landfall in Louisiana on Monday or early Tuesday. Laura is expected to become a hurricane as well by Wednesday.

Source citations (as archived): [USA Today](<https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/nation/2020/08/23/tropical-storm-laura-tropical-storm-marco-double-hurricanes-possible/3423634001/>).

Context: COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in Asia / COVID-19 pandemic in India.

Context: COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in Europe / COVID-19 pandemic in Ukraine.

<a id="event-2020-08-23-2-12"></a>

Context: COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in Australia.

<a id="event-2020-08-23-2-14"></a>

Context: COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in the United States.

**Archived source account.** President Donald Trump and the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) announce the emergency use authorization of convalescent plasma for COVID-19 patients after days of White House officials suggesting there were politically motivated delays by the FDA in approving a vaccine and therapeutics for the disease that President Trump claims has harmed his re-election chances. The FDA said more than 70,000 patients have been treated with convalescent plasma, but they have not yet obtained enough randomized clinical trial data on convalescent plasma for COVID-19. Some of those trials are underway.

#### Law and crime

<a id="event-2020-08-23-4-1"></a>

Context: Shooting of Jacob Blake, George Floyd protests.

**Archived source account.** Protests have erupted in the Kenosha, Wisconsin after police shot a black man, Jacob Blake, many times while responding to what they claimed was a domestic incident. An online video shows Blake being shot in the back in broad daylight as he tries to get into a car. Authorities declared an emergency overnight curfew after unrest broke out following the shooting. Vehicles were set on fire and protesters shouted "We won't back down".

Source citations (as archived): [BBC News](<https://www.bbc.com/news/world-us-canada-53886070>).

<a id="event-2020-08-23-4-2"></a>

#### Armed conflicts and attacks

<a id="event-2020-08-24-0-2"></a>

Context: Moro conflict / 2020 Jolo bombings.

**Archived source account.** Militants believed to be Abu Sayyaf jihadists detonate two bombs in Jolo, Sulu, Philippines, killing 14 people and wounding 75 others. The first occurred as army personnel were assisting in carrying out COVID-19 humanitarian efforts. The second was carried out by a female suicide bomber near the Our Lady of Mount Carmel Cathedral, which was bombed in 2019.

Source citations (as archived): [The New York Times](<https://www.nytimes.com/2020/08/24/world/asia/-philippines-explosions-jolo-sulu.html>).

<a id="event-2020-08-24-0-4"></a>

Context: Syrian civil war.

**Archived source account.** A major blackout is reported in Syria after an explosion hits the Arab Gas Pipeline in the Rif Dimashq Governorate. Syrian Oil Minister Ali Ghanem says the explosion was a "terrorist attack", but does not elaborate on who was behind it.

Source citations (as archived): [Al Jazeera](<https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/08/syria-blackout-suspected-pipeline-attack-200824070256527.html>).

<a id="event-2020-08-24-0-5"></a>

**Archived source account.** An armed assault erupts on Sunday and continues into today in Bugarama, Rumonge, Burundi between militants and security forces, leaving at least 15 people dead. A group named Red Tabara, based in Kivu, Democratic Republic of the Congo, claims responsibility and says that the election of past May won by Évariste Ndayishimiye were a "farce" and calls for new elections. The Burundian army did not comment on the attack.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-burundi-violence-rebels/at-least-15-dead-as-rebels-attack-southern-burundi-idUSKBN25K294?il=0>).

**Archived source account.** Two people are fatally shot and one wounded during protests in Kenosha, Wisconsin over the shooting of Jacob Blake. Police are investigating whether the incident occurred during a confrontation between protesters and armed men.

Source citations (as archived): [CNN](<https://www.cnn.com/2020/08/26/us/kenosha-wisconsin-wednesday-shooting/index.html>).

<a id="event-2020-08-25-5-5"></a>

Context: 2020 United States racial unrest / Shooting of Jacob Blake, Kenosha unrest, Kenosha unrest shooting.

**Archived source account.** Wisconsin's Governor Tony Evers declared a state of emergency due to persistent unrest in Kenosha.

Source citations (as archived): [The Wall Street Journal](<https://www.wsj.com/articles/kenosha-wis-sees-second-night-of-violence-as-unrest-spreads-11598362900>).

<a id="event-2020-08-25-5-6"></a>

**Archived source account.** The High Court of Hong Kong denies release for the first person arrested under the Hong Kong national security law. The 23-year-old man had driven a motorbike into several policemen knocking them down on a narrow street before falling over and getting arrested.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-hongkong-security/hong-kong-court-again-denies-bail-for-first-person-charged-under-new-security-law-idUSKBN25L0CK>).

<a id="event-2020-08-25-5-7"></a>

**Archived source account.** Manchester United captain and England international Harry Maguire is given a suspended sentence of 21 months and 10 days in prison by a Greek court for repeated bodily harm, attempted bribery of police, violence against public employees and insult, following his arrest on the island of Mykonos.

Source citations (as archived): [BBC Sport](<https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/53903703>).

### 2020-08-26

#### Armed conflicts and attacks

<a id="event-2020-08-26-0-1"></a>

Context: Boko Haram insurgency.

**Archived source account.** Boko Haram insurgents carries out an overnight attack against a village in Gwoza, Nigeria, killing 75 elders.

Source citations (as archived): [Premium Times](<https://www.premiumtimesng.com/news/headlines/410990-75-borno-elders-slaughtered-by-boko-haram-in-one-night-senator.html>).

<a id="event-2020-08-26-0-3"></a>

Context: Somali Civil War.

**Archived source account.** The United States Africa Command announces that the U.S. carried out an airstrike on Monday that resulted in the deaths of six militants of the al-Shabaab jihadist group after they had attacked Somali forces during preceding days. It was carried out in Lower Shabelle, Somalia. Three other al-Shabaab militants were wounded.

Source citations (as archived): [AP](<https://english.alarabiya.net/en/News/middle-east/2020/08/26/US-says-airstrike-kills-six-al-Shabab-in-Somalia-after-ambush.html>).

Context: Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on religion / Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on the Catholic Church, COVID-19 pandemic in Vatican City.

**Archived source account.** The Holy See announces that Pope Francis will resume public audiences in September for the first time in nearly six months. However, the events will be limited to 500 people, held in a closed courtyard of the Apostolic Palace.

Source citations (as archived): [AFP](<http://www.koreatimes.co.kr/www/world/2020/08/685_295028.html>).

<a id="event-2020-08-26-1-3"></a>

Source citations (as archived): [The Guardian](<https://www.theguardian.com/books/2020/aug/26/marieke-lucas-rijneveld-wins-international-booker-for-the-discomfort-of-evening>).

<a id="event-2020-08-26-2-0"></a>

**Archived source account.** The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission approves new rules that will allow companies that wish to raise capital, and be listed on the New York Stock Exchange, to use direct listings instead of IPOs.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-nyse-direct-listing/sec-approves-nyse-proposal-to-allow-capital-raise-through-direct-listings-idUSKBN25M2S6?il=0>).

#### Disasters and accidents

<a id="event-2020-08-26-3-1"></a>

Context: 2020 Afghanistan flood.

**Archived source account.** Flash floods brought by torrential rains in northeastern Afghanistan kill at least 100 people in Charikar, Parwan Province, Afghanistan, with at least 300 houses in the area destroyed. The Ministry of Disaster Management has also reported some casualties and destruction of infrastructure in the provinces of Kapisa, Maidan Wardak, Nangarhar, Paktia, and Panjshir.

Source citations (as archived): [Al Jazeera](<https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/08/afghanistan-flooding-dozens-dead-hundreds-homes-destroyed-200826061120112.html>).

<a id="event-2020-08-26-3-6"></a>

Context: 2020 Pacific typhoon season.

**Archived source account.** North and South Korea prepare to receive Typhoon Bavi which is already lashing the South Korean island of Jeju flooding roads, toppling trees, ripping off signboards and knocking down lampposts as it passed over waters off the island’s western shores. No casualties are reported.

Source citations (as archived): [AP](<https://apnews.com/ccdbc526291571a4543f61cb7ed6446f>).

#### Health and environment

<a id="event-2020-08-26-4-4"></a>

Context: COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in the United States / COVID-19 pandemic in Ohio / COVID-19 pandemic in Columbus, Ohio.

**Archived source account.** Ohio State University suspends more than 200 students for breaking some COVID-19 guidelines even before the school year starts.

Source citations (as archived): [NPR](<https://www.npr.org/sections/coronavirus-live-updates/2020/08/25/906039378/more-than-200-ohio-state-university-students-suspended-for-violating-pandemic-ru>).

<a id="event-2020-08-26-4-6"></a>

Context: COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in the United States / COVID-19 pandemic testing in the United States.

**Archived source account.** The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention this week changed its COVID-19 testing guidelines to say that people who've been in close contact with someone known to have COVID-19 but are asymptomatic now "do not necessarily" need to get tested. Health experts are expressing alarm over this revision since, for example, up to 50 percent of all COVID-19 transmissions are due to people who do not exhibit symptoms of the disease.

Source citations (as archived): [Voice of America](<https://www.voanews.com/covid-19-pandemic/cdc-relaxes-covid-testing-guidelines-alarming-some-health-providers>).

<a id="event-2020-08-26-4-7"></a>

Context: COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in the United States / COVID-19 pandemic testing in the United States.

**Archived source account.** Dr. Anthony Fauci, director of the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases and member of the White House Coronavirus Task Force, said he was in surgery for vocal cord polyp removal and was not part of the discussion during the August 20 task force meeting when updated guidelines were discussed. He also expressed concerns over how people would interpret the new recommendations.

Source citations (as archived): [CNN](<https://www.cnn.com/2020/08/26/politics/cdc-coronavirus-testing-guidance/index.html>); [The Daily Beast](<https://www.thedailybeast.com/dr-fauci-says-he-was-under-anesthesia-when-cdc-changed-covid-19-testing-guidelines>).

Context: COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in the United States / COVID-19 pandemic in California.

<a id="event-2020-08-26-4-10"></a>

Context: COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in the United States.

Context: Travel restrictions related to the COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in France, COVID-19 pandemic in Belgium.

**Archived source account.** Belgium's foreign ministry banned travel to Paris amid concerns over a possible resurgence of cases in the French capital. Belgians are being advised to avoid visiting Paris unless travellers agree to take a COVID-19 test or undergo a period of self-isolation on their return.

Source citations (as archived): [Euronews](<https://www.euronews.com/2020/08/26/coronavirus-belgium-bans-travel-to-paris-amid-resurgence-of-covid-19-cases-in-french-capit>).

Context: Travel restrictions related to the COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in Germany, COVID-19 pandemic in Norway, COVID-19 pandemic in Liechtenstein.

Source citations (as archived): [The New York Times](<https://www.nytimes.com/reuters/2020/08/26/world/europe/26reuters-health-coronavirus-norway-germany.html>).

Context: China–United States relations, Territorial disputes in the South China Sea.

**Archived source account.** The United States Department of Commerce adds 24 Chinese state-owned enterprises to its "entity list", restricting the access of these enterprises to U.S. goods and content. U.S. Secretary of State Mike Pompeo claims that these enterprises are involved in China's expansion and militarization efforts in the disputed regions of the South China Sea.

**Archived source account.** In a meeting between U.S. Secretary of State Mike Pompeo and Chairman of the Sovereignty Council of Sudan Abdel Fattah al-Burhan, the United States proposed removing Sudan from the U.S. state sponsors of terrorism list for $330 million compensation. The payment would allegedly go to American victims of Al-Qaida but ministers, opposition leaders, and other people in the country have expressed anger at the prospect of a multimillion-dollar payment to the United States.

Source citations (as archived): [The Guardian](<https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2020/aug/26/us-propose-to-remove-sudan-from-terrorism-list-for-330m-compensation?fbclid=IwAR2xWBZv4tpQdBka-BuAZP9I9kekDwynkVA9ev8CJ0FjUQhZbMmoj4HQoE8>).

Churchill of the U.S. Navy in the Eastern Mediterranean, hours after Greece conducted similar exercises with France, Italy, and Cyprus in the disputed region.

Source citations (as archived): [AFP](<https://www.wionews.com/world/turkey-says-conducted-mediterranean-exercise-with-us-323260>).

<a id="event-2020-08-27-3-12"></a>

**Archived source account.** France records its highest number of new daily infections since the end of the lockdown in early May, with an additional 6,111 cases reported over the past 24 hours, making it the second highest ever, after 7,578 new cases set on March 30.

Source citations (as archived): [BBC News](<https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-53934952>); [France 24](<https://www.france24.com/en/20200827-france-records-more-than-6-000-new-covid-19-cases-highest-figure-since-april>).

<a id="event-2020-08-27-3-14"></a>

Context: COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in Europe / COVID-19 pandemic in Italy.

**Archived source account.** Italy records its highest number of new cases since early May, when the country was still in lockdown, with 1,411 new cases reported in the last 24 hours.

Source citations (as archived): [The Telegraph](<https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/2020/08/27/italy-records-highest-number-coronavirus-cases-since-lockdown/amp/>).

<a id="event-2020-08-27-3-17"></a>

Context: COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in the United States / COVID-19 pandemic in Alabama.

**Archived source account.** Alabama Governor Kay Ivey extends the state's mask mandate and safer-at-home order to October 2.

Source citations (as archived): [Bizjournals.com](<https://www.bizjournals.com/birmingham/news/2020/08/27/safer-at-home-extended-until-october.html>); [Patch.com](<https://patch.com/alabama/birmingham-al/ivey-extends-mask-order-october>).

<a id="event-2020-08-27-3-18"></a>

**Archived source account.** Fiji's opposition parties condemn the government over the handling of the dengue fever and leptospirosis outbreaks, saying that the government has not informed the public of the seriousness of the diseases. Vice-president of the National Federation Party (NFP) Lenora Qereqeretabua says that the government needs to urgently develop a plan and also condemns what she considers is a mishandling of COVID-19.

Source citations (as archived): [RNZ](<https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/424537/fiji-govt-doing-nothing-about-dengue-leptospirosis-opposition-says>).

#### International relations

<a id="event-2020-08-27-4-2"></a>

Context: Travel restrictions related to the COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom, COVID-19 pandemic in Czech Republic, COVID-19 pandemic in Jamaica, COVID-19 pandemic in Switzerland.

**Archived source account.** The British government removes Switzerland, the Czech Republic, and Jamaica from the travel corridor list due to rising COVID-19 infection rates. It means that arrivals from those countries will have to self-quarantine for two weeks, Transport Secretary Grant Shapps confirmed. The change will come into effect on Saturday at 4:00 a.m. BST.

Source citations (as archived): [The Guardian](<https://www.theguardian.com/travel/2020/aug/27/england-may-remove-switzerland-and-jamaica-from-travel-corridor-list>).

<a id="event-2020-08-27-4-4"></a>

Context: Colombia–United States relations.

**Archived source account.** Colombian Defense Minister Carlos Holmes Trujillo permits a U.S. Army unit to resume its advisory mission in the country after the Colombian Senate found that it did not constitute a deployment of foreign troops. A court had suspended the mission in early July after the opposition argued it did count as foreign troop movement, and thus needed Senate authorization.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-colombia-usa/colombia-says-visiting-us-military-unit-to-restart-activities-idUSKBN25N2JT>).

<a id="event-2020-08-27-4-6"></a>

Context: Egypt–Greece relations.

**Archived source account.** The Hellenic Parliament formally ratifies a maritime agreement with Egypt, that defines maritime boundaries and an exclusive economic zone between the two countries in the Mediterranean Sea.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-greece-egypt-parliament-turkey/greek-parliament-ratifies-maritime-accord-with-egypt-idUSKBN25N2M2>).

#### Law and crime

<a id="event-2020-08-27-5-1"></a>

Context: Poisoning of Alexei Navalny.

**Archived source account.** Russian police launch a preliminary investigation into the suspected poisoning of opposition figure Alexei Navalny on August 20 to determine whether to open a criminal investigation.

Source citations (as archived): [AFP](<https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/world/europe/russian-police-launch-initial-check-into-navalny-case/articleshow/77782333.cms>).

Context: Christchurch mosque shootings.

**Archived source account.** Australian Brenton Harrison Tarrant is sentenced to life imprisonment without possibility of parole, a first in New Zealand history, for killing 51 people in last year's mass shootings at two mosques in Christchurch.

Source citations (as archived): [The Guardian](<https://www.theguardian.com/world/2020/aug/27/christchurch-shooting-mosque-gunman-sentenced-to>).

<a id="event-2020-08-27-5-5"></a>

Context: 2020 Malian coup d'état.

**Archived source account.** Ousted Malian President Ibrahim Boubacar Keïta is freed by military authorities, a military junta spokesman informs. "He was freed this morning, \[and\] he has returned to his home", said the spokesman without elaborating.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-mali-security/ousted-mali-president-keita-has-been-freed-by-coup-leaders-says-junta-spokesman-idUSKBN25N1US>).

<a id="event-2020-08-27-5-7"></a>

Context: 2020 Belarusian protests.

**Archived source account.** Police in Belarus arrest 20 journalists who were planning to cover a protest in Minsk and confiscated their telephones and identity documents. The interior ministry later said that the journalists had been driven to the police station to check they had valid accreditation allowing them to work as journalists.

Source citations (as archived): [Al Jazeera](<https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/08/belarus-detains-journalists-anti-gov-protest-minsk-200827155127123.html>).

<a id="event-2020-08-27-5-9"></a>

Context: Travel restrictions related to the COVID-19 pandemic.

**Archived source account.** Delta Air Lines has banned 240 passengers for refusing to wear masks since a policy requiring them went into effect in June.

Source citations (as archived): [CNN](<https://www.cnn.com/travel/article/delta-airlines-no-fly-list-tops-240/index.html>).

<a id="event-2020-08-27-5-10"></a>

**Archived source account.** At least three people are killed when a feud between Hezbollah supporters and a local clan of Sunni Arabs ends with gunfight in south Beirut, Lebanon. The army arrives at the scene and arrests four people.

Source citations (as archived): [Al Arabiya English](<https://english.alarabiya.net/en/News/middle-east/2020/08/27/Clashes-in-Beirut-s-southern-town-of-Khaldeh-erupts-between-local-tribes-Hezbollah.html>).

<a id="event-2020-08-27-5-11"></a>

**Archived source account.** Dutch police report that Two Laughing Boys with a Mug of Beer, a painting by Dutch golden age painter Frans Hals, was stolen from the Hofje van Mevrouw van Aerden in Leerdam. This is the third time the painting had been stolen.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-netherlands-art-frans-hals-theft/frans-hals-painting-two-laughing-boys-stolen-for-a-third-time-idUSKBN25N1WA?il=0>).

<a id="event-2020-08-27-5-12"></a>

**Archived source account.** The FBI arrests Yaser Abdel Said, who had been on their Ten Most Wanted Fugitives list since 2014 for allegedly murdering his two daughters in an honor killing in 2008. His son and brother were also arrested for harboring a fugitive.

Source citations (as archived): [BBC News](<https://www.bbc.com/news/world-us-canada-53934168>).

#### Politics and elections

<a id="event-2020-08-27-6-1"></a>

Context: Afghan peace process.

**Archived source account.** Abdullah Abdullah, chairman of the High Council for National Reconciliation, says that peace talks between the Taliban and the government will start in September with the support of the Trump administration, which pushes both sides to set differences aside.

Source citations (as archived): [Al Arabiya](<https://english.alarabiya.net/en/News/world/2020/08/27/Afghan-officials-Taliban-to-start-peace-talks-in-September.html>).

<a id="event-2020-08-27-6-2"></a>

**Archived source account.** Kurdish human rights lawyer Ebru Timtik dies in hospital after spending 238-days on hunger strike in protest of her imprisonment after being found guilty of being a member of the outlawed Revolutionary People's Liberation Party/Front. At the time of her death, she was reported to only weigh 65 pounds.

Source citations (as archived): [New York Post](<https://nypost.com/2020/08/29/ebru-timtik-dies-after-238-day-hunger-strike/>).

#### Armed conflicts and attacks

<a id="event-2020-08-28-0-2"></a>

Context: War in Afghanistan / August 2020 Afghanistan attacks.

**Archived source account.** Thirteen people are killed and two others injured after two bombs explode in Spin Boldak, Kandahar.

Source citations (as archived): [TOLOnews](<https://tolonews.com/afghanistan/blasts-kandahar-kill-13-civilians-official>).

#### Business and economy

<a id="event-2020-08-28-1-2"></a>

Context: Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in Ecuador.

**Archived source account.** The International Monetary Fund reaches an agreement with the government of Ecuador to lend $6.5 billion to help fund the country's economy amid the pandemic and the subsequent fall in oil prices and finalize a debt restructuring deal with its international investors.

Source citations (as archived): [Financial Times](<https://www.ft.com/content/fe14a91e-a72a-439d-8ac0-bf7f0d9d74c5>).

#### Disasters and accidents

<a id="event-2020-08-28-2-1"></a>

Context: MV Wakashio oil spill.

**Archived source account.** The death toll of dolphins in Mauritius rises to 38, according to a government official. The dolphins showed signs of wounds but no trace of hydrocarbons in their bodies. Greenpeace urged yesterday the government to launch an "urgent investigation to determine the cause of the deaths and any ties to the Wakashio oil spill".

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-mauritius-environment-dolphins/death-toll-of-mauritius-dolphins-is-now-38-government-official-idUSKBN25O1JA?il=0>).

<a id="event-2020-08-28-2-2"></a>

**Archived source account.** Officials in Niger say that floods have killed 45 people and displaced more than 226,000 people since Monday, after torrential rains caused the Niger River to overflow. Prime Minister Brigi Rafini pledges aid.

Source citations (as archived): [AP](<https://apnews.com/e60edb661c13c47d294c56cd57fc3e98>).

<a id="event-2020-08-28-2-3"></a>

**Archived source account.** A polar bear kills a 38-year-old Dutch man at campsite near Longyearbyen, on the Arctic archipelago of Svalbard. The bear was then shot dead near Svalbard Airport. It is the first fatal bear attack on Svalbard since a British student was attacked and killed in 2011.

Source citations (as archived): [BBC News](<https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-europe-53945950>).

Context: COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in North America / COVID-19 pandemic in the United States / COVID-19 pandemic in Michigan.

**Archived source account.** Michigan surpasses 100,000 confirmed cases of COVID-19.

Source citations (as archived): [MLive.com](<https://www.mlive.com/public-interest/2020/08/michigan-surpasses-100000-confirmed-coronavirus-cases.html>).

<a id="event-2020-08-28-3-6"></a>

Context: COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in North America / COVID-19 pandemic in Canada, Travel restrictions related to the COVID-19 pandemic.

**Archived source account.** Canada extends emergency orders that place restrictions on international travel and make mandatory two-week quarantines for anyone entering the country until September 30.

Source citations (as archived): [Global News](<https://globalnews.ca/news/7304292/coronavirus-canada-extending-international-travel-restrictions-mandatory-quarantine-until-sept-30/>).

<a id="event-2020-08-28-3-9"></a>

Context: COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in Asia / COVID-19 pandemic in India.

**Archived source account.** India reports more than 77,000 new cases in the last 24 hours, taking the nationwide total to more than 3.38 million, the highest single day spike for the country for the second consecutive day, and the highest single day caseload in the world apart from the United States.

Source citations (as archived): [The Washington Post](<https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/asia_pacific/india-coronavirus-largest-daily-cases/2020/08/28/7cf61f0a-e7c1-11ea-bf44-0d31c85838a5_story.html?outputType>).

<a id="event-2020-08-28-3-11"></a>

Context: COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in Asia / COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia.

**Archived source account.** Indonesia reports 3,003 new cases in the last 24 hours, taking the nationwide total to 165,887. This is a new record high for the second consecutive day since the pandemic began in the country.

Source citations (as archived): [detikHealth](<https://health.detik.com/berita-detikhealth/d-5150417/update-corona-indonesia-28-agustus-rekor-3003-kasus-baru-total-165887>).

<a id="event-2020-08-28-3-13"></a>

Context: COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in Asia / COVID-19 pandemic in South Korea.

**Archived source account.** Prime Minister Chung Sye-kyun announces that the country's level 2 restrictions, set to expire on August 30, would be extended for at least another week until September 6 as the Ministry of Health and Welfare reports over 370 new infections over the past 24 hours.

Source citations (as archived): [Anadolu Agency](<https://www.aa.com.tr/en/asia-pacific/skorea-extends-covid-19-restrictions-as-virus-spikes/1955842>).

<a id="event-2020-08-28-3-16"></a>

Context: COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in Europe / COVID-19 pandemic in France.

**Archived source account.** The health ministry says that France is seeing an "exponential" rise in cases as the country records its second-highest record of reported cases since March, with 7,379 new cases in the last 24 hours, raising the possibility of another nationwide lockdown.

Source citations (as archived): [BBC News](<https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-53954562>).

<a id="event-2020-08-28-3-18"></a>

Context: COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in Europe / COVID-19 pandemic in Greece.

**Archived source account.** The Ministry of Citizen Protection announces changes to Greece's travel restrictions, effective August 31 until at least September 19, due to a rise in cases in recent weeks. Changes include requiring visitors from a list of countries to show a negative test result to enter and a suspension of flights to and from Catalonia, Spain, but lifting restrictions on the Netherlands.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.channelnewsasia.com/news/world/greece-bans-flights-from-barcelona--extends-covid-19-travel-restrictions-13064106>).

<a id="event-2020-08-28-3-20"></a>

Context: COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in Europe / COVID-19 pandemic in Hungary.

**Archived source account.** Hungary announces that it will close its borders to foreigners on September 1 in an attempt to curb a rise in infections, and Hungarians returning from abroad will have to go into two-week quarantine. Hungarians can only leave if they have provided two negative tests.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-hungary-borders/hungary-to-close-borders-to-foreigners-as-of-sept-1-to-curb-coronavirus-infections-idUSKBN25O273>).

<a id="event-2020-08-28-3-22"></a>

Context: COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in Malawi.

**Archived source account.** The government announces that the Lilongwe International Airport and all public schools in the country will reopen on September 1 and 7, respectively, following a reported significant decrease in new cases and deaths.

Source citations (as archived): [Anadolu Agency](<https://www.aa.com.tr/en/africa/covid-19-malawi-to-reopen-schools-sept-7/1955757>).

#### International relations

<a id="event-2020-08-28-4-1"></a>

Context: Norway–Russia relations.

**Archived source account.** The Russian foreign ministry announces the expulsion of a senior diplomat at the Norwegian embassy in Moscow and declared him persona non grata as a "retaliatory measure" after the Norwegian foreign ministry had expelled the deputy trade representative of the Russian embassy in Oslo on August 19 for alleged espionage.

Source citations (as archived): [AFP](<https://www.themoscowtimes.com/2020/08/28/russia-expels-norwegian-diplomat-in-spy-affair-a71270>).

<a id="event-2020-08-28-4-3"></a>

Context: European Union–Turkey relations, Greece–Turkey relations.

**Archived source account.** Top EU diplomat Josep Borrell threatens Turkey with sanctions unless it and Greece reconcile their differences over maritime borders and gas drilling rights near Cyprus.

Source citations (as archived): [Al Jazeera](<https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/08/eu-warns-turkey-sanctions-east-mediterranean-crisis-worsens-200828145842821.html>).

#### Law and crime

<a id="event-2020-08-28-5-1"></a>

Context: George Floyd protests.

**Archived source account.** 50,000 people gather in Washington, D.C. to commemorate the 1963 civil rights march and in protest against police violence. The event is called the "Commitment March: Get Your Knee Off Our Necks", a reference to George Floyd's killing. The relatives of Jacob Blake, George Floyd, Breonna Taylor, and Eric Garner deliver speeches at the march alongside civil rights leaders Al Sharpton and Martin Luther King III.

Source citations (as archived): [BBC News](<https://www.bbc.com/news/world-us-canada-53949460>).

<a id="event-2020-08-28-5-3"></a>

Context: Protests over responses to the COVID-19 pandemic, COVID-19 pandemic in Germany.

**Archived source account.** An administrative court in Berlin overturns the city government's ban on protests and demonstrations, citing "no indication" that the government's rationale for the ban of protesters breaching social distancing measures would occur.

Source citations (as archived): [AFP](<https://www.bangkokpost.com/world/1976603/berlin-braces-for-anti-corona-demonstration>).

<a id="event-2020-08-28-5-5"></a>

Context: Essex lorry deaths.

**Archived source account.** A 40-year-old haulier from County Armagh, Northern Ireland, pleads guilty in the Central Criminal Court of England and Wales to the manslaughter of 39 Vietnamese people, as well as conspiring to assist unlawful immigration.

Source citations (as archived): [AAP](<https://www.wellingtontimes.com.au/story/6900958/man-pleads-guilty-over-truck-deaths-in-uk/?cs=5461>).

<a id="event-2020-08-28-5-6"></a>

**Archived source account.** Egyptian authorities arrest Mahmoud Ezzat, the leader of the Muslim Brotherhood. He was serving a sentence in absentia and was detained in a hideout in Cairo.

Source citations (as archived): [Al Arabiya](<https://english.alarabiya.net/en/News/middle-east/2020/08/28/Egypt-arrests-Muslim-Brotherhood-leader-Mahmoud-Ezzat.html>).

<a id="event-2020-08-28-5-7"></a>

**Archived source account.** The United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights Michelle Bachelet says that the life of top Congolese doctor Denis Mukwege, a Nobel Peace Prize winner, is "at serious risk" after receiving multiple death threats via phone calls and social media. His hospital is located in the middle of a conflict zone and the Congolese government pledged to protect him after he survived an assassination attempt years ago.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-congo-security-doctor/u-n-says-life-of-congos-nobel-laureate-doctor-in-danger-idUSKBN25O1V4?il=0>).

<a id="event-2020-08-28-5-8"></a>

**Archived source account.** A Pakistani court sentences three leaders of Jamat-ud-Dawa to between one and 16 years in prison for helping coordinate the 2008 Mumbai attacks. The sentences come as the deadline for the country to avoid getting placed on the Financial Action Task Force blacklist approaches.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-pakistan-court-fatf/pakistan-jails-three-accused-of-financing-mumbai-attacks-idUSKBN25O2OI?il=0>).

<a id="event-2020-08-28-5-9"></a>

**Archived source account.** Rioting erupts in Malmö, Sweden, following a Quran book burning event by far-right Danish politician Rasmus Paludan in the city. Police say as many as 300 people gathered to protest the anti-Islam activities, which then became violent as protesters set fires and attacked police.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://uk.reuters.com/article/uk-sweden-riot/violence-erupts-in-swedish-town-of-malmo-after-anti-islam-actions-police-say-idUKKBN25O31L?il=0>).

<a id="event-2020-08-28-5-10"></a>

**Archived source account.** The Brazilian Ministry of Health announces expansions to the country's abortion laws regarding cases of pregnancy from rape, which include requiring the victim to provide "a detailed account" to doctors, a report to police, and the victim being "expressly warned" of the possibility of prosecution for fraud for false or unverified claims. Chamber of Deputies minority leader Jandira Feghali filed a bill in response to block the decree, claiming it "constitutes psychological violence against women".

Source citations (as archived): [AFP](<https://www.straitstimes.com/world/americas/brazil-expands-requirements-for-abortion-in-rape-cases>).

**Archived source account.** Japanese Prime Minister Shinzō Abe announces his intention to resign due to his deteriorating health.

<a id="event-2020-08-28-7-0"></a>

**Archived source account.** American neurotechnology company Neuralink unveils a pig, named "Gertrude", that has been living with a brain-implanted chip for two months at an event in San Francisco.
